_comment: GENERATED from the defineTool registry by scripts/gen-tool-catalog.ts — do not hand-edit. Run `npm run gen:tool-catalog` after adding/changing a tool. The compact, CI-gated projection of the tool + route surface (docs-and-memory-as-projections D-002).

tools.name: ablation:report
tools.description: Prompt-sedimentology dead-weight report: per-SU-playbook-rule shadow-ablation standings (dead-weight-candidate / load-bearing / insufficient-evidence) aggregated across weekly cycles, candidates first, plus recent cycle rows (verdict, pass-rate delta, regressions, cost). Read-only over harness_shared.prompt_ablation_runs.

guidance.when: Reviewing which SU-playbook governance rules earn their tokens: "which rules survived repeated ablation with zero behavioral delta?" — the owner review queue for prompt slimming, or checking what last week's shadow cycle measured.
guidance.notWhen: You want prompt MUTATION history (who changed what) — change_ledger:list. You want to RUN an ablation — the system:prompt-ablation routine (dark until the frontier P-001 arming gate).
guidance.chaining: ablation:report → for a candidate rule, read its ruleKey rows ({ ruleKey }) for the per-scenario evidence → an actual removal is a normal reviewed playbook edit (rides the change ledger + the su llm-test suite).

tools.name: accounts:get-session-override
tools.description: Read the current owner session-now account override (forcedAccounts allow-list + excludeAccounts) the fleet honours when picking a pool account. An un-steered workspace returns both empty (no restriction). The READ twin of accounts:set-session-override. Returns {ok, override}.

guidance.when: Checking how account selection is currently steered, before changing it.
guidance.notWhen: Per-account rate/status — accounts:status. The whole pool — accounts:list.

tools.name: accounts:link-complete
tools.description: Complete the one-click account link (accounts-pool-tab P-002): feed the pasted claude.ai code into the held `claude setup-token` process (keyed by linkId) → it mints the token → write it server-side + register the account. The token NEVER appears in the response. Returns {ok, account} (the registered account row, no token).

guidance.when: Finishing an accounts:link-start flow — paste the `code` claude.ai showed after the owner authorized, with the linkId from link-start.
guidance.notWhen: Starting the flow — accounts:link-start. The reliable path — accounts:register.

tools.name: accounts:link-start
tools.description: One-click Max-account link (accounts-pool-tab P-002): spawns the real `claude setup-token` CLI server-side and returns the claude.ai authorize URL IT prints + an opaque linkId for the held process. The owner opens the URL in a browser logged into the TARGET Max account, authorizes, then pastes the shown code into accounts:link-complete with this linkId. (Driving the real CLI is required — claude.ai rejects a hand-built URL.) accounts:register (setup-token paste) is the manual alternative. Returns {ok, authorizeUrl, linkId}.

guidance.when: Linking a new Max subscription into the pool via the one-click OAuth beta (vs the setup-token paste). Pair with accounts:link-complete.
guidance.notWhen: The reliable path — accounts:register with a `claude setup-token` (token:<path>) or a .credentials.json bundle. Inspecting the pool — accounts:list / accounts:status.
guidance.chaining: accounts:link-start { id } → owner authorizes the URL → accounts:link-complete { linkId, code } → registered.

tools.name: accounts:link-status
tools.description: Poll a held accounts:link-start flow. claude CLI ≥2.1.200 auto-delivers the OAuth code to the held CLI when the approving browser is on the operator's own machine (the owner sees "You're all set up" and NO code) — the server finalizes on its own and THIS reports it. Returns {ok, status: pending|completed|failed|unknown, account?, error?}.

guidance.when: After accounts:link-start, while the owner approves in the browser — poll until completed/failed instead of demanding a code that may never be shown.
guidance.notWhen: You have a pasted code — accounts:link-complete. Inspecting the pool — accounts:list.

tools.name: accounts:list
tools.description: List the Mug's account pool: each account's id/label/credentialRef, the member harness slugs bound to it, and its rate-limit projection (pausedUntil / penaltyCount). Returns {ok, accounts}.

guidance.when: Seeing which accounts the Mug can draw from and what each is bound to.
guidance.notWhen: Wanting live headroom + sustained-limit flags — accounts:status.

tools.name: accounts:pin
tools.description: Pin an agent to a pool account on the inference gateway, LIVE (no respawn). `agent` = the TARGET agent's owner/spawn id — pass your OWN id to pin yourself, or another agent's id to pin them. `account` = a pool account id (see gateway:status / accounts:list). `hard:true` ⇒ NEVER fail over off it (waits / 429s on that account); default (soft) prefers it but yields if it is paused/exhausted. The gateway routes that agent's SUBSEQUENT requests to the account, overriding its spawn-time pin. CAUTION: concentrating many agents on one account rate-throttles it — prefer accounts with headroom (gateway:status) and spread load. In-memory: re-apply after a gateway restart. Returns {ok, ownerId, pin}.

guidance.when: Dynamically routing an agent (yourself or another) to a specific pool account without respawning it.
guidance.notWhen: Steering which account NEW spawns get fleet-wide — that is accounts:set-session-override.
guidance.chaining: gateway:status (pick an account with headroom) → accounts:pin { agent, account } → accounts:unpin to revert.

tools.name: accounts:probe-capacity
tools.description: Ask UPSTREAM for each pooled Claude account's REAL unified-5h/7d budget and record it into the account-pool projection. Sends one minimal (1-token) request per account through that account's own egress + credential and reads the authoritative `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers (present on 200s, not just 429s). This is the ONLY way a usage-walled account gets a fresh reading: it is routed no live traffic, so its projection can never self-heal — it stays walled until its PROJECTED reset (days), even after a real capacity reset. Prefer this over `accounts:reset-rate { resetWindows }`, which merely ASSERTS a reset; this PROVES it (and a 429 reply CONFIRMS a genuine wall instead). Runs out-of-process — no gateway restart needed. `apply:false` for a read-only dry run. Returns { ok, probed, unwalled, applied, rows[] }.

guidance.when: After a capacity/quota reset, or whenever an account reads usageWalled / healthyAccounts is 0 but you suspect the projection is STALE. Also the durable self-heal a schedule should call.
guidance.notWhen: Clearing a stale rate-limit PAUSE (accounts:reset-rate — a different meter). Clearing the gateway’s IN-MEMORY exhaustedUntil (POST /admin/readmit or a gateway restart — a different process).
guidance.chaining: accounts:probe-capacity { walledOnly:true } → accounts:status (confirm usageWalled cleared) → if upstream CONFIRMS the wall, do NOT force it; if the probe cannot run at all, accounts:reset-rate { resetWindows:true } is the deliberate override.

tools.name: accounts:register
tools.description: Register (or update) a provider account in the pool. `provider:'claude'` (default) uses a Claude Max OAuth credential: `token:<path>` (`claude setup-token`) | `file:<path>` / absolute / `~` (`.credentials.json`). `provider:'codex'` uses a bearer credential for the Codex/OpenAI-compatible gateway: `token:<path>` or `env:NAME`. Credential refs are references, never the secret. Optional `egress` pins the account to its own outbound IP. Re-registering an existing id updates credentialRef/provider/label/egress, preserving bindings + rate state. Returns {ok, account}.

guidance.when: Adding a Claude Max subscription the Mug can pool (each subscription has its own 5h/7d rolling budget — more accounts = more aggregate budget). Register ≥2 before flipping papercusp-inference-gateway-multi-account.
guidance.notWhen: Setting the operator API key (operator:credentials). A one-off local run (no deploy).
guidance.chaining: accounts:register (×N Max subs) → flip papercusp-inference-gateway-multi-account → cups route by cache-affinity + 5h-budget drain; deploy:pot binds an account per member.

tools.name: accounts:remove
tools.description: Remove one OR many Claude accounts from the pool. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Does NOT tear down anything already deployed on them. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, removed }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position.

guidance.when: Retiring account(s) from the pool (e.g. subscriptions you no longer use). Retiring several at once? Pass them all via `ids`.
guidance.notWhen: Tearing down a deployed frame — deploy:teardown / deploy:teardown_pot.

tools.name: accounts:reset-rate
tools.description: Clear an account's rate-limit penalty state — its pause (pausedUntil), penalty count, and the rolling penalty window — back to fresh (accounts-pool-tab P-004; wraps the recordAccountReset projection reset). The owner's manual override for when an account's PROJECTED pause is stale (e.g. the 5h window actually reset, or a false-exhaustion). Does NOT touch live governor buckets (those self-expire) or the credential. `resetWindows:true` (WI-3553) is the DELIBERATE further override that ALSO zeroes the observed-budget projection (`utilization`/`windowResetAt`/`utilization7d`/`windowResetAt7d`) for when that probe-derived reading itself is wrong or can't be re-probed — default `false` is byte-identical to today (the budget reading survives the reset). Returns {ok, account}.

guidance.when: Clearing a pool account's projected pause/penalty after a confirmed reset — the Accounts tab's per-account Reset button, or unsticking an account the drain selector is avoiding on a stale projection.
guidance.notWhen: Moving work off an exhausted account NOW — accounts:scale_out. Inspecting state — accounts:status. The observed-budget projection is wrong AND the probe can actually run — prefer accounts:probe-capacity (asks upstream for real evidence) over resetWindows (which only asserts).

tools.name: accounts:scale_out
tools.description: Manually scale out off an exhausted account (P-021): provision a FRESH cloud Swarm on the most-available account for the exhausted account's bound members, instead of waiting on the pause. ⚠ Provisions real machines (costs money) — owner-gated. `force` skips the sustained-limit check. Returns {ok, result}.

guidance.when: An account is rate-limited and you want to move its work onto a fresh account NOW (the same action the auto-scale-out takes; this is the manual lever).
guidance.notWhen: Just inspecting state — accounts:status. No fresh account is available (it will report no-fresh-account).

tools.name: accounts:scale_policy
tools.description: Read or set the account scale-out trigger policy: windowMs (penalty accumulation window) + sustainedPenaltyThreshold (≥N penalties in the window ⇒ "sustainedly limited", which gates PAID auto-scale-out). Default 15min / 3. set is audited + one-call-revertible. Tunes WHEN scale-out fires; provisioning stays owner-gated (accounts:scale_out).

guidance.when: During a provider rate-limit storm: raise the threshold to avoid over-provisioning paid machines on transient 429 bursts, or lower it to scale out earlier under sustained limiting — live, no redeploy.
guidance.notWhen: To actually provision now, use accounts:scale_out (owner-gated). To pause/exclude an account use the accounts:* session-override tools. EXHAUSTED_UTIL/DRAIN_FULL_UTIL are not covered (structural consts, follow-up).
guidance.chaining: accounts:status shows the per-account sustained-limit state; config:list-overrides shows the active override.

tools.name: accounts:set-session-override
tools.description: Set the owner's session-now account override the fleet honours when picking a pool account to spawn/deploy on (accounts-pool-tab P-004): `forcedAccounts` (allow-list — use ONLY these), `excludeAccounts` (skip these, e.g. a flaky/rate-limited account). Both empty ⇒ no restriction (today's behaviour). Applied as a fail-soft precedence layer BEFORE the headroom/drain selectors; an over-restrictive set falls back to the frame-default credential. `clear:true` wipes both. Returns {ok, override}.

guidance.when: Steering account selection for the current session — focus the fleet on one account, or route around a flaky/limited one — without removing it from the pool.
guidance.notWhen: Permanently removing an account — accounts:remove. Clearing a rate-limit penalty — accounts:reset-rate. Pausing the pot — pot:pause.
guidance.chaining: accounts:set-session-override { excludeAccounts:["acct-b"] } → cups stop spawning on acct-b this session. clear:true resets.

tools.name: accounts:status
tools.description: Per-account rate-limit status: availability (not currently paused), the sustained-limit flag (the scale-out trigger), the rate projection, and any LIVE local governor buckets keyed to the account. Returns {ok, accounts}.

guidance.when: Checking which accounts have headroom before a deploy, or why an account auto-scaled out.

tools.name: accounts:test-egress
tools.description: Probe one pooled account's egress: the real exit IP through its dispatcher (or the default shared egress if unpinned), IP reputation (proxy/hosting/ASN), and — unless compareOthers:false — whether that exit IP collides (same ASN or /24 subnet) with any OTHER pooled account's egress. Returns { ok, result: { accountId, hasEgress, exitIp, reputation, asn, distinctFromOthers, comparedOthers, collisions, clean } } — `clean` is the pin-worthiness verdict (has an exit IP, not flagged as proxy/hosting, and distinct from every other account). Read-only, no live-gateway change.

guidance.when: Deciding whether an account's egress IP is safe to pin (accounts:register/accounts:pin egress) — before AND after applying a pin, to prove it actually routes through the new IP and doesn't collide with another pooled account's egress.
guidance.notWhen: Reading current rate-limit headroom (accounts:status) or the pool listing (accounts:list) — this is specifically the network-level egress/IP-reputation probe.
guidance.chaining: accounts:register { egress } → accounts:test-egress { accountId } to verify the pin routes correctly and stays distinct from the rest of the pool.

tools.name: accounts:unpin
tools.description: Remove a dynamic account pin set by accounts:pin (LIVE). `agent` = the target agent owner/spawn id. The agent reverts to its spawn-time routing (its static x-papercusp-account header, or the pool default). Returns {ok, ownerId, cleared}.

guidance.when: Reverting an accounts:pin so the agent routes normally again.
guidance.notWhen: It was never dynamically pinned (no-op — cleared:false).
guidance.chaining: accounts:pin … → accounts:unpin { agent }.

tools.name: actions:recent
tools.description: List recent long-running user-initiated actions for a harness (replan, cleanup, snapshot).

guidance.when: User asks "what have I been doing?", "recent actions". Read-only feed from the actions log.
guidance.notWhen: For workspace-wide audit (cross-harness), use `cross_harness:recent_activity` or `audit:list`.

tools.name: activity:recent
tools.description: Read recent worker-activity rows (native tool calls / lifecycle / todos) from the cross-CLI activity bridge. Filter by owner (one worker's pane), harness, agent (claude/codex/omp), kind (tool/lifecycle/todos); since_id returns only rows newer than a cursor. The curator + fleet view read this; the live push is /api/activity/stream.

guidance.when: You want to inspect what a worker (or the whole fleet) has been doing — the recent native tool-call stream, todo snapshots, or lifecycle transitions. Pass owner to scope to one pane, harness to scope to one project, since_id to page forward.
guidance.notWhen: For a LIVE feed subscribe to the /api/activity/stream SSE (the pui does this). To report activity (you almost never need to) use `activity:report`. For coord messages use `coord:inbox`.

tools.name: activity:report
tools.description: Report one worker-activity event (a native tool call, lifecycle transition, or todo snapshot) to the cross-CLI activity bridge sink (harness_shared.agent_activity). Called by the per-CLI hooks on every tool call; feeds the pui fleet view + curator. The display summary is derived server-side from tool_name+tool_input when not supplied. Fire-and-forget: returns { ok, id } and never blocks.

guidance.when: Almost never call this by hand — the per-CLI hooks (posttooluse-activity-report.sh / the OMP coord-hook port) call it automatically to mirror each worker's native tool stream into the fleet view. Call directly only to inject a synthetic activity marker (e.g. a custom lifecycle note).
guidance.notWhen: To READ the activity stream use `activity:recent` (or the /api/activity/stream SSE). To coordinate with peers use `coord:send`. To drive a pui use `tui:dispatch`.

tools.name: agent_chats:archive
tools.description: Archive (soft-delete) a chat session by id.

guidance.when: User says "close that chat", "archive the X conversation" — moves the chat to archived status so it stops appearing in active lists.
guidance.notWhen: For DELETING a chat, this isn't it — archive is reversible. For UI dismissing without changing state, ignore the request and the user can do it themselves.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:list` first if you need to confirm the chatId.

tools.name: agent_chats:chat
tools.description: Single-turn streaming chat against an already-assembled role prompt. Returns final text + token/cost rollup; the caller is expected to persist the assistant turn.

tools.name: agent_chats:create
tools.description: Open a new chat session for a role in a harness; optionally bind it to a feature_id.

guidance.when: User says "ask the architect to ...", "have the worker do ...", or you're routing a request to a role-scoped agent. Step 1 of the two-step dispatch flow.
guidance.notWhen: For replying in the user's direct chat, just speak — don't spin up a new agent chat. For talking to ANOTHER user, use `messages:send`. For spawning a one-shot agent process (not a long-running chat), use `<spawn>` / `orchestrator.spawn`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:send_message` immediately (step 2 of the dispatch flow), then `ui:dispatch` with `/harness/<slug>?chat=<chatId>` so the user can watch the conversation.

tools.name: agent_chats:get
tools.description: Read one chat by id (transcript, totals, feature_lock state).

guidance.when: User names a specific chat ("the architect conversation about auth") and wants the full transcript or feature_lock state.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of chats in a harness, use `agent_chats:list` first to find the id. Don't fetch full transcripts speculatively.
guidance.chaining: Follow `agent_chats:list` to find the id.

tools.name: agent_chats:list
tools.description: List multi-turn chat sessions for a harness slug (active by default; pass includeArchived=true to see all). Bounded: limit clamped 1..100, default 100; page older chats with offset. Rows are summaries (turn_count, tokens, cost, timestamps) WITHOUT the transcript body — use agent_chats:get for a chat's turns.

guidance.when: User asks "what chats have I had with X?", "show me the conversations on sheets", or you need a chatId before resuming via ui:dispatch.
guidance.notWhen: For agents (who exists), use `agents:list`. For the transcript of a SPECIFIC chat, use `agent_chats:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:get` for detail on one chat, or `ui:dispatch` with `/harness/<slug>?chat=<chatId>` to take the user to it.

tools.name: agent_chats:send_message
tools.description: Append a user message to an existing agent chat. The harness streams the assistant reply via SSE; this tool returns as soon as the message is accepted. Pair with agent_chats:create to start a new conversation.

guidance.when: Step 2 of the dispatch flow — you just called `agent_chats:create` and need to post the user's first message to kick off the conversation. Also for follow-up messages on an existing chat the user named.
guidance.notWhen: For broadcasting to multiple recipients (inbox-style), use `messages:send`. For the user's own chat with you, just speak.
guidance.chaining: Follow `agent_chats:create` (or `agent_chats:list` if resuming). Then `ui:dispatch` to take the user to the chat.

tools.name: agent_tools:list
tools.description: List MCP-exposed tools with permission status for the caller. Each entry includes name, description, capability, roles allowlist, an `allowed` flag with `reason` when blocked, AND per-tool `guidance` (when/notWhen/chaining resolved for the queried role). Use to discover what you can call without trial-and-error.

guidance.when: Your tools playbook didn't cover a user request and you need to discover what's callable. Returns the full catalog filtered by your role, with each tool's guidance — treat this as the runtime fallback playbook.
guidance.notWhen: Don't use as a fishing expedition. If your playbook covers it, just call the tool. `agent_tools:list` costs a tool call.

tools.name: agents:list
tools.description: List agents across the workspace (optionally filtered by harness slug). Limit clamped 1..100, default 40.

guidance.when: User asks "which agents are working on X?", "what crew does sheets have?", or you need to pick the most-active matching role before calling agent_chats:create.
guidance.notWhen: For active CHAT sessions, use `agent_chats:list`. agents:list is who-exists; agent_chats:list is what-conversations.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `agent_chats:create` once you've picked the role to dispatch to.

tools.name: architect:chat
tools.description: Architect-mode chat turn: clarify spec, propose patches. Streams deltas; returns the assembled final text.

tools.name: artifacts:append
tools.description: Append to one OR many PG-canonical text artifacts (harness_text_artifacts); creates the row if absent. Pass a single `{ slug?, rel_path, suffix }` or `items:[{ slug?, rel_path, suffix }]` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, rel_path, appended_bytes, total_bytes, updated_at | error }], counts } — correlate by (slug, rel_path), not by position; a missing / invalid-slug item fails only itself.

guidance.when: Add to an existing artifact without losing prior content — running notes, ongoing log, accumulating findings. Append to several at once via `items`.
guidance.notWhen: For replacing the whole file, use `artifacts:save`. For ephemeral within-turn notes, just hold them in your reply.
guidance.chaining: Bulk: single { slug?, rel_path, suffix } | items[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by (slug, rel_path) not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: artifacts:delete
tools.description: Delete one OR many PG-canonical text artifact rows by (harness_slug, rel_path). Restricted to architect/operator/curator roles. Pass a single `{ slug?, rel_path }` or `items:[{ slug?, rel_path }]` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, rel_path, deleted | error }], counts } — correlate by (slug, rel_path), not by position; a missing / invalid-slug item fails only itself.

guidance.when: Remove an artifact that's no longer relevant. Restricted to architect/operator/curator roles by `roles` allowlist. Delete several at once via `items`.
guidance.notWhen: Don't delete to "clean up" speculatively — artifacts cost nothing to keep, and other agents may rely on them.
guidance.chaining: Bulk: single { slug?, rel_path } | items[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by (slug, rel_path) not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: artifacts:load
tools.description: Read one OR many PG-canonical text artifacts (harness_text_artifacts) by (harness_slug, rel_path). Pass a single `{ slug?, rel_path }` or `items:[{ slug?, rel_path }]` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, rel_path, found, content, updated_at | error }], counts } — correlate by (slug, rel_path), not by position; a missing / invalid-slug item fails only itself.

guidance.when: You need to read a file the harness wrote earlier (notes, intermediate outputs, plans) by its harness_slug + rel_path. Pass every (slug, rel_path) at once via `items`.
guidance.notWhen: For SOURCE CODE in the user's repo, use the filesystem tools / gitnexus. Artifacts are harness-scoped PG-canonical text only.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `artifacts:save` to round-trip, `artifacts:append` to add to an existing one. Bulk: single { slug?, rel_path } | items[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by (slug, rel_path) not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: artifacts:save
tools.description: Upsert one OR many PG-canonical text artifacts (harness_text_artifacts) by (harness_slug, rel_path); replaces existing content. Pass a single `{ slug?, rel_path, content }` or `items:[{ slug?, rel_path, content }]` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, rel_path, bytes, updated_at | error }], counts } — correlate by (slug, rel_path), not by position; a missing / invalid-slug item fails only itself.

guidance.when: Persist a generated text artifact for later reads by other agents or future turns. Replaces existing content at the same (harness_slug, rel_path). Save several at once via `items`.
guidance.notWhen: For appending to an existing file, use `artifacts:append` — save fully replaces. For source code, write to the repo via filesystem tools, not artifacts.
guidance.chaining: Bulk: single { slug?, rel_path, content } | items[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by (slug, rel_path) not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: audit:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what happened recently?", "who did X?", or you need a forensic timeline of agent + user actions.

When NOT to use: For ACTIVE / in-flight work, use `harness:status` or `actions:recent`. Audit is a write-log, not a live view.

guidance.when: User asks "what happened recently?", "who did X?", or you need a forensic timeline of agent + user actions.
guidance.notWhen: For ACTIVE / in-flight work, use `harness:status` or `actions:recent`. Audit is a write-log, not a live view.

tools.name: auth:set_full_access_roles
tools.description: Read/set/clear the runtime testing-phase full-access bypass-role set (REPLACES the baked TESTING_FULL_ACCESS_ROLES — roles that skip all role+capability gates). DARK behind papercusp-auth-config-overrides (OFF ⇒ baked set, byte-identical); the owner flips it ON to ratify. The global enable/disable is the papercusp-testing-full-access flag. set/clear audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: A role needs the testing-phase full-access bypass mid-incident (add it), or you are trimming the bypass set toward least-privilege — live, no deploy. Requires the owner to have flipped papercusp-auth-config-overrides ON. op:get to read the override + baked set.
guidance.notWhen: To globally DISABLE testing-full-access use the papercusp-testing-full-access flag (the kill-switch). To confine a role's capabilities use capability_envelope:set_role. This widens access — the highest-stakes dial; prefer tightening.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active auth-config-overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts to the baked set.

tools.name: autoloop:control
tools.description: Pause/resume a harness's blueprint-scheduled autoloop (flips its bp-schedule-* routine rows — durable) or reset its error circuit (zeroes consecutive_errors so backoff stops withholding fires).

guidance.when: User says "pause the autoloop", "turn autopilot back on", or a circuit-open harness needs its error counter reset after a fix. Per-harness, durable.
guidance.notWhen: For PAUSING all of the operator (silence-mode-style), use the operator-pause flag — autoloop is per-harness. For pausing git-sync or another non-schedule routine, flip that routine directly.
guidance.chaining: autoloop:status first to see the schedule routines + circuit state; reset-errors after fixing whatever made the fires fail. A dead loop:arm loop's red counter lives under the workspace-wide '*' scope, not your harness — reset-errors {harness, role:'<the dead loop's owner/role>'} clears BOTH scopes in one call (EI-6753); literal harness:'*' is still rejected (P-004), pass any real harness.

tools.name: autoloop:status
tools.description: Read autoloop_state rows (last_fired_at, last_status, consecutive_errors) for a harness slug.

guidance.when: User asks "is the autoloop running?", "is the harness on autopilot?". Reads enabled/paused state + recent tick info.
guidance.notWhen: For TURNING the autoloop on/off, use `autoloop:control`. For harness liveness in general, use `harness:health`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `autoloop:control` if the user wants to change state.

tools.name: autonomy:decide
tools.description: The autonomy gate (D-004): given an action + its risk/authority/reversibility, returns auto (decide it without asking) or gated (routes to the owner Queue), with the category, effective ceiling, and the reasons. The policy is ARMED (all 13 categories at ceiling `critical`): `auto` when within ceiling + reversible + system-authority; `gated` only for protected surfaces, authority=owner, or above-ceiling / graduation asks. With the owner full-autonomy grant ON, even that residue is `auto`. Overwatch callers get the overwatch envelope (B-06) instead: nudge/observe/escalate/wake bookkeeping auto, structural escalate-only.

guidance.when: You are the Mug (or a cup) deciding whether to auto-handle a queue item / answer a card without the owner — or the Kettle deciding whether to nudge/observe/escalate (auto) vs escalate a structural change (gated). Pass the action's tool name (group:verb) + the item's risk_tier / reversibility; the gate tells you auto vs the owner Queue and why.
guidance.notWhen: To READ or render the whole policy use autonomy:policy_get. To CHANGE a ceiling use autonomy:policy_set (owner-authority). This tool DECIDES one action; it never mutates.
guidance.chaining: pot:survey / improvements:digest → autonomy:decide per item → place/auto-handle the `auto` ones, route the `gated` ones to the owner Queue. Overwatch: per anomaly suggestedAction → autonomy:decide → perform the `auto` ones, coord:escalate the `gated` ones.

tools.name: autonomy:graduation_status
tools.description: Read the Queen trust-graduation standings: per-(category, class) clean-auto-pass streaks from the tripwire ledger, each category's earned graduated_level vs its current level + ceiling, and which classes are graduation-eligible (an owner ratification ask to raise a ceiling). Read-only.

guidance.when: Rendering the owner graduation surface, or checking how close a category is to earning more autonomy. Pairs with autonomy:policy_get (ceilings) + autonomy:tripwire_list (the underlying passes).
guidance.notWhen: To raise a ceiling use autonomy:policy_set (owner authority). The graduated_level itself is written by the autonomy-trust-scan routine, not here.

tools.name: autonomy:policy_get
tools.description: Read the Queen autonomy policy (per-category risk ceilings, locks, graduated levels, and the derived effective ceiling) for this workspace.

guidance.when: Inspecting the Mug's per-category autonomy ceilings — the decider checking whether a category may auto-decide, or the owner settings surface rendering the policy. Pass `category` for one row; omit for all 13.
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE a ceiling use autonomy:policy_set. For feature flags use flags:get.

tools.name: autonomy:policy_set
tools.description: Set the Queen autonomy ceiling / lock / graduated level for one category. High-risk: widens or narrows what the Queen may auto-decide without asking. Audited; provide a reason.

guidance.when: The owner (or the owner control surface) deliberately changes a category's autonomy — lower/raise the risk ceiling, lock/unlock (protected = never-auto), or the graduation engine records an earned level (clamped ≤ the ceiling).
guidance.notWhen: To read the policy use autonomy:policy_get. This does not arm autonomy — categories ship never-auto and widen only after the owner lowers a ceiling AND the arming gate (P-092).

tools.name: autonomy:record_disposition
tools.description: Log the Queen's disposition of a considered item to the decision ledger (P-111): act | defer | reject | route-to-research | no-op. Resolves the autonomy gate from the action + risk/authority/reversibility (same as autonomy:decide), then records one disposition row with the decision axes, the chosen disposition, why, and links (the item, a realized action row, or a routed research task). Behavior-neutral record-keeping.

guidance.when: You are the Mug and you've DECIDED what to do with a queue item — record the disposition so it lands in the decision ledger / the owner's recent-auto-decisions feed. Use disposition='act' (links the action row), 'defer' (+revisitAt), 'reject' (+why), 'route-to-research' (+researchTaskId), or 'no-op' (+why).
guidance.notWhen: Just QUERYING whether you may auto-handle something (no commitment yet) → autonomy:decide. Changing a category ceiling → autonomy:policy_set.
guidance.chaining: autonomy:decide (or the same inputs) → act on the item → autonomy:record_disposition to log what you did. The worked example: a plan that "needs more research" → record_disposition { action:"plans:add-item", disposition:"route-to-research", researchTaskId } → a plan-governance disposition linked to the spawned research task.

tools.name: autonomy:tripwire_list
tools.description: List recent Queen auto-decisions and their auto-revert tripwires (category, class, action, watch status armed/cleared/tripped/reverted, revert handle). Backs the settings recent-auto-decisions feed. Read-only.

guidance.when: Rendering the owner recent-auto-decisions feed, or inspecting which auto-decisions are under watch / tripped. Filter by status (armed|cleared|tripped|reverted) or category.
guidance.notWhen: To UNDO one use autonomy:tripwire_revert. To see graduation standings use autonomy:graduation_status. To read ceilings use autonomy:policy_get.

tools.name: autonomy:tripwire_revert
tools.description: Owner one-click undo of a Queen auto-decision: trip its tripwire (owner-thumbs-down), revert the action, and demote the category one step. Owner-authority; the strongest counter-signal.

guidance.when: The owner rejects a recent auto-decision in the settings feed — undo the action + tell the graduation engine this category was too aggressive (demote one step).
guidance.notWhen: To just LIST auto-decisions use autonomy:tripwire_list. To change a ceiling directly use autonomy:policy_set.

tools.name: backup:diff
tools.description: Diff two kopia snapshots — list files added/changed/removed.

guidance.when: Diff current state vs a backup snapshot — what would change if we restored. Read-only.
guidance.notWhen: For applying the diff, use `backup:restore`. diff is the dry-run view.

tools.name: backup:promote
tools.description: Promote a restored clone to live by atomic rename. Live dir becomes .broken-<ts>-<name>/. Reversible by renaming back. Auto-snapshots before promotion as belt-and-suspenders.

guidance.when: Promote a backup to active (roll forward to it without rolling back). Used after testing a restore.
guidance.notWhen: For UNDOING to an earlier state, use `backup:rollback`. promote moves forward; rollback moves back.

tools.name: backup:restore
tools.description: Restore a kopia snapshot. mode="clone" (default) writes to .restored/<id>/ and never overwrites live state; mode="in_place" overwrites the target after taking a safety snapshot first.

guidance.when: Restore a backup snapshot — replay PG dump + filesystem into the workspace. Destructive: replaces current state.
guidance.notWhen: For ROLLING BACK without changing the snapshot list, use `backup:rollback`. restore is the full apply.

tools.name: backup:rollback
tools.description: Undo a previous backup:promote. Renames the .broken-<ts>-<name>/ dir back to live; current live becomes .rolled-back-<ts>-<name>/.

guidance.when: Roll back to the immediately-prior backup. Reversible only by re-applying via restore.
guidance.notWhen: For applying a SPECIFIC backup, use `backup:restore` with the id.

tools.name: backup:settings_get
tools.description: Read backup settings + repo stats for the active workspace.

guidance.when: Read backup configuration — schedule, retention, destinations.
guidance.notWhen: For runtime BACKUP state (last run, next run), check the destinations directly.

tools.name: backup:settings_set
tools.description: Patch backup settings for the active workspace. All fields optional; missing keys preserve existing values.

guidance.when: Update backup configuration. Confirm the change out loud first — affects automated backups going forward.
guidance.notWhen: For one-shot backup creation, use `backup:snapshot_create`. settings_set is for the schedule/policy.

tools.name: backup:snapshot_create
tools.description: Create a kopia snapshot of the active workspace before a destructive op. Returns the snapshot id so the same agent can restore from it if needed.

guidance.when: Create a new backup snapshot of the workspace. Use before risky migrations or major state changes.
guidance.notWhen: For routine commits, this isn't needed — backup snapshots are heavyweight (whole-workspace). For per-harness portable snapshots, use the snapshots tools instead.

tools.name: backup:snapshot_list
tools.description: List recent kopia snapshots for the active workspace.

guidance.when: List backup snapshots — point-in-time captures of the workspace's PG + filesystem state.
guidance.notWhen: For HARNESS snapshots (portable artifacts you can publish), use `snapshots:list`. backup:snapshot_list is the full-workspace recovery view.

tools.name: behaviour:catalog
tools.description: Read the desktop behaviour standard — the 8 checks behaviour:run scores, each with whether it is CRITICAL (a failed critical check fails the whole run, like cert-battery) and the concrete failure it catches. No args. Returns {ok, checks, count}.

guidance.when: Understanding what behaviour:run grades before running it, or which check a failing run tripped.
guidance.notWhen: Actually scoring a run — behaviour:run.

tools.name: behaviour:run
tools.description: Score a real desktop-agent run against the 8-check behaviour standard. mode:"score" reads an existing transcript by sessionId or transcriptPath; mode:"launch" runs a visible agent on a fixture plan, captures the transcript, and scores it. Returns the behaviour report plus session/transcript metadata, and best-effort dual-emits ONE su-agent-behavior rubric scorecard (observation lane) so the checks feed rubrics:trend — the `scorecard` field reports that emit; it never alters the verdict.

guidance.when: Use when you need to grade how a desktop agent behaved on a plan run: routing, gating, scope, execution, launch discipline, and completion evidence. score grades an existing run; launch runs and grades a fresh fixture.
guidance.notWhen: Not for raw model certification (cert:run), subjective gym scoring (gym:judge), or reading plan/work-item state (plans:get / work_items:list).
guidance.chaining: omp:sessions or dev:sessions → behaviour:run { mode:"score", sessionId }. Or create/pick a fixture plan → behaviour:run { mode:"launch", planSlug, model }.

tools.name: blender:grade-idea
tools.description: Grade a routed Blender idea 1–5 with optional feedback (≤2000 chars). Grades steer Blender's learning: fractional win credit in the lens weights + the critique primed into next cycles' ideator prompts. Key by ideaId or routedRef.

guidance.when: You want to score a routed Blender idea 1–5 (optional one-line critique) so Blender learns which lenses to favor. Key by ideaId (Blender view / learning.scout snapshot callers) or by routedRef — the routed artifact's change-feed ref 'plan:<slug>' | 'wi:<id>' | 'gym:<id>' — when you hold the artifact but not the ideaId (the Mug's triage path: grade each ungraded routed draft).
guidance.notWhen: Not an accept/reject of the routed artifact — a grade is a pure learning signal; the draft proceeds through normal triage regardless. Never pass grader attribution: gradedBy is derived from the caller role (Mug vs owner surface).
guidance.chaining: Nothing to chain: weights update on the next refreshScoutOutcomes pass and feedback enters ideator priming automatically. applied:false + reason 'owner-grade-sovereign' (Mug regrading an owner-graded row) is expected, not an error — owner grades are sovereign; the returned summary carries the standing grade.

tools.name: blender:ideation-feedback
tools.description: Your IDEATE-pass read of your OWN past graded proposals: the owner/Mug grades + critiques on features you filed (improvements:capture kind:'feature'), formatted as a grader-feedback priming block (newest-first; owner grades outrank Mug volume grades). Read-only; su-ideate origin only — never touches Blender's lens-weight learning.

guidance.when: Opening an IDEATE-mode grounding pre-pass — pull this to see how your past feature proposals were graded, so the pass builds on what landed / what the grader flagged rather than starting cold. Pairs with curation:state-of-pot + rubrics:list + scorecards:freshness as the IDEATE grounding reads.
guidance.notWhen: Grading an idea — that is blender:grade-idea. Reading Blender's OWN lens-routed ideas or lens weights — a different, lens-learning surface; this returns your su-ORIGINATED ideas only.
guidance.chaining: curation:state-of-pot + rubrics:list + scorecards:freshness + blender:ideation-feedback → your IDEATE pass, grounded.

tools.name: blueprint:catalog
tools.description: List the blueprints available to instantiate — built-in + Cupboard-installed (installed shadows built-in, like the extends resolver). Each entry summarizes the shape: id, tier, version, description, workItem kind, decider + roles, spine model (decider-edges vs program-steps), triggers, dispatch policy (when declared), requiresRepo, and whether it is a one-shot launch blueprint (fired via system:blueprint-run) vs a harness pipeline (instantiated via harness:create). Broken entries are kept as {id, tier, error}.

guidance.when: Deciding WHICH blueprint shape fits a piece of work before creating a harness — the Pot operator's first stop (decomposable features → coding, investigation → research, parallel codemod → migration, a decision → vote/deliberate). Also the discovery surface for what launch blueprints exist.
guidance.notWhen: Deep-inspecting one blueprint (validation errors/warnings) — blueprint:validate {id}. Authoring — blueprint:create/extend.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:catalog → blueprint:validate {id} → harness:create {blueprintId} (pipelines) or fire the launchable ones via their trigger/system:blueprint-run.

tools.name: blueprint:create
tools.description: Author a NEW Harness Blueprint from a blueprint object. Validates it (schema + semantics) and returns {ok, errors, warnings, yaml} — the canonical YAML to persist at .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. Does not write files or create a harness. For a blueprint that inherits, use blueprint:extend.

guidance.when: Authoring a brand-new blueprint shape from scratch (rare — usually you extend `coding`/`base`/`research`). Returns validated canonical YAML.
guidance.notWhen: Inheriting from an existing blueprint — use blueprint:extend (cheaper, less to author). Creating the harness itself — harness:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:create → (inspect yaml) → harness:create { blueprint } or write .papercusp/blueprint.yaml.

tools.name: blueprint:extend
tools.description: Author a CHILD blueprint extending a parent (e.g. extend "coding"). You supply only the overrides; the tool merges onto the parent, validates the resolved result, and returns {ok, errors, warnings, yaml} — the small child override file for .papercusp/blueprint.yaml. The parent resolves installed (~/.papercusp/blueprints, e.g. Cupboard-installed) → built-in.

guidance.when: The usual way to make a new blueprint: inherit shared structure from any resolvable parent (a built-in, or a Cupboard-installed blueprint) and override only what differs (knobs, a few roles, a spine tweak). Cheap to author.
guidance.notWhen: Authoring a wholly new shape with no parent — blueprint:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:extend { parent:"coding", overrides } → (inspect yaml) → harness:create { blueprint }.

tools.name: blueprint:publish
tools.description: List a local/private blueprint on the Comb: resolves the member repo's GitHub coords + publishes a kind='blueprint' listing (listing_ref = blueprintId) with the operator's gh token + attestation. DELTA-NOT-COPY — the blueprint is listed keeping its `extends:`, so an install composes it against the upstream parent and inherits upstream improvements. Lands PENDING (D-007) — an operator must approve it before it is publicly visible.

guidance.when: Sharing a blueprint you authored or customized — a local/private blueprint living at <repo>/.papercusp/blueprints/<id>/ — so others can install it from the Comb.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing/installing blueprints (blueprint:catalog lists what's installable); authoring one (blueprint:create / blueprint:extend); or when the blueprint files are not on GitHub yet — publish points at the repo, so commit + push first.
guidance.chaining: Run after the blueprint files are committed + pushed via the project's normal flow. The response carries review_status=pending — operators approve at /admin/cupboard-moderation; once approved it installs via the Cupboard like any blueprint listing.

tools.name: blueprint:validate
tools.description: Validate a Harness Blueprint — a blueprint id (resolved installed → built-in, e.g. "coding" or a Cupboard-installed id) OR inline YAML/JSON. Returns {ok, errors, warnings, summary} (errors/warnings instead of throwing) so you can iterate. Checks the Zod schema + reachability/termination/guards/bounded-recursion.

guidance.when: Before persisting a blueprint you authored (with blueprint:create/extend) or to inspect a built-in. Always validate before writing .papercusp/blueprint.yaml or calling harness:create.
guidance.notWhen: To run a blueprint — that is the orchestrator. To create a harness — harness:create.
guidance.chaining: blueprint:create/extend → blueprint:validate → (write .papercusp/blueprint.yaml or harness:create).

tools.name: brainstorm:chat
tools.description: Brainstorm partner chat turn: expand ideas, suggest analogues, challenge assumptions. Streams deltas; returns the assembled final text.

tools.name: calibration:summary
tools.description: Per-persona per-domain calibration from recorded bets: Brier score, base rate, sample size, and the shrunk trust weight (0.5 = unknown, →1 proven-sharp, →0 proven-noisy) — plus the open-bet rollup. Read-only over harness_shared.calibration_predictions.

guidance.when: Weighing how much to trust a persona's stated confidence — before acting on a 'fixed, 0.9 sure' claim, when triaging items whose ranker breakdown shows a calibration contribution, or when reviewing whose bets are sharp vs noise.
guidance.notWhen: You want the queue order itself — improvements:digest (the ranker already folds calibration in as a feature). You want raw bet rows — they are deliberately not exposed; the scores are the consumption surface.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest (rank.features shows a 'calibration' contribution) → calibration:summary { predictor } for that bettor's record → weigh their claim accordingly.

tools.name: capability:bash
tools.description: Run a shell command (bash -c) server-side in the project dir. Streams combined output; large output spills to a log file. Set run_in_background for long jobs (build/test/dev-server) and poll with capability:bash_output.

guidance.when: Run any shell command — build, test, git status, file inspection, scripts. For a command that runs longer than ~1–2 min (build, test suite, dev server), pass run_in_background:true and poll capability:bash_output.
guidance.notWhen: To read/write/edit a single file, prefer capability:read / capability:write / capability:edit (they coordinate the file lock and mirror the native editors). For git, prefer capability:git.
guidance.chaining: run_in_background:true → returns a bash_id → capability:bash_output { bash_id } to read incremental output → capability:bash_kill { bash_id } to stop. Never push (git push is refused).

tools.name: capability:bash_kill
tools.description: Stop a background shell job (started by capability:bash run_in_background:true). Sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL. Returns the final tail of output.

guidance.when: Stop a background job you no longer need (a dev server, a runaway build).
guidance.notWhen: A job that already finished — capability:bash_output already shows its terminal status.
guidance.chaining: capability:bash { run_in_background:true } → … → capability:bash_kill { bash_id }.

tools.name: capability:bash_output
tools.description: Read new output from a background shell job (started by capability:bash run_in_background:true). Returns output since the last read plus status (running/completed/failed/…) and exit code.

guidance.when: Poll a background job started by capability:bash. Call repeatedly to drain output as it runs; the final call after status leaves "running" gives the tail + exit code.
guidance.notWhen: For a foreground command — its output is in the capability:bash result directly. Note: on a shared dev box, ANY agent restarting the operator (:3070/:3170) kills every other agent's in-flight background jobs — a miss reporting `reason: "stranded_by_operator_restart"` (with a log tail) means that happened, not a wrong id; re-run capability:bash rather than treating it as a tool bug.
guidance.chaining: capability:bash { run_in_background:true } → capability:bash_output { bash_id } (repeat) → capability:bash_kill to stop early.

tools.name: capability:computer
tools.description: Operate a sandboxed desktop (GUI) — screenshot, click, type, key, scroll — using the canonical computer-use action vocabulary. Returns a screenshot image after each action so you can see the result. ONLY for genuinely visual/GUI steps: for anything scriptable (files, CLIs, APIs) prefer capability:bash, and for web pages prefer a browser tool — both are faster and more reliable than pixel-clicking.

guidance.when: A task needs a GUI app that has no CLI/API — clicking buttons, reading what is on screen, operating a desktop program. Call `screenshot` first to see, then act on what you see.
guidance.notWhen: Anything scriptable (create files, run a program, hit an API) → capability:bash. A web page → a browser tool (DOM automation is more reliable + cheaper than pixel-clicking). Never use this to operate the host machine — it only drives the agent's leased sandbox desktop.
guidance.chaining: screenshot → inspect the image → left_click/type/key at the coordinates you see → screenshot to confirm. Repeat.

tools.name: capability:edit
tools.description: Exact string replacement in a file, like the native Edit tool. old_string must match exactly and (unless replace_all) be unique. Acquires the per-path file lock server-side before editing. Path is absolute or relative to the project dir.

guidance.when: Make a targeted in-place change to an existing file. Include enough surrounding context in old_string to make it unique, or set replace_all.
guidance.notWhen: Creating a file or replacing it wholesale — use capability:write. Reading — use capability:read.
guidance.chaining: capability:read → capability:edit. On a file_locked result, wait/pivot/coordinate with the holder.

tools.name: capability:fetch
tools.description: Make an outbound HTTP(S) request and return status, headers, and (truncated) body. Body beyond the byte cap spills to a file. The sandbox egress policy bounds which hosts are reachable.

guidance.when: Fetch a URL — an API, a raw file, a docs page. For rich page-to-markdown extraction prefer the fetch_plus / firecrawl plugin tools when available.
guidance.notWhen: Reading a local file — use capability:read. Running a network CLI — use capability:bash (curl/wget).
guidance.chaining: Standalone. Large bodies spill to a log path you can capability:read.

tools.name: capability:git
tools.description: Run a git subcommand (argv, no shell) in the project dir. `push` is refused (git-sync owns push). Output spills to a log if large.

guidance.when: Inspect or stage git state — status, diff, log, show, add, commit (within a worktree). Prefer this over capability:bash for git so the action is gated as git, not arbitrary shell.
guidance.notWhen: Pushing (refused — git-sync owns push). Arbitrary shell — use capability:bash.
guidance.chaining: capability:git { args: ["status","--porcelain"] } → inspect → capability:git { args: ["add","-A"] } etc.

tools.name: capability:grant_role
tools.description: Runtime-grant capabilities to a role (unioned into loadRoleCapabilities, flag-gated). Replaces editing BLUEPRINT_ROLE_CAPS + redeploying to unblock a role. Privilege-escalation surface — enforces D-007: no protected-floor caps (secrets:*/processes:kill), cannot grant above the granter's own envelope, operator-authority only. Audited + one-call-revertible. Dark until papercusp-capability-grant-tool is enabled.

guidance.when: A role is blocked from its job for lack of a capability and you (operator/architect/mug) need to grant it live, instead of editing role-principal-caps.ts + redeploying.
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a cap, use capability:revoke_role. The protected floor (secrets:*, processes:kill) can never be granted. While the papercusp-capability-grant-tool flag is off this refuses (the grant surface is owner-ratified, D-007).
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows active grants (concern role-capability-grants); config:reset-overrides wipes them.

tools.name: capability:inspect
tools.description: Run a READ-ONLY code verification (typecheck or test) to confirm a claim about the code before diagnosing. Fixed safe commands only (npx tsc --noEmit, npm run test:affected, npx vitest run); never an arbitrary shell command. Use this — not capability:bash — to verify.

guidance.when: VERIFY a code claim before you report or diagnose: typecheck a package after a suspected type error, or run a package / test-file suite to confirm a failure actually reproduces. This is the sanctioned read-only exec for confined fleet agents (capability:bash is gated for them).
guidance.notWhen: To READ a file use capability:read; to SEARCH use the Grep tool. To run an arbitrary or mutating command you need capability:bash (gated — escalate if you truly need it). This tool runs ONLY tsc --noEmit / tests, never a free-form command.
guidance.chaining: capability:read / Grep (inspect) → capability:inspect (typecheck/test to CONFIRM) → report a VERIFIED diagnosis. For a long suite pass run_in_background:true and poll capability:bash_output.

tools.name: capability:read
tools.description: Read a file (text) with line numbers, like the native Read tool. offset/limit window large files; long lines are truncated. Path is absolute or relative to the project dir.

guidance.when: Read a source/text file before editing it, or to inspect content. Use offset+limit to page through a large file.
guidance.notWhen: To run a command, use capability:bash. To search across files, use capability:bash with grep/rg.
guidance.chaining: capability:read → capability:edit (exact string replace) or capability:write (overwrite).

tools.name: capability:revoke_role
tools.description: Remove runtime-granted capabilities from a role (the inverse of capability:grant_role). Only affects the runtime grant store, never code-level role caps. Operator-authority, audited + one-call-revertible. Dark until papercusp-capability-grant-tool is enabled.

guidance.when: Walk back a runtime capability grant — confine a role after a grant proves too broad, or clean up grants. Reducing privilege, so always safe.
guidance.notWhen: To GRANT a cap, use capability:grant_role. To wipe ALL runtime grants at once (incident), use config:reset-overrides on the role-capability-grants concern.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active grants before/after.

tools.name: capability:terminal
tools.description: Open a NEW terminal window on the user's desktop and run a command in it — or open MANY at once with `terminals: [...]`. Each command runs, then its terminal drops to an interactive shell (stays open). Use this when the user should SEE / interact with real terminals (a dev server, a REPL, a watch process, an installer, a desktop fleet of agents). For headless execution with captured output, use capability:bash instead.

guidance.when: Open one or more visible desktop terminals and run commands the user should watch or interact with — a dev server, a REPL/installer, a `tail -f`, or N agent windows at once (pass `terminals: [...]`).
guidance.notWhen: For headless command execution with captured output / exit code, use capability:bash. This tool returns as soon as the terminals are spawned and CANNOT capture output (they are interactive and detached).
guidance.chaining: Returns immediately after spawning — it does NOT wait for the commands and has no output channel. Use EITHER `command` (single) or `terminals` (bulk, max 12), not both.

tools.name: capability:write
tools.description: Write a file (create or overwrite) like the native Write tool. Acquires the per-path file lock server-side before writing (busy → returns who holds it). Path is absolute or relative to the project dir.

guidance.when: Create a new file, or fully replace an existing one. For a partial change to an existing file prefer capability:edit.
guidance.notWhen: A small in-place change — use capability:edit (exact string replacement). Reading first — use capability:read.
guidance.chaining: capability:read (if overwriting) → capability:write. On a file_locked result, wait/pivot/coordinate with the holder.

tools.name: capability_envelope:set_role
tools.description: Read/set/clear a fleet role's runtime capability-envelope override (denyCapabilities / allowCapabilities), merged over the baked ROLE_ENVELOPES. Confine or loosen a role live (e.g. re-confine a misbehaving bee to read-only) without a deploy. DARK (papercusp-capability-envelope-overrides) + requires the CAPABILITY_ENVELOPE enforcement flag to bite. The universal floor (secrets:*/processes:kill) always applies. set/clear audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Incident response: confine a hallucinating/misbehaving role to read-only (denyCapabilities: capability:fs-write/capability:bash) or restore it, live. get to inspect the active override.
guidance.notWhen: To TIGHTEN the universal protected floor use capability_envelope:set_protected (tighten-only). To change quota use quota tools; tiers use capability_tier:set. Loosening cannot bypass the protected floor.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active envelope overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts them. Needs the owner to flip papercusp-capability-envelope-overrides + CAPABILITY_ENVELOPE to enforce.

tools.name: capability_tier:set
tools.description: Read/set/clear a runtime capability→tier override (low|medium|high), consulted before the baked tier table by papercuspTierFor. Fix a mis-tiering (e.g. a read mis-classified as a write inflating watchdog/ledger posture) without a deploy. DARK behind papercusp-auth-config-overrides; empty/OFF ⇒ baked table (byte-identical). LIVE for runtime tierFor callers (capability catalog + decision-ledger); load-time-stamped consumers (endpoint-auth exposure, watchdog timeout) pick it up on the next operator boot. set/clear audited + revertible.

guidance.when: A capability is mis-tiered (e.g. a cheap read classified medium/high, inflating its watchdog timeout or decision-ledger posture) and you want to correct it live. Requires papercusp-auth-config-overrides ON. op:get to read the active overrides.
guidance.notWhen: To grant/deny a capability to a role use the capability/envelope tools (tier is risk CLASSIFICATION, not access). A re-tier reaches the endpoint-auth exposure gate + watchdog only after an operator restart (it re-stamps tools at boot).
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active capability-tier-overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts to the baked table.

tools.name: cert:catalog
tools.description: Read CERTIFIED_CATALOG (provisioner/catalog.ts) — the provisioner wizard's certified/provisional combo catalog. Each entry carries its `status` ('provisional' = grounded in a real running config but not yet battery-certified; 'certified' = passed cert:run, with the `certification` evidence stamp attached). Pass `id` to fetch one entry; omit for the full catalog. Returns {ok, catalog} or {ok, entry} / {ok:false, error} if `id` is unknown.

guidance.when: Checking what's already certified before running cert:run again (avoid a redundant re-cert), or reading a specific entry's certification evidence (verdict/ranAt/manglingRate/summary).
guidance.notWhen: Certifying a NEW combo — that is cert:run. This tool never mutates the catalog (a certified verdict is hand-promoted into provisioner/catalog.ts per D-005, never written by an agent tool).
guidance.chaining: cert:catalog → (a combo is missing or provisional) → cert:run to certify it → hand-add/flip the CERTIFIED_CATALOG entry in code.

tools.name: cert:run
tools.description: Run the P-006 model-certification battery (behavior · trimmed-shape · comms · mangling-rate — a deterministic, no-LLM-judge harness, coordination-eval.ts D-002) LIVE against a served OpenAI-compatible backend, and return the CertReport (per-probe pass/fail + the aggregate mangling rate + a `certified`/`failed` verdict). Resolve the target EITHER by `backendId` (looked up in the local-backend registry — gateway:local_backend_list) OR an explicit `baseUrl` + `backend` kind. This is the on-demand re-cert surface for certifying additional models/configs beyond CERTIFIED_CATALOG entry #1 — it does NOT itself write a catalog entry; a human/agent promotes a `certified` verdict into provisioner/catalog.ts CERTIFIED_CATALOG by hand (per D-005, "never a parallel catalog"). Returns {ok, report}.

guidance.when: Certifying a NEW (model, quant, num_ctx, parallel, backend) combo before adding it to CERTIFIED_CATALOG, or re-certifying an existing one after a config/prompt change. Pass `backendId` when the backend is already registered (gateway:local_backend_list); otherwise pass `baseUrl` + `backend` directly.
guidance.notWhen: Reading already-certified entries — cert:catalog. Certifying a CLOUD (Claude/Codex) account — this battery is for the LOCAL inference-backend pool only. Scoring one gym run's subjective quality — gym:judge.
guidance.chaining: gateway:local_backend_list (find backendId) → cert:run { backendId, model } → on a `certified` verdict, hand-add the entry to provisioner/catalog.ts CERTIFIED_CATALOG.

tools.name: change_ledger:calendar
tools.description: The mutation-calendar advisory over the behavior-change ledger: per mutation class (gym, manual-prompt, repo-prompt, ablation) the activity count, first/last timestamps, and liveness inside the window — plus the D-003 overlap advisory when more than one AUTOMATED class is live ("one live mutation class at a time" is policy, not enforcement).

guidance.when: Before starting/scheduling a prompt-layer mutator (gym autoloop bring-up, an ablation run) — is another mutation class already live? Also the EKG's "what could explain this shift window" first read.
guidance.notWhen: You want the individual mutation rows — change_ledger:list.
guidance.chaining: change_ledger:calendar → on overlap, serialize with the other class's owner → change_ledger:list { mutationClass } for the specific rows.

tools.name: change_ledger:list
tools.description: List recent behavior-affecting changes — every ledgered prompt/rule mutation (gym champion commits, prompt-override API edits, repo playbook/persona file edits, ablations) newest first, with source, mutation class, target, diff ref, and actor. Read-only over harness_shared.behavior_change_ledger.

guidance.when: Attributing a behavior shift: "what changed in the prompt layer recently?" — after a fleet anomaly, before/after a gym promotion, or when auditing who mutated which role prompt and when.
guidance.notWhen: You want the overlap advisory / per-class liveness rollup — change_ledger:calendar. You want prompt CONTENT — read the prompt source or harness_prompt_overrides.
guidance.chaining: change_ledger:calendar (which classes are live) → change_ledger:list { mutationClass } for the rows → the diff_ref (gym proposal id / git sha) for the change content.

tools.name: chat:ask_choice
tools.description: Present the user with a structured set of clickable choices and BLOCK until they pick. The tool returns the chosen option(s) (or {declined:true} if the user skipped). Use for yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of questions with up to 6 options. Set multi:true for "select all that apply".

guidance.when: You need a yes/no, accept/reject, or pick-one-of decision from the user before continuing. Renders clickable buttons in the chat; the tool returns the choice as its result. You can keep working in the same turn after the result lands.
guidance.notWhen: For OPEN-ENDED questions ("describe what you want", "paste the error"), keep using plain text. Use 2-3 options; 4+ only when genuinely distinct (6 hard max).

tools.name: checkpoint:await
tools.description: Sleep until the current pipeline green-checkpoint resolves — arms awaits on BOTH release:green:<pipeline> (passed → advanced to main) and green-checkpoint:red:<pipeline> (held → not green) so you wake either way, instead of polling for the gate verdict. Pass pipeline to override; pass global:true only when you intentionally want every co-hosted pipeline verdict and will lineage-check payload.pipeline/payload.sha yourself. Then END YOUR TURN.

guidance.when: You need to know whether the gate went green (your change cleared into main) or is held (a test is red) before proceeding — instead of re-polling dev:pipeline_position / dev:build_status.
guidance.notWhen: Waiting for the DEPLOY (past the gate, live on :3070) — that is deploy:await. Configuring the gate — release:checkpoint-config.
guidance.chaining: checkpoint:await → end turn → on wake, payload tells you green (advanced) or red (payload.summary = failing tail) for this pipeline; resume or go fix the red.

tools.name: clamp:set_safe_tools
tools.description: Read/set/clear the NARROW-only override of the scoped-superuser cross-workspace safe-tool allowlist. Lists tools to REMOVE from the baked SCOPED_SAFE_CROSSWORKSPACE allowlist (the clamp then denies them from a scoped SU session). TIGHTEN-ONLY (remove-set, never add). DARK behind papercusp-auth-config-overrides; empty ⇒ baked allowlist (byte-identical). set/clear audited + revertible.

guidance.when: You want a scoped-superuser session to be DENIED a crossWorkspace tool the baked allowlist permits (narrow its cross-workspace reach) — live, no deploy. Requires papercusp-auth-config-overrides ON. op:get to read the active remove-set.
guidance.notWhen: You cannot ADD tools to the allowlist with this dial (tighten-only by design). To grant capabilities use the capability tools.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active auth-config-overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts (restores the full baked allowlist).

tools.name: code:run
tools.description: Run a multi-step tool-orchestration script (tools.ns.verb(args) + JS control flow) in ONE call and get back ONLY the script's returned summary — collapsing N tool round-trips (each re-reads your whole context) into one. WRITE THE SCRIPT DIRECTLY: no discovery pre-call is required — if you reference a tool name wrong, the result hands you the exact typed signatures inline to fix. Use dryRun:true to preview write-effect mutations before committing.

guidance.when: A task needs MANY tool calls with control flow — loop/branch/filter over results (list N items then act per item, fan-out reads, retry-until). Orchestrate them in ONE code:run and return a compact summary instead of paying a round-trip per call. Just write the script against tools.ns.verb(args) — you do NOT need a code:tools pre-call: a wrong name comes back with the typed signatures inline to fix (code:tools is there only if you want to pre-check shapes). Pass title+description so the run is saved as a reusable RECIPE other agents in your hive can find + reuse (every successful run is captured; the title+description make it discoverable instead of an auto-derived label).
guidance.notWhen: A single tool call, or a step that needs YOUR judgment mid-flow (read a result, then decide) — call tools directly. Preview mutations with dryRun before a committing run.
guidance.chaining: write the script → code:run { dryRun:true } → inspect plannedMutations → code:run. (Optional pre-check: code:tools { namespaces } for typed signatures — NOT required, a bad name returns them inline.)

tools.name: code:tools
tools.description: OPTIONAL pre-check of typed signatures for code:run — not required before a run (code:run returns the signatures inline if you name a tool wrong). No args → the namespace index (cheap). { namespaces } / { names } → full TS `tools.ns.verb(args)` signatures for just those, scoped to your allowed set. Read the signatures, then write a code:run script.

guidance.when: OPTIONAL — only when you want to pre-check exact arg shapes before authoring a code:run script (you do NOT have to: code:run hands you the typed signatures inline if a name is wrong). Start with no args to list namespaces, then request the one or two you need.
guidance.notWhen: A single direct tool call (no script), or you already know the signatures, or you would rather just write the code:run script and let a bad name return signatures inline. This is a lookup — it executes nothing.
guidance.chaining: OPTIONAL: code:tools {} → pick namespaces → code:tools { namespaces } → code:run { script }

tools.name: computer:list_desktops
tools.description: List the sandbox-desktop leases held in this operator process — each hive that holds a desktop and its display/width/height. Use to confirm computer:provision_desktop landed or to spot a leaked lease.

guidance.when: Checking which pots currently hold a sandbox desktop — after provisioning, before a VNC view, or auditing for leaks.
guidance.notWhen: Driving a desktop (capability:computer) or standing one up (computer:provision_desktop).
guidance.chaining: computer:provision_desktop → computer:list_desktops (verify) → computer:release_desktop.

tools.name: computer:provision_desktop
tools.description: Provision a sandboxed GUI desktop (isolated Xvfb + openbox, never host :0) for a pot so its cups can operate it via capability:computer. Optionally launches GUI apps on it. Idempotent (returns the existing desktop; apps launch only on first provision). Tear down with computer:release_desktop or pot:dissolve.

guidance.when: Equipping a pot for visual/GUI work — before a cup in that pot uses capability:computer. Pass `apps` to pre-launch the programs the cup will operate (e.g. a browser, a spreadsheet).
guidance.notWhen: For scriptable work (files/CLIs/APIs) no desktop is needed — bees use capability:bash. On a deployed desktop FRAME the per-slot Xvfb is leased by the frame bootstrap (acquireAgentDisplay), not this tool.
guidance.chaining: computer:provision_desktop { pot, apps } → spawn/let a bee in that hive call capability:computer → computer:list_desktops to inspect → computer:release_desktop when done.

tools.name: computer:release_desktop
tools.description: Tear down a pot's sandbox desktop (kill its Xvfb + apps, free the display) without dissolving the pot. Idempotent — a no-op if the pot holds no desktop. (pot:dissolve releases automatically.)

guidance.when: A pot is done with GUI work but stays alive — reclaim the Xvfb/display. Also good demo hygiene after computer:provision_desktop.
guidance.notWhen: Tearing down the whole pot — pot:dissolve already releases the desktop. There is nothing to release if the pot never provisioned one.
guidance.chaining: computer:list_desktops to see what is leased → computer:release_desktop { pot }.

tools.name: config:list-overrides
tools.description: Read every live runtime-config override diverging from baked defaults, across all registered concerns (watchdog tunables, …). Each key reports its effective value, the layer that set it, and the latest audit row. The observability surface over the runtime-config control tools so the override layer is never opaque.

guidance.when: You (or an operator debugging odd fleet behavior) need to see what runtime config has been changed away from its baked defaults — every override across all concerns, in one place, with who/when.
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE a value, use that concern's set tool (e.g. improvements:set-watchdog-tunables). To revert overrides to defaults, use config:reset-overrides.
guidance.chaining: config:reset-overrides to revert a concern (or all) back to baked defaults.

tools.name: config:reset-overrides
tools.description: Revert runtime-config overrides back to baked defaults — one concern (concern:"watchdog-tunables") or all (all:true). Each reset is audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness. The mid-incident "undo the overrides" companion to config:list-overrides.

guidance.when: Roll back runtime-config changes to baked defaults — a single concern after a bad tune, or everything at once during an incident ("reset all overrides").
guidance.notWhen: To SEE what's overridden first, use config:list-overrides. To change one value, use that concern's set tool.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides before to see what will reset, and after to confirm it cleared.

tools.name: config:set-compaction-limit
tools.description: Set THIS session's soft compaction limit (tokens) — a target below your model window; near it, reach a stopping point and call session:request_compaction. Persisted per session; visible in coord:presence.

guidance.when: Tune how large your context grows before you self-compact — raise it for wide-context work, lower it to stay sharp on a tight task.
guidance.notWhen: To compact right now — use session:request_compaction. To read your usage — it is injected each turn as `context: N/limit (X%)`.

tools.name: config:tiers-get
tools.description: Read the model-tier menu (stored, else the committed defaults) with each tier’s effective soft compaction limit — explicit per-tier value, else the model-derived default floor((window − margin) / 1.2). Also returns the per-role tier ceilings.

guidance.when: You need the tier menu (names, specs, backends) or the compaction limit a tier would seed — e.g. before editing it via config:tiers-set or picking a cup:spawn tier.
guidance.notWhen: To change YOUR OWN session’s limit — config:set-compaction-limit. To edit the menu — config:tiers-set.

tools.name: config:tiers-set
tools.description: Replace the model-tier menu wholesale (names, specs, backends, when-guidance, per-tier soft compaction limits). Invalid rows are dropped and limits clamped to each spec’s model-derived ceiling (limit × 1.2 ≤ window − margin). Pass tiers: [] to revert to the committed defaults.

guidance.when: Editing the tier menu — adding a tier, changing a spec, or setting a per-tier compaction limit the fleet seeds sessions with.
guidance.notWhen: To change YOUR OWN session’s limit — config:set-compaction-limit. To read the menu — config:tiers-get.
guidance.chaining: config:tiers-get first to see the current menu; edit; write back the full array.

tools.name: conversation:append
tools.description: Append a turn to the SHARED operator conversation thread the app's webview chat displays. Mirror your voice/TUI turns here so the local user sees the conversation in the app.

guidance.when: You (the voice-first Papercup) just heard the user or spoke a reply — append BOTH sides so the webview chat reflects the live conversation: the user's words as role:'user' (source 'voice_stt'), your spoken reply as role:'assistant' (source 'voice_tts').
guidance.notWhen: Don't append internal tool noise, code, or unspoken scratch — only the user-visible conversation turns.

tools.name: conversation:recent
tools.description: Read the most recent turns of the SHARED operator conversation thread (the app's webview chat) so you continue ONE thread across voice/TUI and the app.

guidance.when: You want the recent context of the shared app conversation — what the user typed or said in the webview chat — e.g. at the start of a voice exchange to continue where the app left off.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR own scrollback just read your TUI; this is the SHARED webview thread, not your session history.

tools.name: conversations:answer
tools.description: Answer one OR many question conversations. Appends an answer to each thread and notifies subscribers (the asker gets it in their inbox). The asker/resolver accepts an answer with conversations:resolve. Single: { id, body, mentions? }. Many same body: { ids:[…], body }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, body, mentions? }] (each carries its own answer). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, post_id? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You can answer an open question (you saw it via a topic subscription or conversations:list). Post the answer here so the asker is notified and the answer is captured on resolve. Answer several at once via items:[…] (each item supplies its own body).
guidance.notWhen: For a non-answer comment/clarification, use conversations:post. To accept your own/another answer and close the question, use conversations:resolve.
guidance.chaining: conversations:answer → the asker conversations:resolve (accepts it, captures it to the knowledge layer for the next asker).

tools.name: conversations:get
tools.description: Read one OR many conversations in full: the seed, topic tags, the whole thread (posts oldest-first), the accepted answer if resolved, and follower count. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, conversation? + topics/posts/subscriber_count | error }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest.

guidance.when: You have one or more conversation_ids (from coord:ask, conversations:list, or an inbox notice) and want the full thread. Pass every id you need at once via `ids` instead of calling per id.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing many → conversations:list.
guidance.chaining: conversations:get { ids:[…] } → conversations:answer / conversations:post / conversations:join / conversations:resolve.

tools.name: conversations:join
tools.description: Follow one OR many conversations so their updates are injected into your inbox. mode = full | digest | mention (D-006). Idempotent — re-joining updates the mode/TTL. leave:true stops following. Single: { id, mode?, ttl_sec?, leave? }. Many same mode: { ids:[…], mode?, leave? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, mode?, ttl_sec?, leave? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, mode? | left? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A specific conversation is one you want to track or contribute to. Posting/answering auto-joins you; call this to follow without posting, or to change your delivery mode. Follow several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…].
