guidance.notWhen: To follow an AREA (not one thread), use topics:subscribe. For a one-time read, just conversations:get.
guidance.chaining: conversations:list / conversations:get → conversations:join.

tools.name: conversations:list
tools.description: List conversations (questions + discussions), newest first. Filter by kind, state (open|resolved|closed), harness, and topic. Each row carries its topic tags; conversations:get for the full thread.

guidance.when: Browsing for open questions you could answer, or finding a conversation by topic/harness. For updates pushed to you, subscribe to a topic instead.
guidance.notWhen: You already have a conversation_id → conversations:get.
guidance.chaining: conversations:list → conversations:get → conversations:answer / conversations:join.

tools.name: conversations:post
tools.description: Start a discussion (open-ended) or append a reply to an existing conversation. Omit conversation_id to start a new discussion tagged with topics; pass conversation_id to reply. Replies fan out to the conversation's subscribers.

guidance.when: Open-ended coordination with no single answer ("how should we approach X?"), or contributing to an existing thread. For a question that wants an answer, use coord:ask instead.
guidance.notWhen: A factual question → coord:ask (it tries knowledge first). To accept an answer + close a question → conversations:resolve.
guidance.chaining: conversations:post (start) → others conversations:post (reply) / conversations:join. conversations:get to read the thread.

tools.name: conversations:promote
tools.description: Promote one OR many conversations (question/discussion) into engineer issues, carrying their thread. Mints an engineer_issues row (with the conversation's topics + scope), closes the conversation, and records the issue id. Single: { id, severity?, source?, harness? }. Many same severity/source: { ids:[…], severity?, source? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, severity?, source?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, issue? + thread_carried | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one not-found item never fails the rest. Use when a discussion concludes there is a real problem to track.

guidance.when: A conversation has concluded that there is a concrete, trackable problem — turn it into an issue so it can be claimed, prioritized, and promoted to a feature. Promote several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: A question that just needs an answer → conversations:resolve (captures the answer). An open discussion still in progress → leave it. To file a fresh issue unrelated to a conversation → work_items:create.
guidance.chaining: conversations:get → conversations:promote → work_items:get / work_items:claim. The issue keeps the conversation's thread; further discussion uses work_items:comment.

tools.name: conversations:resolve
tools.description: Resolve one OR many questions: accept an answer (by text or by accepted_post_id) and close it. The accepted answer is captured to the knowledge layer (mem0 by default) so the next coord:ask finds it synchronously. Notifies subscribers. Single: { id, accepted_answer | accepted_post_id, capture? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, accepted_answer | accepted_post_id, capture? }] (each carries its own answer). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, state? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one item that lacks an answer or is not found never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A question conversation has been answered satisfactorily. Accept the best answer here — this both closes it and feeds the answer back so nobody has to ask again. Resolve several at once via items:[…] (each item supplies its own accepted answer).
guidance.notWhen: Still gathering answers → leave it open. For an open-ended discussion that just ran its course, this still works (capture is skippable with capture:none).
guidance.chaining: conversations:answer → conversations:resolve { id, accepted_post_id }. Provide accepted_answer to write a synthesized answer instead of quoting a single post.

tools.name: coord:ack
tools.description: Acknowledge one OR many coord messages by msg_id. Posts a `kind: "ack"` entry in your outbox addressed back at each original sender, so they can see you received it. Single: { msg_id }. Many: { msg_ids:[…] } or items:[{ msg_id }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, msg_id, ack_msg_id? + acked_from? | error }], counts } — correlate by msg_id; an unknown msg_id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: After acting on (or deliberately not acting on) coord message(s) — closes the loop for the sender. Ack several at once via msg_ids:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For routine read-and-forget. Acks are most useful for hand-offs and questions where the sender is waiting.

tools.name: coord:ask
tools.description: Ask a question knowledge-FIRST. Runs search:semantic + mem0 before interrupting anyone: a hit returns answer candidates inline (with sources); a miss opens a `question` conversation routed to topic subscribers and returns immediately (answers arrive in your inbox — never blocks). Pass topics to route a miss; force_open:true to ask peers even when knowledge had candidates.

guidance.when: DEFAULT FIRST MOVE for any question you cannot answer from your own knowledge or the code — it routes to the peer/expert who owns the area (knowledge-first, non-blocking). Reach for this BEFORE escalating to the owner/human: ask peers here first; only ask the owner (coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate) if the best answer is still unclear after asking. Always include topics so a miss reaches the right people; pass harness for a harness-specific question.
guidance.notWhen: For an open-ended discussion (no single answer), use conversations:post. Do NOT jump to coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate (interrupting the owner) before trying coord:ask — escalate to the owner only when peers + knowledge leave the answer unclear. coord:ask is deliberately non-blocking; to turn-block on a peer/handoff use coord:escalate / coord:handoff.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → coord:ask (with topics). On a miss you get a conversation_id; conversations:get to read replies, conversations:resolve when answered. Still unclear after peers replied? THEN coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:ask-owner
tools.description: Ask the OWNER (the human) a question and wait a bounded time for an answer (opens a question thread + lands it in the human inbox). Returns { answered, answer }. For asking PEERS knowledge-first, use coord:ask instead.

guidance.when: You need the owner's (human's) input on a decision and can wait briefly, but want to proceed (e.g. fall through to a vote) if they don't respond in time.
guidance.notWhen: A peer question or a knowledge lookup — use coord:ask (knowledge-first: searches existing knowledge, then routes to topic subscribers). A blocking decision that MUST have a human answer — use coord:escalate (severity: blocker).

tools.name: coord:await-inbox
tools.description: Annotate your idle state at end-of-turn: refresh the "why I am idle" note on your inbox-wake watch (and optionally its wake floor), then end your turn. You are ALREADY always-armed at session start (turn-lifecycle-control), so a later coord:send {wake:true} re-invokes you whether or not you call this — this just records why you are idle for the wake turn. Returns the watch id + your inbox-wake key.

guidance.when: Optional, at end-of-turn when idle — to record WHY you are idle (the note rides your wake turn) and tune your wake floor. You are wakeable regardless; arming is automatic at session start. Then END YOUR TURN.
guidance.notWhen: You still have queued work — keep going. A specific one-shot readiness (a lock grant, a peer's artifact) — use events:await on that exact key. A sub-minute wait inside one turn — just block.
guidance.chaining: coord:await-inbox → end your turn. On wake the turn text carries the message that woke you (read coord:inbox for the full set). To stop watching: events:cancel.

tools.name: coord:catch-up
tools.description: Catch up on the message HISTORY for an audience you belong to — everything broadcast to a @fleet:<slug> / @topic:<slug> (or @plan:/@object:/@file:/*) you're a member of, newest-first. This is how you get the backlog after JOINING a fleet/topic or WAKING from a pause: broadcasts are not auto-polled, and your inbox only shows messages whose recipient list named you at send time. Bound the read by `limit` (last N messages) and/or `token_budget` (as much as fits in ~N tokens); paginate older with before_ts/next_cursor. Returns { audience, count, total, tokens, next_cursor, rows }. You must currently belong to the audience (low-tier, membership-checked) — use coord:feed for the unscoped, high-tier firehose.

guidance.when: You just joined a fleet/topic, or woke after being paused/offline, and want what was said to that audience while you were away. The pull counterpart to an @fleet:/@topic: broadcast.
guidance.notWhen: For messages addressed to YOU personally use coord:inbox; for the all-agent firehose use coord:feed (audit:read). This is scoped to ONE audience you belong to.

tools.name: coord:conditions
tools.description: The live "what is wrong RIGHT NOW" view: folds condition-keyed severe-event broadcasts (git-sync stalls, green-gate freezes, …) into per-condition STATE instead of message history. Returns open conditions first (latest alarm newer than any resolution) with first_seen/last_seen/alarm_count/latest_summary, then recently-resolved ones (resolved_at + resolved_summary). An OPEN condition is claimable work; a resolved one needs no action.

guidance.when: Orienting on current system health — "is anything wrong right now?" — before claiming a stall/red-gate broadcast, or when an old severe-event alarm in your inbox needs a live open/resolved verdict.
guidance.notWhen: For your addressed mail use coord:inbox (stale alarms there already carry resolved:true). For human-facing escalations use coord:escalations. For agent liveness use coord:presence.

tools.name: coord:declare-intent
tools.description: Declare what you are working on right now — a one-line intent, optionally the plan slug, the plan items you are taking (auto-claimed as your lane), and the files in scope. Other agents see this via coord:presence / fleet:assignments. Declares your whole current state; omitted fields reset (except claims — omitted `items` leaves claims untouched). A broad "all remaining items" intent declared with no structured `items` gets an advisory `overCoverageHint` back (EI-5873) — a peer declaring the same broad scope has no structural signal to catch the overlap otherwise.

guidance.when: Starting a distinct piece of work, so other agents see what you have taken on. When the work is plan items, pass them as `items` — that claims your lane structurally instead of describing it in prose. Especially for a broad "take everything remaining" directive: enumerate the items so a colliding peer sees a real conflict instead of two agents each independently claiming to own the whole set (EI-5873).
guidance.notWhen: Every turn — the OMP hook heartbeats automatically; call this when your intent changes.
guidance.chaining: coord:declare-intent { intent, current_plan_slug, items: ["P-001", "P-002"] } → work → plans:set-status done releases each as you finish. A reported conflict means a live peer holds that item — coordinate or re-lane. Items in `claims.unknown` did not parse as plan items and were NOT claimed — fix the plan format or the ids.

tools.name: coord:deliberate
tools.description: Run the uncertainty ladder on a decision: ask the owner first → if unresolved, run a vote → if the vote is split, escalate a curated summary. The full escalate-only-when-needed flow.

guidance.when: A consequential decision where the owner might already have an answer, but you want an automatic fallback to a vote and a curated escalation rather than blocking.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the owner has no opinion (go straight to coord:vote) or the choice is trivial (just decide).

tools.name: coord:dispatch
tools.description: Hand a lane to a peer in ONE call: assign the plan items to `to` (durable lane) + deliver the `note` to its inbox + WAKE it now, then report pickup ({ woken, delivered, sessionState }). Replaces hand-composing plan_items:assign + coord:send + events:emit + the coord:inbox-wake:<id> key. FLAGS a non-wakeable target: an `ended` sessionState (or recipient_dead) means the lane was assigned but no live process will pick it up until a relaunch — a loud miss, never a silent woken:0. `planSlug`+`items` are optional (omit for a pure directed wake — "resume what I sent you").

guidance.when: You are a coordinator/Mug handing a specific lane to ANOTHER agent and want it picked up NOW — "su-7a2a, take fleet-dispatch P-001..P-004". One call assigns + wakes + confirms. Target a `parked` agent (coord:presence → sessionState:parked is the ideal); a `live` agent already running sees the note mid-turn.
guidance.notWhen: Just sharing context / asking a question (coord:send). Claiming work for YOURSELF (plan_items:claim / coord:declare-intent items). A broadcast — dispatch is single-target + wake, never "*". The target is `ended` (coord:presence) — it needs a relaunch/resume, not a dispatch (the wake cannot land).
guidance.chaining: coord:presence (find a `parked`/wakeable target) → coord:dispatch { to, planSlug, items, note } → check `woken`/`warning`. A woken target then: coord:orient → plan_items:my_items → claim + work the dispatched lane.

tools.name: coord:emit
tools.description: Emit a structured LIFECYCLE coordination notification (completion / claim / window / handoff / finding). The system fires this automatically from lifecycle events; agents rarely call it directly — use coord:send for unpredictable, contextual messages.

guidance.when: Almost never directly — the event-reaction rules fire coord:emit automatically when a work_item completes/claims, a coordination-window opens/closes, etc. Call it by hand ONLY to emit a recognized-shape lifecycle event the rules do not yet cover.
guidance.notWhen: For a genuinely contextual message (a finding's nuance, a design call, a question, a hand-written status), use coord:send — that is the unpredictable residual coord:emit deliberately does NOT carry.
guidance.chaining: The lifecycle rules render the payload via the coord-lifecycle render layer, then fire this. Pair with coord:inbox to see emitted lifecycle.

tools.name: coord:escalate
tools.description: Raise an escalation to the human. Provide severity (blocker | question | advisory), a one-line summary, and optionally a body and a small list of choice options to make resolution one click.

guidance.when: A decision you should not make alone, a blocker that requires human input, or a risky operation that needs explicit confirmation.
guidance.notWhen: Routine status updates — use coord:send. File contention — locks:queue already names the holder.

tools.name: coord:escalations
tools.description: List escalations addressed to the human — NEWEST-FIRST and bounded at the storage layer (EI-1548: never loads the whole backlog into memory). Default page 50, max 500. Filter by status=open / status=resolved. `truncated:true` means older escalations exist beyond the window — raise maxRecords or narrow by status.

guidance.when: Showing the human inbox; diagnostics; checking your own past escalations.
guidance.notWhen: A specific msg_id you already have — there is no escalation read-by-id tool yet; coord:escalations + filter is enough at current volumes.

tools.name: coord:feed
tools.description: Read the COMPLETE coordination stream across every agent and channel — messages, acks, notifies, broadcasts, handoffs, escalations, resolutions, plan events — newest-first with a next-page cursor. Filter by kinds, owner (matches sender OR recipient; broadcasts match any owner), plan_slug, free-text `q` (over summary/body/from/to), and a since_ts/before_ts time window. before_ts is the pagination cursor (pass back the returned `nextCursor`). Returns `{ count, total, by_kind, next_cursor, rows }`; each row is the raw envelope plus `surface` (messages|escalations|handoffs|plan-events) and a derived `broadcast` flag.

guidance.when: You need the full fleet-wide coordination timeline — auditing what agents said to each other, tracing a broadcast/handoff/escalation chain, or backing an observer UI. The all-traffic counterpart to the per-owner coord:inbox.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR addressed messages use coord:inbox; for open human escalations use coord:escalations; for live "who is active" use coord:presence. coord:feed is the read-everything firehose, not a working inbox.

tools.name: coord:glance
tools.description: One cheap combined fleet glance: wake mode (default) + staged-wake count, bees in flight (bees.running = fresh-heartbeat nursery rows, a process-alive signal that can include parked/idle sessions; bees.working = the confirmed-active subset with fresh child-stdout output — prefer it for real health checks), paused governor buckets, recent cross-CLI activity rows, and contextual tips (with ready-to-run slash commands) evaluated for the caller's audience. With audience 'user' also returns a server-rendered `display` block (title + statusline lines + tip notice) that client status surfaces print verbatim — the single-source TUI render. The statusline/TUI read — one call instead of four.

guidance.when: A status surface (statusline, TUI bar, dashboard widget) needs the fleet's headline state in one round-trip, or you want the current contextual tips for an audience.
guidance.notWhen: Deep rate-limit telemetry (usage %, $spend) — dev:rate_governor_status. Full presence roster — coord:presence. Reviewing/releasing the staged wakes themselves — coord:wake-queue.

tools.name: coord:handoff
tools.description: Record a work transition. Either OPEN a new handoff to other agents (provide `to[]`, `plan_slug`, `summary`, etc.) OR ACCEPT an existing one by passing `accept_msg_id` alone.

guidance.when: Wrapping up your piece of a plan and naming who picks up next — or accepting a handoff someone made to you.
guidance.notWhen: A routine status update — use coord:send. A blocking decision — use coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:handoff_config
tools.description: Read or set the stale-handoff auto-expiry TTL (handoffTtlMs): a pending coordination handoff older than this is auto-expired by the periodic reconcile sweep. Default 12h. set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Shorten the TTL to clear stale handoff offers faster (a successor chasing a dead offer wastes a turn), or lengthen it if legitimate handoffs routinely sit unaccepted longer than 12h.
guidance.notWhen: For stale work-item CLAIMS use work_items:reclaim_config; for idle sessions use coord:session_reaper_config. This only governs pending HANDOFF expiry.
guidance.chaining: coord:handoffs lists open handoffs; config:list-overrides shows the active override.

tools.name: coord:handoffs
tools.description: List handoff records, each annotated with its acceptance/expiry sibling if one exists. Optional `status` filters to open (no acceptance, not auto-expired), accepted, or expired (auto-expired by the stale-handoff reconcile after sitting pending past the 12h TTL — F-FIX-037).

guidance.when: Diagnostics — "who handed what to whom?", "what handoffs to me are still open?", or "which lapsed unaccepted?" (status: "expired").
guidance.notWhen: A single known msg_id — there is no read-by-id tool yet; the listing is small.

tools.name: coord:inbox
tools.description: Read your coordination inbox — messages, acks, handoffs etc. addressed to you (or broadcast). Returns a summary header (counts by kind) + the most-recent `limit` entries (default 50). Ambient system broadcasts (service-health, rate-limit pauses, and the per-sync doc-freshness RE-VERIFY digest) are excluded by default — pass include_ambient to see them. Repeated categorized system broadcasts collapse to one row with `repeat_count` + `first_seen_ts`; a stale severe-event alarm whose condition later cleared carries `resolved:true` + `resolved_at` — do not investigate a resolved condition. `since_ts` filters strictly later than the given ISO timestamp; `kinds` narrows to specific entry kinds. CAUTION (WI-1600 since_ts gap): in a tail-poll, never seed since_ts to wall-clock now/poll-start — anything that landed earlier stays invisible to every later poll. Read once unfiltered, then advance the cursor to that read's `summary.newest_ts`; or skip polling via the push-based `coord:await-inbox`.

guidance.when: At turn start (the OMP hook will do this for you once it ships); whenever you suspect another agent contacted you.
guidance.notWhen: For agent-presence ("who is active?") — use coord:presence. For file locks — use locks:queue. To WAIT for one specific message/handoff — prefer coord:await-inbox (push/wake) over a since_ts poll (see the WI-1600 CAUTION).

tools.name: coord:message-agent
tools.description: Open a work-item-scoped conversation with one OR several specific agents — the inbox's "Message owner" action, generalized. Creates a browseable discussion thread (Brief 25's conversations tab) scoped to the item's harness, subscribes the named agent(s), and pings them so they reply in-thread. Returns { conversation_id, thread_id, notified, subscribed }.

guidance.when: You (or the human via the inbox) want to message the agent that owns a specific work-item — start a durable, scoped thread with them about that item.
guidance.notWhen: A quick one-off note to a peer with no thread — use coord:send. A question to the OWNER/human — coord:ask-owner. A reply in an existing conversation — conversations:post.
guidance.chaining: coord:message-agent → conversations:get to read the thread → conversations:post to reply.

tools.name: coord:orient
tools.description: One agent wake-orientation + session-bootstrap read: your assignments (+lane+load), the claimable backlog, your inbox summary, and the recent plan-events delta — plus, with `intent`, a memory recall AND a coord:declare-intent so peers see you. The mandated bootstrap (memory:search + coord:inbox + coord:plan-events + declare + assignments + claimable) in ONE round-trip; a fleet member also gets a compact fleet-health glance.

guidance.when: At the START of a turn / on waking. Pass `intent` (your one-line task) for the whole bootstrap in ONE round-trip: assignments + claimable + inbox + plan-events + a memory recall + your intent DECLARED to peers. Omit `intent` for a lighter re-orientation. On a repeating LEADER/MONITOR tick pass `mode:'monitor'` — skips the claimable/facts/plan-events/fleet/recipes/recall legs, keeping fleet:assignments + inbox + declare.
guidance.notWhen: A human status-surface render (coord:glance display block — orient folds only the health counts) or the full presence roster (coord:presence). After a successful orient do NOT re-call coord:plan-events / memory:search / coord:inbox / coord:glance / coord:declare-intent — it ALREADY returned them (pass afterCompaction:true for fuller inbox + the recovery block).
guidance.chaining: Bundles fleet:assignments + work_items:list + coord:inbox + coord:plan-events [+ memory:search + recipes:search + declare with `intent`] — prefer at wake over separate calls. A close `recipes` hit → recipes:run it. → work_items:pickup { id, intent }.

tools.name: coord:plan-events
tools.description: Read the plan-event history — created / now_updated / decision_added / item_added / item_status_changed / promoted events across all plans. Returns the most-recent events first-bounded (a no-arg call is always size-capped so it never overflows the result), newest kept. Widen with `since_ts` (events strictly later than that ISO timestamp), `plan_slug` (one plan), `files_back` (N rotation files), or `limit` (max events). Returns `{ events, total, truncated }`. Distinct from coord:inbox (which scans messages, not plan-events).

guidance.when: Turn start — the OMP coordination extension calls this to show which plans changed since the agent last read. Also ad-hoc, to review recent plan activity.
guidance.notWhen: For messages / notifies / handoffs addressed to you — use coord:inbox.

tools.name: coord:presence
tools.description: List coordination agents and whether each can take work now. Active rows are the actionable roster; ended rows are excluded except in an owner-targeted lookup. Read summary.wakeable plus each row's sessionState and wakeable before dispatching. Defaults to your hive; admins/queen may widen scope. Re-poll cheaply with since:<etag>.

guidance.when: Use before dispatch or handoff to see who is live, parked, wakeable, and already occupied. Parked + wakeable is the normal dispatch target; ended needs relaunch. Pass owner:<id> for one specific agent.
guidance.notWhen: Not for file freedom (locks:queue), not as a default every-turn poll when coord deltas already cover changes, and not for a full historical ended-agent dump.
guidance.chaining: Read once, then follow coord deltas. If you must re-poll, pass since:<etag>; unchanged state returns a tiny stub instead of the full roster.

tools.name: coord:rebind-identity
tools.description: Migrate every ownerId-keyed surface from a DEAD predecessor sid to a live one after a relaunch/recovery changed your PAPERCUSP_SID: armed loop routine, loop carry-note (+walls), plan/work-item claims, scheduler claim-spec, standing awaits, fleet membership/leadership, open held work-items, owner-scoped facts, held FILE LOCKS + lock waiters (EI-8999/P-002 — a separate side-database, rekeyed too). Idempotent — re-run to finish a partial pass. Refuses while the old sid still shows a fresh presence heartbeat (a live peer) unless force:true. Returns { ok, from, to, surfaces:[{surface,moved,…}], totalMoved }.

guidance.when: Your session recovered under a NEW PAPERCUSP_SID (the SessionStart banner names both ids, or coord:whoami disagrees with the id that armed your loop/claims): rebind from the old id to yours, or your loop fires at a dead owner and your carry-note, claims, awaits and held items never follow you.
guidance.notWhen: Both ids belong to LIVE sessions — this migrates a dead identity, it does not merge two live ones. Routine wake/claim issues without an id change — that is coord:orient / loop:status territory.
guidance.chaining: After a successful rebind run coord:orient { afterCompaction:true } — the recovery block re-reads the moved surfaces under your live id.

tools.name: coord:resolve
tools.description: Resolve one OR many escalations by msg_id. Records the chosen option id (or arbitrary string) and optional note as an append-only escalation_resolved event. Single: { msg_id, choice, note? }. Many same choice: { msg_ids:[…], choice, note? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ msg_id, choice, note? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, msg_id, escalation? | error }], counts } — correlate by msg_id; a not_found / already_resolved on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: The human (or an authorised agent acting on their behalf) has decided how to proceed on open escalation(s). Resolve several at once via msg_ids:[…]+choice or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Acknowledging without deciding — use coord:ack. The escalation file is the human-resolution surface.

tools.name: coord:roster
tools.description: ONE read door with an explicit lens: view=live (in-a-turn presence), members (fleet/hive membership), claims (who-on-what-item), history (who-was-ever-here). Same underlying model; coord:presence / fleet:status / fleet:assignments / coord:glance become thin aliases (or deprecate). Kills "which of 5 tools do I call".

guidance.when: Before dispatch/handoff/routing: who can take work (view=live)? Who joined what fleet (view=members)? Who's on plan P (view=claims)? Historical who-was-ever-here (view=history).
guidance.notWhen: Being notified of future changes (subscribe fleet_assignment change-feed). Full message history (coord:inbox). Rate-limit telemetry (dev:rate_governor_status).
guidance.chaining: coord:roster { view } → read ONCE per turn; tail [coord+N] deltas for transitions. For history, use coord:catch-up after to refine by topic/plan.

tools.name: coord:send
tools.description: Send a message to other coordination agents — ONE message (single form) OR N distinct messages (items:[…]). `to` is ownerIds; ["*"] broadcasts, ["human"] surfaces to the user. In a fleet, a bare ["*"] auto-scopes to your fleet (reported `scopedBroadcast`); pass allHive:true for a genuine hive-wide notice. Default INJECTED — lands in the recipient's inbox, seen next turn. `wake` ALSO re-invokes a sleeping recipient now ('required' → a miss returns recipient_absent:true; 'optimistic' → silent best-effort over a durable backstop). Single: { to, summary, body?, wake?, … }. Many distinct: items:[{ to, summary, … }]. A DIRECTED send defaults `wakeOnReply` — you're auto-woken when a peer replies (set false to opt out; broadcasts off). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, to, msg_id? … | error }], counts } — correlate by `to`, not position; one failed message never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Sharing context or asking a question. Use items:[…] for many distinct messages. wake:'required' = recipient must act now, miss → recipient_absent. wake:'optimistic' = best-effort over a named backstop (`backstop:`). A running recipient already sees the inject — a wake is wasted on it.
guidance.notWhen: Human reply: just speak. File lock: locks:acquire. Don't wake for ambient notes (inject is default; wake = billable). ONE msg to MANY: single `to:[…]` — `items` is many-distinct-messages. Work transfer: coord:handoff. Without a backstop, wake:'optimistic' miss is SILENT — use wake:'required' + confirm woken≥1.

tools.name: coord:session_reaper_config
tools.description: Read or set the idle-session reaper grace (sessionReaperGraceMs): a dead-process session is reaped once its owner has been gone past this window. Default = the 10-min liveness window. A set with dryRun returns a WOULD-REAP count at the proposed grace (marks nothing) to de-risk the change. set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune how aggressively dead-process ghost sessions are reaped — shorten to reclaim the operator footprint faster, lengthen if a just-launched session is being reaped before its first presence beat. dryRun first to see the would-reap count.
guidance.notWhen: For stale work-item claims use work_items:reclaim_config; for handoff expiry use coord:handoff_config. To ARM the reaper itself, flip FLAGS.IDLE_SESSION_REAPER via /admin/features (this only tunes the grace).
guidance.chaining: set with dryRun:true previews the would-reap count; config:list-overrides shows the active override.

tools.name: coord:thread
tools.description: Reconstruct a coord thread rooted at `root_msg_id` — every entry connected via the `related_msg_id` chain, sorted by ts ascending.

guidance.when: You want the full conversation around a coord message (replies, acks, resolutions).
guidance.notWhen: For a fresh inbox sweep — use coord:inbox.

tools.name: coord:thread-post
tools.description: Post a message to a coordination thread by conversation_id (e.g. a spawned voter casting its structured ```vote``` block, or the advocate posting its ```advocate``` objection).

guidance.when: You were spawned into a vote/deliberation with a CONVERSATION_ID and need to cast your structured vote or objection into that thread.
guidance.notWhen: Replying in an open conversation you joined — use conversations:post. A direct message to an agent — coord:send.

tools.name: coord:vote
tools.description: Run a diverse-lens, confidence-weighted vote on a decision and get back a resolution (decisive) or a curated escalation (split). One voter per lens + an advocate arguing against the lead.

guidance.when: You face a genuinely uncertain, consequential choice between named options and want a diverse, anti-correlated read before committing — instead of deciding alone or escalating raw.
guidance.notWhen: A trivial or reversible choice — just decide. A pure factual lookup — use search/docs. To ask the human directly, use coord:ask-owner / coord:escalate.

tools.name: coord:wake
tools.description: Wake a PARKED agent NOW so it starts a turn and re-orients on its already-claimed lane — the discoverable alias for the events:emit coord:inbox-wake:<id> key (which agents kept 404ing on as coord:wake/coord:nudge). Single-target (never '*'). Optional `note` is a one-line nudge; omit for a bare wake. Returns { ok, to, woken, recipient_dead?, warning? }. A wake that reaches no live session is a LOUD miss (the target is `ended` → relaunch it), never a silent woken:0. To ALSO hand off a lane, use coord:dispatch; to deliver a contextual message, coord:send {wake:'required'}.

guidance.when: The work is ALREADY assigned to the target (plan_items:assign or a prior dispatch) and you just need it to start a turn and pick it up — a re-orient nudge. Pick a `parked` target (coord:presence → sessionState:parked).
guidance.notWhen: You are assigning a NEW lane — use coord:dispatch (assign+wake+confirm). You have a contextual message to deliver — use coord:send {wake:'required'}. The target is `ended` (coord:presence) — it needs a relaunch/resume, not a wake.
guidance.chaining: coord:presence (find a parked target) → coord:wake { to } → check `woken`/`warning`. The woken target: coord:orient → claim + work its lane.

tools.name: coord:wake-mode
tools.description: Read or set an agent's wake mode — auto (wakes fire immediately) or manual (wakes are staged for the owner to release/edit/skip). Omit `mode` to read; omit `agent` to read/set the global default. The pause/edit gate (hive-agent-tabs D-005).

guidance.when: Switching an agent (or the default) between auto and manual wake delivery — e.g. pausing a cup's auto-injected turns to review them first, or switching back.
guidance.notWhen: Reading who's online or what an agent is doing — that's coord:presence / fleet:assignments. Reviewing the staged wakes themselves — that's coord:wake-queue.

tools.name: coord:wake-queue
tools.description: Review a manual-mode agent's STAGED wakes: list them, release one (deliver as-is or edited as the agent's next turn), skip one (discard), or drain the whole queue — release_all delivers ONE coalesced wake for everything staged; skip_all discards everything. The pause/edit gate's review surface (hive-agent-tabs D-005 / P-009).

guidance.when: Reviewing a manual-mode agent's staged wakes from its pane — releasing the ones to deliver (optionally edited) and skipping the rest. Draining a backlog → release_all (one consolidated turn) or skip_all, never N individual releases.
guidance.notWhen: An auto-mode agent — its wakes fire immediately, nothing is staged. Changing the mode itself — that's coord:wake-mode.

tools.name: coord:watermark
tools.description: Read a coordination watermark — last-read ISO timestamps for messages / escalations / plan-events + the notify msg_ids surfaced. DEFAULT: your own. Pass `agent` to read a PEER's: their `read_through_ts` (messages_shown_ts) is a READ-RECEIPT — ≥ your message's ts ⇒ they've SEEN it (ping them, don't re-route); behind ⇒ not yet seen (wait, or wake if idle). With `agent`+`sent_ts` you get a direct `seen` boolean.

guidance.when: Turn start — the OMP coordination extension calls this to scope the inbox to new entries. To check if a PEER has seen a message you sent (READ-RECEIPT, EI-2042): coord:watermark { agent: <their ownerId from coord:presence>, sent_ts: <your message ts> } → seen:true means it was injected into their context.
guidance.notWhen: Routine reads — coord:inbox without a watermark returns the full inbox.

tools.name: coord:watermark-set
tools.description: Advance your coordination watermark. Call at TURN END with the newest ISO timestamp you have seen on each surface. Partial update — omitted fields keep their current value. `subscriptions_fired` is replaced wholesale when supplied.

guidance.when: Turn end — the OMP coordination extension records how far you read this turn.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-turn — advancing early would hide notifications that arrive before the turn finishes.

tools.name: coord:whoami
tools.description: Return the coordination identity the server resolved for you: ownerId (the stable per-agent id), ownerLabel, source, workspaceId, userId, your named-fleet membership (fleetSlug/fleetRole, from the launch env), and your inbox_wake_key (the key a coord:send {wake:true} fires + the one coord:await-inbox watches). A debug aid for confirming how the coordination layer sees this agent.

guidance.when: Debugging identity — "what ownerId am I?" before relying on lock or message behaviour.
guidance.notWhen: Routine work — identity is resolved automatically by every coord:* and locks:* call.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_get
tools.description: Fetch documentation pages from any registered harness by explicit slug. Batch up to 10; pass `heading` (single-slug only) for a section slice. Per-slug error envelope.

guidance.when: You have slugs from cross_harness:docs_outline and need the page contents from a specific harness (named by harnessSlug arg).
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs } → optionally re-fetch with { harnessSlug, slugs: [picked], heading } for surgical reads.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_outline
tools.description: Outline of any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. For engineers operating outside a harness context who need to query a specific harness's docs. Per-run cached.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (no spawn URL harness slug) but need a specific harness's documentation. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already inside a harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use docs:outline instead, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_outline { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs }.

tools.name: cross_harness:docs_search
tools.description: Keyword search across any registered harness's documentation by explicit slug. Returns ranked hits (slug, title, description, excerpt). For out-of-harness engineers who need to find content in a specific harness without scanning its outline by hand.

guidance.when: You have specific terminology in mind and want to find which page in a specific harness covers it. Faster than scanning cross_harness:docs_outline by hand when the section name is non-obvious.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside a harness — use docs:search, which auto-targets your harness. You do not know which harness to query — list with `harness:list` or `cross_harness:docs_outline` per slug first.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:docs_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:docs_get { harnessSlug, slugs: [top-hit] }.

tools.name: cross_harness:inbox
tools.description: Read messages addressed to a harness (status pending|all|other; optional role filter).

guidance.when: You need to see messages addressed TO a specific harness across senders. The cross-harness analog of `messages:inbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR (the calling principal's) inbox, use `messages:inbox`. For sent items, use `cross_harness:outbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:outbox
tools.description: Read messages a harness sent (cross-schema scan by from_slug).

guidance.when: You need to see what a specific harness sent — across recipients. Cross-harness analog of `messages:outbox`.
guidance.notWhen: For YOUR outbox, use `messages:outbox`. For incoming, use `cross_harness:inbox`.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_get
tools.description: Fetch the full parsed structure of one plan in any harness by explicit slug: frontmatter, ## Now, items with effectiveStatus, decisions. Read-only.

guidance.when: You have a slug + harness from cross_harness:plans_list (or know both directly) and need the plan contents.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:get, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_list
tools.description: List plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. For agents operating outside a single harness context who need to query another harness's plans. Read-only — writes go through ambient plans:*.

guidance.when: You are not inside a harness context (or want to inspect a different harness from outside) and need a directory of that harness's plans. Pass harnessSlug explicitly.
guidance.notWhen: You are already in the target harness (ctx.harnessSlug is set) — use plans:list, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_list { harnessSlug } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug }.

tools.name: cross_harness:plans_search
tools.description: Keyword search across plans of any registered harness by explicit slug. Scopes: slug, title, now, items, decisions, prose (a slug fragment finds the plan it names). Read-only.

guidance.when: You're looking for prior work in another harness and don't have a slug. Pass harnessSlug + query.
guidance.notWhen: You are inside the target harness — use plans:search, which auto-targets your harness.
guidance.chaining: cross_harness:plans_search { harnessSlug, query } → cross_harness:plans_get { harnessSlug, slug } on the top hit.

tools.name: cross_harness:recent_activity
tools.description: Workspace-wide recent activity feed (ts, harness_slug, action, subject, actor) from harness_shared.audit_log.

guidance.when: User asks "what's been happening across all my harnesses?", "any cross-harness activity?". The workspace-level activity feed.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's activity, use `harness:status`. For your own audit trail, use `audit:list`.

tools.name: cross_harness:supervisor_notes
tools.description: Read supervisor notes for a harness (id, body, source, created_at).

guidance.when: You need the supervisor's annotations on a harness — context the supervisor logged that's not in audit_log.
guidance.notWhen: For escalation flags + raw notes from the on-disk files, use `harness:escalation`. supervisor_notes is the PG-backed view.

tools.name: cup:spawn
tools.description: Spawn one background agent into a harness and return its spawn_id immediately. This is for autonomous-loop workers, not visible desktop terminals; use fleet:launch-on-plan for a desktop fleet on a plan. The run is tracked durably in the nursery, visible in fleet:tree, and stoppable with fleet:cancel. role="worker" requires chunk.

guidance.when: Use to place a background autonomous worker on new work: a cup, validator, scoper, architect, worker, or another supported role in a harness. Prefer role="cup" for self-pulling claim-spec work; factory roles are handed explicit feature/chunk work.
guidance.notWhen: Not for visible desktop terminals on a plan (fleet:launch-on-plan), simple lookups, or work that should just enter the durable work-item pipeline. Unsure which spawn tool you want? See the decision table: /internal/docs/agent-insights/desktop-fleet-vs-loop-cup.
guidance.chaining: cup:spawn → (later) fleet:tree { spawn_id } to watch → fleet:cancel { spawn_id } to abort.

tools.name: curation:change-feed
tools.description: The Change Feed — a derived projection over completion records (work-item completions, gym proposals, plan runs). Summaries reference the originals (rationale:feed pattern). One calm rollup per tick, drill-down on demand. Filter by harness or user-requested work.

guidance.when: You want to see recent changes across the fleet (what work finished, what proposals landed) without a replicated log. Pass userRequestedOnly to see only user-facing changes; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw fleet signals use curation:feed. For historical audit of all changes use the underlying work-items / coord-event-log directly.

tools.name: curation:feed
tools.description: Pull the curator-operator's salience-ranked fleet signals (escalations / blockers / decisions-needed / completions / progress) — the READ projection of the salience policy for a dashboard. A pure read of the CURRENT salient state (no loop, no chat-surface, no flag); the pui Fleet 'curated' view consumes this.

guidance.when: You want the curator's view of what matters across the fleet right now — the salience-ranked signals (escalations, blockers, decisions owed, recent completions) for a dashboard or status read. Pass surfaceOnly to get just the always-surface signals; harness to scope to one project.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw tool-call firehose use activity:recent / the activity stream. To make the operator SURFACE a message into the chat, that's the curation loop (flag-gated), not this read.

tools.name: curation:state-of-pot
tools.description: The "state of the Pot" corpus digest — a deterministic rollup of cross-corpus meta-patterns (recurring friction, time/token sinks, chronic deferrals, capability gaps) over the change feed + completions + reverts. The Blender loop's grounded ideation substrate; each pattern references the originals (drill in via work_items:get / plans:get / curation:change-feed).

guidance.when: You want the introspective "what are the Pot's standing meta-patterns" rollup — the recurring friction, where time/tokens go, what keeps being deferred, and the absent capabilities — as the grounded substrate for generative ideation (the Blender loop) or a state-of-the-Pot review. Each pattern carries refs back to the originals.
guidance.notWhen: For the raw stream of recent completions use curation:change-feed. For salience-ranked live fleet signals (escalations/blockers) use curation:feed. For the captured-improvement triage queue (auto vs human lanes) use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: curation:state-of-pot → drill into a pattern via its refs (work_items:get on wi:<id>, plans:get on plan:<slug>, curation:change-feed) → feed the digest to the Blender ideators.

tools.name: datatypes:catalog
tools.description: Browse the GLOBAL catalog of APPROVED published datatypes (the shared tier) — datatypes other workspaces published and an operator approved. Install one into your workspace with datatypes:install. Read-only.

guidance.when: Before declaring a new datatype — check whether an approved global one already fits, to reuse instead of re-inventing.
guidance.notWhen: To browse YOUR workspace's datatypes (datatypes:list). To declare one (meta:define-datatype).
guidance.chaining: datatypes:catalog → datatypes:install { id } → work_items:create { kind } / blueprint dependencies.datatypes.

tools.name: datatypes:get
tools.description: Fetch one OR many datatypes by id from the workspace registry — including the payload schema, tier, authoritative writer, and self-improvement surface. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, datatype? | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not position. Read-only.

guidance.when: When you have datatype id(s) (from datatypes:list) and want the full definition before referencing or instantiating it.
guidance.notWhen: To browse the registry — datatypes:list. To declare — meta:define-datatype.
guidance.chaining: datatypes:list → datatypes:get { ids:[…] } (inspect) → work_items:create { kind } / blueprint dependencies.datatypes.

tools.name: datatypes:install
tools.description: Install an APPROVED global datatype (from datatypes:catalog) into your workspace — copies its definition as a LOCAL datatype you can use like one you declared. Idempotent: already-present ⇒ no change.

guidance.when: After finding a useful approved datatype via datatypes:catalog — install it so this workspace can create instances / reference it.
guidance.notWhen: To declare a NEW datatype (meta:define-datatype). To publish one (datatypes:publish).
guidance.chaining: datatypes:catalog → datatypes:install { id } → work_items:create { kind } / dependencies.datatypes.

tools.name: datatypes:list
tools.description: List the workspace datatype registry — the reusable entity TYPES (bet, wager, forecast, position, …) declared via meta:define-datatype. Optionally filter by tier. Read-only. Pair the returned `total` with the (capped) `datatypes` array to know if the list was truncated.

guidance.when: To discover what datatypes exist before declaring a new one (avoid duplicates), or to find the name to put in a blueprint's dependencies.datatypes, or the generic-kind to pass to work_items:create.
guidance.notWhen: To read one datatype's full definition — use datatypes:get. To declare one — meta:define-datatype.
guidance.chaining: datatypes:list → datatypes:get { id } (inspect) → work_items:create { kind } / blueprint dependencies.datatypes.

tools.name: datatypes:publish
tools.description: Offer a workspace-local datatype to the shared/global tier (D-010): marks it PENDING operator moderation. Local usability is UNCHANGED — an operator approves it before it is globally visible. Idempotent: a datatype already pending/approved/rejected reports its current review_status.

guidance.when: When a datatype you declared (meta:define-datatype) is worth sharing globally, not just locally — so other workspaces can discover/reuse it.
guidance.notWhen: To declare a datatype (meta:define-datatype). To use one locally — a local datatype needs no publishing. Publishing does NOT distribute it cross-machine by itself (that rides the Comb worker once approved).
guidance.chaining: meta:define-datatype → datatypes:publish { id } → (operator moderates) → globally visible.

tools.name: datatypes:summary
tools.description: Workspace observability over the datatype registry (P-011): active datatypes counted by TIER (generic-kind / first-class / projection) and by global REVIEW-STATUS (none / pending / approved / rejected), plus how many are published. Read-only — the at-a-glance "what datatypes does this workspace have".

guidance.when: For a dashboard / status read of a workspace's datatype surface and its local→shared graduation.
guidance.notWhen: To list the datatypes themselves (datatypes:list) or fetch one (datatypes:get).
guidance.chaining: datatypes:summary (overview) → datatypes:list (the rows) → datatypes:get (one definition).

tools.name: db:check_drift
tools.description: Report DB migration drift — sql/*.sql files not yet applied (per harness_shared.schema_migrations). Detection only. `missing` = added since the last operator boot; restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or use db:migrate. `extra` = applied but file gone (investigate).

guidance.when: After adding a migration, or when a runtime "missing column/relation" error suggests the live DB lags the sql/ dir.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration — that is the boot auto-apply (restart) or db:migrate for a one-off.
guidance.chaining: missing non-empty → restart the operator (or db:migrate the file under exclusive(db-schema)). EI-6955: the returned `sql_dir` is the RELEASE checkout's sql directory, NOT your staging tree — a migration you JUST added in staging is invisible here (not 'missing') until it reaches release. A clean/in-sync result does not mean your new staging migration needs no action; apply it directly via db:migrate { file: <absolute staging-tree path> } regardless of what this tool reports.

tools.name: db:migrate
tools.description: Apply a SQL migration file, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(db-schema) and drains schema-dependent work (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before running psql -f <file>, then releases. The real apply also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE=1. Prefer this over a raw psql -f.

guidance.when: Applying a migration / destructive DDL that could disrupt in-flight queries. Dry-run to see holders; confirm to drain + apply.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only SQL needs no lock. Never apply migrations casually on a shared box.
guidance.chaining: db:migrate { file } (dry) → review → db:migrate { file, confirm: true }. EI-6955: `file` is an arbitrary absolute path — pass it a migration you JUST wrote in the STAGING tree (don't wait for db:check_drift, whose sql_dir is the release checkout and won't see it). On a dev box the real apply is normally WITHHELD (PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DB_MIGRATE is host-only), but confirm:true still hands you the exact psql + schema_migrations INSERT command to run by hand — use that instead of hand-deriving it from CLAUDE.md's escape hatch.

tools.name: db:migrate-policy
tools.description: Read or set the deploy-migration connection policy: lockTimeoutMs (the DDL lock_timeout the deploy migrator uses — default 15000, the value behind two deploy outages) and statementTimeoutMs (optional; null to unset). set is audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness; migrate.ts reads it fail-safe (defaults on any read error).

guidance.when: Before a deploy whose migration legitimately needs longer to acquire its lock — raise lockTimeoutMs for that window — or to add a statement_timeout, without editing migrate.ts and redeploying through the path you are tuning.
guidance.notWhen: For the BOOT-time migration lock_timeout (it runs before PG config is readable — stays an env/code default per the plan keep-hardcoded list). To see all live overrides, config:list-overrides.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it to the 15000 default.

tools.name: db:next-migration
tools.description: Atomically reserve the next migration number for a libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql/<NNN>-*.sql file. Hands out GREATEST(max-on-disk across the serving + canonical staging trees, max-reserved, max-applied)+1 under a pg advisory lock so two agents racing `ls | tail` never collide. Returns the number + a suggested filename/path; write the file there and it auto-applies on the next operator restart (A1 boot-apply).

guidance.when: BEFORE creating a new SQL migration file — reserve the number first instead of `ls | tail`, so a concurrent agent cannot pick the same NNN.
guidance.notWhen: Applying a migration (that is the boot auto-apply / db:migrate) or checking drift (db:check_drift).
guidance.chaining: db:next-migration { name } → write the returned path → restart the operator (boot auto-applies) or db:migrate.

tools.name: db:txn-timeouts
tools.description: Read/set/reset runtime PG timeouts. (1) per-workspace inWorkspaceTxn lockTimeoutMs / statementTimeoutMs over the baked 5s/5s defaults — mid-incident raise lockTimeoutMs to ride out same-workspace contention or statementTimeoutMs to let a slow mutation finish. (2) adminPoolStatementTimeoutMs (WI-832) — a DEFAULT statement_timeout for NEW org pool connections that bounds the whole interactive admin-pool write class at the source; 0 = OFF (today's behavior). Empty override / kill-switch off (papercusp-txn-timeouts-config) = byte-identical (5s/5s + no pool default). set/reset audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: State-mutating tools are failing with workspace_contended (PG lock_timeout 55P03 / statement_timeout 57014) under same-workspace contention, and you need to widen the window for the incident — raise lockTimeoutMs and/or statementTimeoutMs. get to inspect the effective timeouts + override.
guidance.notWhen: Not for the DEPLOY-migration lock_timeout (db:migrate-policy), nor for the BOOT migration timeout (env/code). This only sizes the per-workspace inWorkspaceTxn lock_timeout/statement_timeout.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active txn-timeouts override; config:reset-overrides reverts it. The kill-switch papercusp-txn-timeouts-config (default ON) forces the baked 5s/5s defaults when OFF.

tools.name: decision_ledger:list
tools.description: The Mug's decision ledger newest-first: governed actions (layer=action — what ran, with posture auto/gated/rejected) and the Mug's per-item dispositions (layer=disposition — act/defer/reject/route-to-research/no-op + why). Filter by layer/category/posture/disposition/time. Each row carries the autonomy axes (category, risk_tier, reversibility, authority) + provenance links. Read-only.

guidance.when: Auditing what the Mug has decided / what the fleet has done: 'what auto-decisions happened?', 'show the gated actions in spend-budget', 'what did it defer?'. Pair with autonomy:policy_get to see why a category gates.
guidance.notWhen: A roll-up of counts by posture/category — decision_ledger:summary. Prompt/rule mutations specifically — change_ledger:list. The live policy ceilings — autonomy:policy_get.
guidance.chaining: decision_ledger:summary (the shape) → decision_ledger:list { layer, category, posture } for the rows → a row.links (runId/spawnId/itemRef) to drill to the transcript / item.

tools.name: decision_ledger:summary
tools.description: Roll-up of the Mug decision ledger: total + counts by layer (action/disposition), posture (auto/proposed/gated/rejected), category, and disposition verb, over a time window. Optionally include harness-scoped completion integrity stats so progress reads can separate genuine completions from dedup churn. The cheap shape-read before decision_ledger:list. Read-only.

guidance.when: Getting oriented: 'how much is the Mug auto-deciding vs gating?', 'which categories see the most gated actions?', 'what's the disposition mix this week?'. Then decision_ledger:list for the rows.
guidance.notWhen: You want the actual rows — decision_ledger:list. Live ceilings — autonomy:policy_get.
guidance.chaining: decision_ledger:summary → decision_ledger:list { the posture/category that stands out }.

tools.name: deploy:await
tools.description: Sleep until a deploy lands (a staging sha reaches the live GREEN :3070 operator) instead of polling dev:pipeline_position. Arms awaits on BOTH release:deployed (success) and release:deploy-failed (failure) so you wake either way. Pass sha to target a specific commit; omit to wake on the next deploy of any sha. Then END YOUR TURN.

guidance.when: You left an edit in the tree and need it LIVE on :3070 before your next step — instead of re-polling dev:pipeline_position, arm this and end your turn.
guidance.notWhen: Just checking where a change sits (not blocked on it) — that is dev:pipeline_position, one read. Forcing a deploy — release:deploy / the deploy-cli.
guidance.chaining: deploy:await { sha } → end turn → on wake, payload.sha confirms which deploy landed; resume the work that needed it live.

tools.name: deploy:harness
tools.description: Deploy a harness's execution plane to its configured cloud frame: provision the machine, bootstrap the runtime (own loop + own embedded-pg), join it as a federated peer. The harness must have been created with a non-local `deployment` (e.g. {target:'latitude'}). Set `deployment.desktop` (true | {displays,geometry}) for a GUI-capable frame: one Xvfb display per agent slot, agents get a leased DISPLAY. Returns {ok, frame}.

guidance.when: Moving a cloud-configured harness onto a real frame so its agents run remotely (distinct IP, own Claude sub) while state federates to the local view.
guidance.notWhen: A local harness (no cloud deployment). Tearing one down — deploy:teardown. Checking status — deploy:status.
guidance.chaining: harness:create { …, deployment:{target:"latitude", desktop:true, …} } → deploy:harness { slug } → deploy:status / deploy:teardown.

tools.name: deploy:pot
tools.description: Deploy a pot (grouping of harnesses) to a Swarm (cloud fleet): place the Mug (local|dedicated|colocated) and deploy each member harness's execution to a frame. Per-member failures are reported, not fatal. Returns {ok, result}.

guidance.when: Running a whole group of harnesses in the cloud — full-auto laptop-optional, or just to scale out execution across frames.
guidance.notWhen: A single harness — deploy:harness. Tearing one down — deploy:teardown_pot.
guidance.chaining: deploy:pot { potId, members, swarm } → deploy:teardown_pot when done.

tools.name: deploy:status
tools.description: Report a harness's deployment: its `deployment` config + the live frame handle (id/host/region) if deployed. Returns {ok, deployment, frame|null}.

guidance.when: Checking where a harness runs (local vs which cloud frame) and the frame's reachable host.

tools.name: deploy:teardown
tools.description: Tear down a harness's cloud frame — DESTROY (not stop) to end billing. No-op if nothing is deployed. Returns {ok, destroyed}.

guidance.when: Done with a cloud harness (or to stop its billing). Teardown destroys the machine so it stops costing money.
guidance.notWhen: Pausing temporarily — there is no stop; destroy + redeploy is the model (frames are cattle).

tools.name: deploy:teardown_pot
tools.description: Tear down a pot — DESTROY every member execution frame + the Mug control frame (ends all billing). Pass the same potId + members + queen placement used to deploy. Returns {ok, destroyed, failed}.

guidance.when: Done with a deployed pot (or to stop all its billing). Frames are cattle — destroy + redeploy is the model.

tools.name: deploys:vintage
tools.description: Lists every runtime that has self-reported its build identity (bg-host, staging-api, dev-api, desktop sidecars, watchdogs, gateway, …) with commit-lag vs origin/staging HEAD per unit. Answers "is the fix actually RUNNING there" without manual ssh + log-tailing.

guidance.when: Before trusting that a landed fix is live on a specific runtime/host — a Mac/Windows desktop bundle, the tower bg-host, a watchdog, the inference gateway, or any service that calls reportRuntimeVintageOnBoot at boot.
guidance.notWhen: For the git-sync → green-checkpoint → :3070 pipeline of a single commit, use dev:pipeline_position instead — this tool is about WHICH RUNNING PROCESSES carry which build, not about one commit's pipeline position.

tools.name: dev:activity
tools.description: Most-recent tool invocations across selected workspaces (live activity feed).

guidance.when: Diagnostic feed of recent workspace activity — for dashboards and debugging. Lower-detail than `audit:list`.
guidance.notWhen: For agent action audit, use `audit:list`. dev:activity is for the /dev panel, not for analysis.

tools.name: dev:audit
tools.description: Cross-workspace audit_log feed (last N hours).

guidance.when: Dev-panel audit view — filtered + paginated for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For analysis or LLM consumption, use `audit:list` directly. dev:audit is a UI-shaped projection.

tools.name: dev:build_status
tools.description: Local-host build mtime + bin/prod log tail + dev/prod server reachability.

guidance.when: Read recent build status from the dev panel — pass/fail per harness.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE harness's smoke tests, use harness-specific tools. dev:build_status is the cross-harness dev panel feed.

tools.name: dev:claude_session
tools.description: Find / search / read local Claude Code chat transcripts — the Claude-Code analogue of dev:omp_session. Scans BOTH ~/.claude/projects AND the per-session isolation dirs ~/.papercusp/session-claude/<owner>/projects, so psu/su CONSOLE sessions are found too. op=list (sessions by cwd + recency, the reliable read), op=search (RAW substring grep — lossy; for ranked cross-client content search prefer sessions:search), op=read (one session as a compact bounded turn list). Pass filePath or sessionId to read.

guidance.when: op=list by cwd to pin "the operator-vite session from ~06-29"; op=read to see where a session left off. For CONTENT search prefer sessions:search (indexed, ranked, cross-client, returns surrounding turns) — op=search here is a raw-file substring grep, for the un-indexed pre-window tail or when the session index is off.
guidance.notWhen: Content search → sessions:search / search:* (the indexed episodic corpus), not op=search. For PRODUCTION agent runs the orchestrator owns sessions (dev:sessions / dev:session_detail). For OMP CLI sessions use omp:sessions. To reconstruct "where they left off" the transcript is a LOSSY secondary — prefer the durable artifacts (git per-file history + the work-item/plan ledger), which are canonical.
guidance.chaining: dev:claude_session { op:"list", cwd } → { op:"read", sessionId }. Content search → sessions:search { query } (indexed), not op:"search".

tools.name: dev:code_run_adoption
tools.description: code:run adoption: of spawns that COULD batch (same-tool burst / fan-out), how many folded the flow into one code:run — per role/day, a fleet rollup, and the graded tool-utilization rating. Last N days.

guidance.when: Grading pot-coordination-health tool-utilization, or checking whether the code:run nudges / recipes-at-orient are moving adoption. Returns the fleet rate + a ready rating + the per-role/day breakdown.
guidance.notWhen: Raw per-tool call counts (dev:telemetry); which tools co-occur in a spawn (dev:tool_cooccurrence).

tools.name: dev:coord_categorize
tools.description: Categorize the coord_event_log `messages` corpus into lifecycle buckets (completion/claim/intent/restart/ack/finding) vs the irreducible contextual residual. The instrument for coord-lifecycle-automation D-006: re-run after each phase; contextualPct + automatedPct are the headline metrics.

guidance.when: Measure coord-lifecycle automation progress — how much free-text coord is predictable lifecycle vs genuinely contextual.
guidance.notWhen: To read your inbox use coord:inbox; this is an aggregate measurement over the whole corpus, not a feed.

tools.name: dev:dogfood_substrate_status
tools.description: Hyperbee substrate diagnostic: booted harnesses, per-row health verdict, workspace summary. The substrate is always active (no flag gate). Mirrors /api/admin/dogfood-substrate-health.

guidance.when: Investigating substrate boot state, claim error rates, or workspace-level dogfood health. The substrate always boots, so run this any time after the operator has started.
guidance.notWhen: For per-harness Insights or feature-level data, use the harness:* tools. This is the dogfood substrate layer specifically.
guidance.chaining: Pair with reading the agent-insights/substrate-flag-flip-runbook page for what to do if verdicts come back degraded/unhealthy.

tools.name: dev:event_emitter
tools.description: Replay-buffer probe — emits N tick events with serial ids. Dev-only.

tools.name: dev:harnesses
tools.description: List harnesses across selected workspaces with health verdict for each.

guidance.when: Dev-panel harness enumeration with diagnostic columns (active connections, recent errors).
guidance.notWhen: For ordinary list, use `harness:list`. dev:harnesses is the diagnostic projection.

tools.name: dev:ipc_echo
tools.description: IPC transport verification — echoes the message back as a small typed event stream.

tools.name: dev:limit_failure_rate
tools.description: Tool-arg limit-rejection failure rate: too-long-string validation failures by tool over the last N days (measuring-code-run-adoption.mdx metric #1) — a fleet total, per-tool breakdown, and a graded rating.

guidance.when: Checking whether a string/advisory-field cap fix landed (should trend toward 0), or which tool is currently rejecting long args most often.
guidance.notWhen: Raw per-tool call counts (dev:telemetry); code:run adoption (dev:code_run_adoption).

tools.name: dev:omp_session
tools.description: Find and read the omp session JSONL file for a spawn_id, by cwd + start-time match against ~/.omp/agent/sessions/.

guidance.when: Inspect an OMP CLI session's state — useful when debugging long-running CLI flows.
guidance.notWhen: For PRODUCTION agent runs, the orchestrator owns sessions. dev:omp_session is the CLI-tool inspector.

tools.name: dev:orient_dedup_rate
tools.description: coord:orient redundant-recall rate: of spawns that called coord:orient, how many ALSO re-called a tool orient already subsumed (plan-events/memory:search/inbox/declare-intent) — a fleet rollup + graded rating.

guidance.when: Checking whether the orient-dedup guidance is landing (pctRedundant should trend down from the ~100% baseline).
guidance.notWhen: Raw per-tool call counts (dev:telemetry); which tools co-occur in a spawn (dev:tool_cooccurrence).

tools.name: dev:pg_active_queries
tools.description: List current pg_stat_activity rows (pid, state, query, duration) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: list currently-running PG queries (pg_stat_activity). Use when investigating slow / hung queries.
guidance.notWhen: For routine diagnostics, the /dev/pg panel is enough. Use this tool when scripting an investigation.

tools.name: dev:pg_health
tools.description: PostgreSQL version + connection counts (total/active/idle) for the operator database.

guidance.when: Diagnostic snapshot of PG health — connections, longest query, lock count. For the /dev/pg dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For application-level health, use `harness:health`. pg_health is the database layer.

tools.name: dev:pg_query
tools.description: Run a read-only SELECT / WITH…SELECT against the operator Postgres (the canonical store behind plans, work-items, issues, observations, tool_invocations, scorecards, recipes, …). Read-only enforced; statement_timeout 5s; rows capped.

guidance.when: A filtered / aggregate / recency read of PG-CANONICAL state. Plans, work-items, issues, observations (engineer_issues), tool_invocations, scorecards are PG tables — the `*:list` tools and `docs/plans/*.md` files are PROJECTIONS. Query PG directly instead of fetching a whole `*:list` and post-filtering (which returns a huge result that spills to a file → don't then jq the projection). Example — recent plans this workspace: `SELECT plan_slug,status,created FROM harness_shared.harness_plans WHERE created >= '2026-06-17' AND workspace_id = '<ws>' ORDER BY created DESC LIMIT 50`. Aggregates (counts/group-by) are first-class here and awkward to jq.
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE state — use the documented write verbs (plans:*, work_items:*, issues:* — they emit audit + sync invalidation). Writes are rejected here anyway (read-only transaction). For code-graph queries use `gitnexus:query`; for prose full-text use `search:fulltext` / `search:semantic`.
guidance.chaining: Alias any duplicate output column names (the result is wrapped in a subquery for the row cap, and PG rejects duplicate subquery columns). Pass `maxRows` to widen the cap up to 2000; if `truncated` is true, add a tighter WHERE / LIMIT rather than raising the cap blindly.

tools.name: dev:pg_table_sizes
tools.description: List tables in a pg schema with total size, index size, and estimated row count. Defaults to harness_shared.

guidance.when: Diagnostic: per-table sizes + row counts. Use when investigating storage growth.
guidance.notWhen: For application data analysis, query the relevant tools directly. pg_table_sizes is an ops view.

tools.name: dev:pipeline_position
tools.description: Read-only: where a change sits along the git-sync → green-checkpoint → release pipeline. Pass a repo-relative `path` (its latest commit) OR a `sha`; returns committed/on-staging/in-main/deployed + the green-gate stall context + a one-line summary. Answers "did my edit land + is it live on :3070?" without forensic git/PG/curl.

guidance.when: After leaving an edit in the tree (git-sync owns commit/push), to confirm it reached origin/staging, passed the green gate into main, and deployed to the live :3070 operator — or to see WHY it is stuck (gate red/stalled).
guidance.notWhen: To PAUSE sync (use locks:acquire_resource on git-sync:<slug>). For the whole-pipeline dashboard use the /admin Git tab; this is the targeted per-path/sha probe.
guidance.chaining: Edit a file → (git-sync commits within minutes) → dev:pipeline_position{path} to confirm it reached staging/main/:3070.

tools.name: dev:processes
tools.description: Inventory of agent-related processes on this host (run.sh, omp, claude, paperclip, pty, next) with cmdline, cwd, and inferred harness/workspace.

guidance.when: List tracked processes (delegates, plugin subprocesses, orchestrator children) for the /dev panel.
guidance.notWhen: For ACTIVE spawns, use `orchestrator.list_active`. For delegates, use `delegates:list`. dev:processes is the unified diagnostic view.

tools.name: dev:rate_governor_status
tools.description: Snapshot the fleet rate-limit layer now: live config (maxSimultaneousAgents + AIMD floor), fleet cap vs in-flight vs AIMD-effective concurrency, per (provider, model-class) governor buckets (paused/until, in-flight vs maxConcurrent, RPM/ITPM/OTPM headroom), recent usage telemetry (token throughput, $spend, usage% where a provider ceiling is known), and the opusBudget pacing state (aggregate 5h opus utilization + zone + which criticality classes are shedding opus→sonnet to stay under the ceiling, B-GW-4). Buckets are empty until a governed agent turn has run. Use to see whether the fleet/gym is currently rate-limit-paced, paused, AIMD-throttled, or opus-budget-shedding.

guidance.when: Diagnose whether agent spawns / stateless LLM calls are being paced or paused by the rate-limit governor (e.g. "why are runs slow / stalled?"), or read the fleet cap / effective concurrency / usage% the top-bar shows.
guidance.notWhen: Service up/down — dev:service_health. Migration drift — db:check_drift. EDITING the cap — operator:rate_limit_config.

tools.name: dev:resolve_owner
tools.description: Resolve a coordination owner id (su-…/s-…/pus-…) to its session(s): the native resume session_id (claude/codex), omp_thread_id, spawn/run ids, plan, cwd, and per-turn telemetry activity. The owner↔session link the dev:sessions list lacks.

guidance.when: You have an agent OWNER id (from coord:presence, a plan-event's `from`, or coord:whoami) and need the session it ran in — e.g. the id to pass to `claude --resume`.
guidance.notWhen: You already have a spawn_id — use `dev:session_detail`. For the session LIST, use `dev:sessions`.

tools.name: dev:restart
tools.description: Restart the operator dev server, coordinated. DRY RUN unless confirm:true. With confirm, acquires exclusive(dev-server) and drains current users (wait:{max_drain_sec}) before restarting, then releases (broadcasts "back up"). The real restart also requires PAPERCUSP_ALLOW_DEV_RESTART=1 on the host. Prefer this over a raw systemctl restart.

guidance.when: You need to restart the dev server (e.g. to pick up a lib/** edit). Run dry first to see who is using it; then confirm to drain + restart.
guidance.notWhen: Just probing the server — that needs no restart. Never restart casually on a shared box; it disrupts every agent using the app.
guidance.chaining: dev:restart (dry) → review holders → dev:restart { confirm: true, max_drain_sec } → connection drops as it restarts.

tools.name: dev:service_health
tools.description: Probe the dev services now (:3070 operator, :3055 vite, :3350 scout, the Tauri desktop via its dev-bridge eval + IPC socket + recent error toasts, AND the papercup-bg-host DBOS ticker via routine fire-freshness) — up/down + status + latency, PLUS a `supervision` block per critical-process-supervisor entry (layer/autoRestart/consecutiveProbeFailures/restartsLast10m/flapState) sourced from the failed-unit reconciler. The "bg-host-ticker" entry is a SEPARATE service from :3070: when it reads down, git-sync + every scheduled routine are FROZEN even though :3070 is up — do NOT dev:restart the operator for that, the bg-host needs reviving. The desktop entry reports present:false when no desktop is running. Use before relying on a service or after a "connection refused".

guidance.when: Confirm which dev services are up before testing against one; diagnose a "connection refused" / stale-server symptom; OR diagnose a git-sync / routine-engine stall — the "bg-host-ticker" entry tells you whether the SEPARATE bg-host routine engine is frozen (so you do not misattribute it to :3070).
guidance.notWhen: File/lock contention — that is locks:queue. Migration drift — db:check_drift.

tools.name: dev:session_detail
tools.description: Drilldown for one spawn_id: agent metadata, tool invocations timeline, child spawns, related chats.

guidance.when: Read full detail of one /dev session — request history, env, traces.
guidance.notWhen: For the SESSION LIST, use `dev:sessions` first.

tools.name: dev:sessions
tools.description: Cross-workspace agent sessions, one row per spawn_id with started/ended/tool_count/error_count/duration totals.

guidance.when: List recent /dev panel sessions — used by the dev UI to populate session pickers.
guidance.notWhen: For application AGENT chat sessions, use `agent_chats:list`. dev:sessions is the panel's own concept.

tools.name: dev:state_counter
tools.description: Demo state-shaped tool: ticks a counter and publishes each tick via ctx.publishState. Reconnect-resilient by construction.

tools.name: dev:telemetry
tools.description: Per-tool invocation rollup (count, error rate, p50/p95) across selected workspaces over the last N hours.

guidance.when: Read recent telemetry datapoints (errors, slow requests). For the /dev/telemetry dashboard.
guidance.notWhen: For per-agent audit, use `audit:list`. telemetry is observability-shaped, not action-shaped.

tools.name: dev:tool_cooccurrence
tools.description: Pairwise tool co-occurrence (support / confidence / lift) grouped by spawn_id over MCP tool_invocations — which tools get invoked together in one agent turn. The deterministic candidate-generator for wrapper/bundle tools.

guidance.when: Find which agent tools are invoked TOGETHER in the same turn (spawn), ranked by support / confidence / lift — to spot bundle/wrapper candidates and feed code-recipes candidate generation. Analytical / offline; MCP-transport calls only.
guidance.notWhen: For per-tool counts or latency use `dev:telemetry`; for a forensic per-agent timeline use `audit:list`. A high lift on tiny support is spurious — keep a support floor (minSupport), and remember lift != determinism: this NOMINATES pairs, a human/gate judges whether the steps are mechanical before wrapping.
guidance.chaining: dev:tool_cooccurrence (find bonded pairs) → judge determinism → wrap as a composite (e.g. extend coord:orient) or feed code-recipes promotion.

tools.name: dev:why
tools.description: "Why is nothing shipping?" in one read: walks green-checkpoint gate health -> release-gate deploy position -> account-pool rate-limit status top-down, and returns one causal sentence per stage plus a ROOT CAUSE line naming the current blocking leaf (a red test file, a stuck promotion, a saturated pool). Deterministic — no LLM. Read-only.

guidance.when: The owner or an agent asks "why is nothing shipping / deploying" or a deploy has been frozen/stalled for a while and you need the causal chain in one call instead of manually cross-referencing dev:pipeline_position, testing:flakiness, and accounts:status.
guidance.notWhen: To check ONE specific path/sha's position, use dev:pipeline_position. To rank flaky files over a longer window, use testing:flakiness. This is the top-down "what is the root blocker right now" read.

tools.name: dev:worker_chunk_loop_metrics
tools.description: Monitoring metrics for the operator-hosted worker:chunk-loop rollout (P-020), all six gate metrics: feature completion RATE, outcome DISTRIBUTION (completed/escalated/planning_failed/aborted), file-lock CONTENTION rate, replan FREQUENCY across all runs, crash-RESUME success rate, and per-chunk DURABILITY — split by execution PATH (subprocess vs the operator-hosted op) — plus the op−subprocess completion-rate delta. Reads harness_shared.worker_chunk_loop_outcomes for the active workspace over a lookback window.
