tools.description: Backfill a harness's existing FS docs into the typed drift-tracked model: anchor docs that declare/imply a subject as manual records (baselined to HEAD). One-time per harness; idempotent.

guidance.when: After this harness has existing docs/*.md that predate the typed model, to make the ones with a declared/inferable subject drift-tracked.
guidance.notWhen: Record-less docs already show as "not drift-tracked" via the merged read — ingest is only needed to anchor docs that declare a subject. No need to run repeatedly.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:ingest → harness_docs:list (review which anchored) → harness_docs:anchor (fix any wrong/missing anchors).

tools.name: harness_docs:list
tools.description: List a harness's merged docs (generated · manual · augmented) with source badges + drift status (fresh/stale/review/untracked), and the active doc's body + augmented overlay. Supersedes the FS-only project-docs read.

guidance.when: You want a harness's project docs WITH provenance + freshness — which are generated vs human, which are stale, which are not drift-tracked.
guidance.notWhen: For Papercusp framework docs use docs:get/outline. For raw markdown without metadata the old project-docs endpoint still exists but is superseded.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:regenerate (stale generated) / harness_docs:verify (stale manual) / harness_docs:set_overlay (add human nuance).

tools.name: harness_docs:record
tools.description: Record one OR many generated docs' provenance + drift anchor (subject_ref) and stamp each generated-from the harness repo's current HEAD. Single: { docId, documents? }. Many: items:[{ docId, documents?, title?, harness? }]. Call immediately after writing the file(s), passing what you read. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, source?, status?, generatedFromSha?, subjectRef?, anchorPaths? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You (the documenter) just wrote or refreshed generated doc file(s) (docs/features/F-<id>.md, a guide). Call once per doc with the feature + the exact files/symbols you read; record several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a human-authored manual doc, use harness_docs:anchor instead (it sets a verify baseline, not a generated baseline). Do not call for docs you only read.
guidance.chaining: Write the .md file(s) → harness_docs:record { docId, documents } (or items:[…]). The freshness sweep then tracks them against future commits.

tools.name: harness_docs:regenerate
tools.description: Request a documenter regeneration of one OR many stale generated/augmented docs (preserving any human overlay). Single: { docId }. Many same harness: { docIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ docId, harness? }]. Each enqueues; the doc refreshes when the documenter re-records it. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, enqueued? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A generated doc is stale (its subject code changed) and you want it refreshed. Regenerate several at once via docIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a manual doc use harness_docs:verify. To preserve human nuance across the regen, add it via harness_docs:set_overlay first.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find stale generated) → harness_docs:regenerate { docIds:[…] }.

tools.name: harness_docs:retire
tools.description: Remove a stale harness_docs tracking row (a doc whose file was moved/deleted, e.g. into docs/archive/) so the freshness sweep stops perpetually flagging it as review/bodyMissing. Only deletes the PG tracking record, never a file. Single: { docId }. Many: items:[{ docId, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, existed? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A harness_docs:list row shows status review/bodyMissing (or the freshness sweep gave up healing it) because its file was moved/deleted — confirm the file is genuinely gone (or relocated with a fresh tracked twin) before retiring.
guidance.notWhen: The doc's file still exists and is just drifted/stale — use harness_docs:regenerate (generated) or edit + harness_docs:anchor (manual) instead of retiring a live doc's record.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (spot bodyMissing/review debris) → confirm the file is gone → harness_docs:retire { docId } (or items:[…]).

tools.name: harness_docs:set_overlay
tools.description: Attach a human "augmented" overlay to one OR many docs — nuance that rides on top of the generated body and survives regeneration; empty string clears it. Single: { docId, overlay }. Many: items:[{ docId, overlay, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, source?, hasOverlay? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A generated doc is accurate but missing the human "why"/caveats you want preserved across regenerations. Add it as an overlay rather than hand-editing the generated body (which a regen would lose). Set several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: To change the generated body itself, fix the code/feature and regenerate. For a fully human doc, author it as a manual doc.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list → harness_docs:set_overlay { overlay } (or items:[…]).

tools.name: harness_docs:verify
tools.description: Re-verify one OR many manual docs: stamp the drift baseline to the current HEAD and mark fresh. Single: { docId }. Many same harness: { docIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ docId, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, docId, verifiedSha? | error }], counts } — correlate by docId not position; one failure never fails the rest. Use after reviewing a doc the freshness sweep flagged for re-verify.

guidance.when: A manual doc was flagged for re-verify (its subject code changed) and you confirmed it's still accurate — or you just edited it to match. Verify several at once via docIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: For a generated doc use harness_docs:regenerate. To set the anchor in the first place use harness_docs:anchor.
guidance.chaining: harness_docs:list (find review docs) → read → harness_docs:verify { docIds:[…] }.

tools.name: hooks:known
tools.description: Static well-known hook-event allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered hooks extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of supported hook event names — use to validate an event string before firing or registering for it.
guidance.notWhen: For PENDING events queued up, use `pending_events:list`. For firing an event, use `plugins:fire_event`.

tools.name: improvements:capture
tools.description: Capture a papercusp improvement you discovered (a friction, a missing affordance, a bug in the tooling) as a durable, claimable, `papercusp-improvement`-tagged work-unit. kind=bug → auto-implement-eligible later; change|feature → human-reviewed. Search-first: declines an obvious duplicate (link to it instead) unless force. Pass `paths` when you know the files involved — it feeds the protected-path safety gate. Pass lane:"observation" for a turn-end-reflection PRE-IDEA — it files into a separate lane that NEVER enters the work queue (Scout-digest + the Observations pane only).

guidance.when: You hit a papercusp DX / tooling / code friction worth fixing but out of your current scope. File it here so it lands in the triage backlog instead of being lost. Use kind=bug for something broken, kind=change for a desired improvement, kind=feature for net-new (the last two stay human-gated). Include `paths` (repo-relative files involved) when known — the auto-implement risk gate reads them.
guidance.notWhen: A problem in a MANAGED harness/project (not papercusp itself) — that is work_items:create with that harness scope. Something needing real design — write a plan (plans:new) and capture with kind=feature linking it. A passing question — coord:ask.
guidance.chaining: improvements:capture { kind, title, paths? } → (later) improvements:digest triages it → an agent claims + fixes it self/inline, or the auto-implement loop picks up the bugs and improvements:resolve closes them.

tools.name: improvements:digest
tools.description: Triage the captured papercusp-improvement backlog: scores + dedups every improvement work-unit and splits it into the auto-eligible lane (kind=bug, no protected surface) vs the human-review queue. Read-only — surfaces the queue, implements nothing. (P-010) Supports per-Hive scope filtering.

guidance.when: To review the papercusp self-improvement backlog — what is captured, what is auto-eligible vs needs a human, and which items look like duplicates to merge. The human-facing triage view. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug to filter to a specific Pot's ideas.
guidance.notWhen: You want one improvement in full — work_items:get { id }. You want to file one — improvements:capture. You want to browse another area — topics:feed { topic }.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → work_items:get / work_items:claim on a queued item → fix it self/inline (or improvements:capture to add more).

tools.name: improvements:keyless-digest
tools.description: Triage surface for KEYLESS improvement items (no payload.watchdogKey — manual / non-watchdog EIs) — the un-managed backlog that never dedups, ages, or auto-closes. Returns the keyed-vs-keyless headline split, age-band rollup (fresh < 7d · aging 7–30d · stale ≥ 30d), and the review queue (keyless EIs ≥ 7d, oldest-first) with a per-item disposition (claim-or-close / follow-up-owner). Read-only — closes nothing; surfaces the pile so a human/Queen can drain it (P-014).

guidance.when: To see and triage the un-managed backlog — the keyless EIs that the watchdog lifecycle (dedup/aging/auto-close) cannot touch because they carry no watchdogKey. Use it as the periodic keyless human-review digest: drain the stale-review queue (claim, close if obsolete, or convert a recurring one to a keyed form).
guidance.notWhen: You want watchdog/auto-implement health — improvements:watchdog-status. You want the full captured (keyed) backlog triage — improvements:digest. You want one item — work_items:get.
guidance.chaining: improvements:keyless-digest → for each review item: work_items:claim (take it), work_items:set_state (obsolete), or re-file via improvements:capture with a stable key if it is a recurring signal. improvements:watchdog-status surfaces the same keyless headline split.

tools.name: improvements:learning_loops
tools.description: Inspect the self-learning loop routines: per workspace-singleton learning loop (calibration, scout, graduation, iq-battery, …) its routine state — firing / stale (active but not firing) / dark-by-design (frontier, unarmed) / should-be-on-but-dark (an always-on loop gone dark) / absent — plus the @singleton↔legacy double-state. Read-only — the dark-loop visibility surface so a built-but-never-armed loop does not rot unseen.

guidance.when: To answer "which learning loops are dark / wedged / never armed?" — the standing health of the self-learning machinery (calibration sweep, blender, graduation, gym, iq-battery, …). Catches the recurring class: a loop seeded inactive behind a default-OFF flag that nobody armed, an always-on loop that wedged (stopped firing), or a @singleton↔legacy migration collision.
guidance.notWhen: For the watchdog tick health + auto-implement dispatch ledger use improvements:watchdog-status. For the captured backlog use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: improvements:learning_loops → (a dark frontier loop) the per-lane arming runbook; (a should-be-on-but-dark / stale loop) investigate the routine then improvements:capture.

tools.name: improvements:resolve
tools.description: Close the loop on a captured papercusp improvement you worked: outcome `fixed` (requires testsRun — the verification evidence) marks it resolved so it leaves the queue; `could-not-fix` releases it for a retry (exhausted retries route to a human); `needs-human` routes it to the human queue permanently.

guidance.when: You finished working a dispatched/claimed improvement (usually as the implement worker). Fixed + tests green → outcome fixed with the evidence. Could not make it work → could-not-fix with what you tried. The fix would touch a protected surface (operator-core safety / deploy machinery / a migration) or needs judgment → needs-human.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to comment progress — work_items:comment. You are closing a non-improvement issue — work_items:set_state. The item was never captured (no EI/WI id) — improvements:capture it first if it is worth tracking.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest → (dispatch/claim) → implement + test → improvements:resolve { id, outcome, summary, testsRun }.

tools.name: improvements:set-auto-policy
tools.description: Read or set the auto-implement risk policy: autoKinds (the bug→change→feature graduation dial), maxPerRun / maxAttempts (dispatch ceilings), and TIGHTEN-ONLY protected-path/keyword additions (the baked TCB floor is unioned + never removable — no remove op by design, D-002). Inert until the IMPROVEMENT_AUTO_IMPLEMENT flag is armed; audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Graduate the auto-implement lane (widen autoKinds as trust is earned), tune the dispatch rate (maxPerRun/maxAttempts), or ADD a path/keyword to the never-auto protected set — live, no redeploy.
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a baked protection (impossible by design — D-002 tighten-only). To arm auto-implement itself, flip FLAGS.IMPROVEMENT_AUTO_IMPLEMENT via /admin/features (this only configures the policy). To triage the queue, use improvements:digest.
guidance.chaining: improvements:digest shows the auto/human partition under the current policy; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: improvements:set-watchdog-tunables
tools.description: Live-tune the improvement-watchdog's collector bars + per-tick caps (its payload_template tunables) without a deploy. `get` reads the current standing tunables; `set` merges a patch through the control harness (dryRun preview, post-apply verify+auto-revert, audit, one-call revert). Keys are the watchdog PAYLOAD_TUNABLE_KEYS (e.g. transientMinCount, maxPerTick, structuralMinRate).

guidance.when: A watchdog collector is too noisy or too quiet on a running fleet (e.g. raise transientMinCount during a flaky-infra window, or lower a min-count to capture more) and you want to retune it live instead of poking the routine payload by hand or editing code.
guidance.notWhen: To turn the watchdog on/off (flip its routine `active` — autoloop/routine control). To READ what it last captured, use improvements:watchdog-status. This tool tunes the payload layer; the maxPerTick env override still wins at tick time.
guidance.chaining: improvements:watchdog-status to see current capture behavior; set with dryRun:true to preview the proposed-vs-current diff before applying.

tools.name: improvements:triage
tools.description: Queen-turn triage: route each scored idea by the D-005 taxonomy (product→place; code-bug→the policy tier's lane; infra-environment→owner-escalation; process-prompt→gate/gym; needs-design→plans:new). The risk-tier policy is the one safety verdict — triage adds only routing (D-003). Persists the decision on the idea lifecycle. (P-010) Per-Hive scope filtering.

guidance.when: To triage captured ideas: read the digest summary, walk the human queue in RANK order (the P-040 ranker — triage-all carries each item's rank breakdown), classify by the D-005 taxonomy, decide (place/gate/gym/reject), and record the Queen's judgment. (P-010) Pass harnessSlug for one Hive. mode=retriage-all re-routes the whole open backlog after a taxonomy/policy change.
guidance.notWhen: You want to READ ideas — use improvements:digest. You want to CAPTURE — use improvements:capture. You want implementation status — use improvements:resolve.
guidance.chaining: improvements:triage → work_items:create/update for placed ideas, or coord:escalate for human-gate ideas. A rank breakdown showing a 'calibration' contribution → calibration:summary { predictor } to weigh the bettor's claim before deciding.

tools.name: improvements:watchdog-status
tools.description: Inspect the improvement watchdog: the last N tick records (collector health, signals, captured ids, known-open/stale-resolved pre-filter drops, deferred keys, self-escalations) plus a rollup summary AND the auto-implement dispatch ledger (counts by state + recent dispatches). Read-only — the diagnostic surface over harness_shared.watchdog_ticks + improvement_dispatches.

guidance.when: To check whether the improvement watchdog is running and healthy — when it last ticked, which collectors failed, what it captured vs declined vs deferred, and which standing signals the key pre-filter is dropping. The first stop for "why did/didn't the watchdog file X?" — and for the auto-implement lane's dispatch ledger ("did the dispatch fire / is a worker on it / did it die?").
guidance.notWhen: You want the captured backlog itself — improvements:digest. You want one improvement — work_items:get { id }. You want to file one — improvements:capture.
guidance.chaining: improvements:watchdog-status → work_items:get on a captured/self-escalated/dispatched id → improvements:digest for the full backlog triage.

tools.name: inbox:triage
tools.description: Triage one OR many attention items (the operator inbox PASS): downgrade a false positive or resolve it → the auditable "Handled by operator" tier; escalate an under-flagged item or confirm a real one → the Decisions tier. Pass a single `{ itemId, action, note? }` for one or `items:[{ itemId, action, note? }]` for several. Record WHY in `note` (required on downgrade/resolve). The downgrade is always visible + auditable, never a silent vanish. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, itemId, action, triageState, tier | error }], counts } — correlate by itemId, not position; one bad item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Operator inbox PASS — run FIRST each wake over the Decisions tier: re-tier attention items after reading them (downgrade noise, escalate something a worker under-flagged, confirm/resolve a real decision), always recording the why in `note`. Triaging several at once? Pass them all via `items:[{ itemId, action, note? }]`. Leave the inbox clean before sleeping.
guidance.notWhen: Acting on the item itself (resolve an escalation → coord:resolve; mark a plan item done → plans:set-status). Messaging the owning agent → coord:message-agent.

tools.name: instance:boot
tools.description: Boot a new harness from an InstanceSpec, reproducing the captured instance. Reuses harness:create.

guidance.when: Instantiate a NEW harness identical to a captured InstanceSpec (same blueprint + SHA + deployment + genome).
guidance.notWhen: To create a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`. To clone-and-vary in one call, use `instance:clone`.
guidance.chaining: instance:capture → instance:boot.

tools.name: instance:capture
tools.description: Capture an InstanceSpec (blueprintRef + repoSha + deploymentConfig + genome) from a live harness, for reproducible boot/vary.

guidance.when: Capture a reproducible descriptor of a live harness/instance — its blueprint + git SHA + deployment + genome — to boot or vary an identical one. The replacement for the retired snapshot clone path.
guidance.notWhen: For a full state backup (code+data), git + PG already cover it. To create a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`.
guidance.chaining: instance:capture → instance:boot (identical) or instance:clone (with a genome delta).

tools.name: instance:clone
tools.description: Capture a harness → optionally apply a genome delta → boot an identical / same-origin clone.

guidance.when: Clone a live harness into a new identical one, or a same-origin variant (pass a genomeDelta). The reproducible-clone replacement for the retired snapshot fork.
guidance.notWhen: For a fresh harness from scratch, use `harness:create`. To capture a spec without booting, use `instance:capture`.
guidance.chaining: instance:clone = instance:capture → (vary) → instance:boot in one call.

tools.name: intel:artifacts
tools.description:
When to use: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.

When NOT to use: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

guidance.when: You need the Intel-panel-shaped view of recent artifacts — grouped + summarized for UI display.
guidance.notWhen: For loading a specific artifact body, use `artifacts:load`. For listing artifacts a tool produced, use the tool's response. intel:artifacts is the panel feed.

tools.name: intel:spawn_tree
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.

When NOT to use: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

guidance.when: User asks "what triggered this?", "show me the lineage of agent X", or you need the parent-child spawn graph for an Intel-panel-style view.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE running spawns only, use `orchestrator.list_active`. spawn_tree is historical + structural; list_active is the now-snapshot.

tools.name: kettle:declare-wake
tools.description: Declare the Kettle's next wake (REPLACE semantics): a time (`at` ISO / `inSeconds`), the configured cadence (no time given), or nothing (`mode:'none'` — sleep until the owner). Clamped to a wake floor. The Kettle's OWN channel — distinct from the Mug's pot:declare-wake; ALWAYS call this before ending a turn.

guidance.when: You are the Kettle ending a turn — ALWAYS declare your next wake. Use a SHORT inSeconds (60–180) while a drift is unresolved (verify the nudge landed), a LONGER one (600–1800) when the system is calm. Omit the time to use the configured cadence.
guidance.notWhen: To schedule the Mug / pot — that is pot:declare-wake (a different channel you cannot and must not touch). To wake right now — the owner's kettle:start does that.
guidance.chaining: Follows your nudges/observations for the turn; this is the last loop step before your end-of-turn verb.

tools.name: kettle:pause
tools.description: PAUSE the Kettle (the autonomous system-health supervisor): persist overwatch_started=false (disarms the loop + liveness watchdog), clear its pending wake, and optionally send the live Kettle session a graceful stop cue. Resume with kettle:start.

guidance.when: The user clicks Pause Kettle / asks to freeze the system-health supervisor (incident, review, cost control), or the Kettle is misbehaving and must be quieted.
guidance.notWhen: To pause the Mug / pot — pot:pause (distinct loop). To pause one plan — plans:pause. Pausing does not kill a running Kettle turn; it finishes and nothing re-arms.
guidance.chaining: kettle:pause { drain:true } for the harder stop → kettle:start to resume.

tools.name: kettle:start
tools.description: START the Kettle (the autonomous system-health supervisor, a sibling to the Mug): persist overwatch_started=true, set its wake cadence, and wake it now. The loop (B-04) + liveness watchdog (B-09) hold "a wake is always armed" from here until kettle:pause. Gated by the papercusp-overwatch flag — while the flag is OFF the bit/cadence are persisted (pre-armed) but no live wake fires.

guidance.when: The user clicks Start Kettle / asks to boot the system-health supervisor, or you are bringing a paused Kettle back to autonomous operation.
guidance.notWhen: To start the Mug / pot — pot:start (distinct loop). To start one plan — plans:start. The Kettle nudges + observes; it never places work.
guidance.chaining: kettle:pause to suspend. The papercusp-overwatch flag (/admin/features) must be ON for the loop to actually run (B-04 gate).

tools.name: learning:set-scout-budget
tools.description: Read/set/clear the runtime Scout WORKSPACE spend-ceiling override (USD), consulted before the PAPERCUSP_SCOUT_WORKSPACE_CEILING_USD env. Tighten the aggregate scout cap mid-incident or raise it for a planned exploration burst — live, no deploy. set/clear audited + one-call-revertible; empty override ⇒ env/default (byte-identical).

guidance.when: Blender spend across armed pots is summing too high (tighten the workspace ceiling live) or you want to raise it for a planned exploration burst, without a host restart. op:get to read the active override + effective ceiling.
guidance.notWhen: To tune regret-mining replay knobs (minScore/maxSessions/maxReplaysPerTick) use the regret routine payload via routines:set. To set a per-cycle learning SPEND budget use the learning-governor arming surface. This dial is the workspace-wide ceiling only.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active scout-workspace-budget override; config:reset-overrides reverts it to env/default.

tools.name: learning_packs:candidates
tools.description: List learning-pack item CANDIDATEs — cross-hive recurring lessons the recurrence-escalation loop staged for owner review (default: pending only). Each carries provenance: the friction signature, the scopes it recurred across, the recurrence count, and the source improvement-item ids.

guidance.when: The owner asks what fleet lessons await review, or before learning_packs:decide_candidate (the id comes from here).
guidance.notWhen: To read a hive's installed learnings (learning_packs:list / memory:list) or the pack catalog (learning_packs:list).
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:decide_candidate { id, action } to adopt into the fleet-lessons pack or dismiss; after an adopt, hives pick the item up via learning_packs:install/upgrade.

tools.name: learning_packs:decide_candidate
tools.description: Decide one OR many pending learning-pack candidates: adopt (write it into the fleet-lessons pack — version bumps so hives see updateAvailable; optionally edit title/text first) or dismiss (terminal — the signature never re-stages). This is an OWNER decision; candidates are never auto-published. Single: { id, action, note?, title?, text? }. Many same action: { ids:[…], action }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, action, note?, title?, text? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, action?, … | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; one bad candidate never fails the rest.

guidance.when: The owner has reviewed pending candidate(s) (learning_packs:candidates) and says adopt/dismiss — or asks you to apply their edits while adopting. Decide several at once via ids:[…]+action or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: To seed a lesson into a hive pool directly (adoption only updates the PACK; hives adopt via learning_packs:install/upgrade). Unprompted bulk adoption — each candidate is an explicit owner call.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:candidates first (ids + drafts). After adopt: hives with fleet-lessons installed show updateAvailable → learning_packs:upgrade { hive, pack: "fleet-lessons" }; others via learning_packs:install. Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: learning_packs:export
tools.description: Export a hive's shared learnings into the standard pack shape (learning-packs/<packId>/ — manifest + one-learning-per-file) inside a member repo's working tree, ready to commit + publish. Defaults to the hive's ORGANIC learnings only; includePackRows re-exports installed-pack content too (explicit opt-in).

guidance.when: The user wants to share their pot's accumulated learnings — first step of the publish flow.
guidance.notWhen: Installing or browsing packs — learning_packs:list/install.
guidance.chaining: After the files are committed + pushed by the project's normal flow, learning_packs:publish lists the pack on the Comb (it publishes PENDING — operator approval gates public visibility, D-007).

tools.name: learning_packs:install
tools.description: Install a learning pack into an existing hive's shared memory, with the install-time conflict review: incoming learnings are classified clean/duplicate/conflict against the hive's current pool; clashes require explicit per-item resolutions (install · skip · replace · keep-both). Defaults skip clashes — existing content outranks the incoming pack.

guidance.when: Adding a pack to an EXISTING hive (a new hive seeds its pack at creation). Call once to get the review; re-call with resolutions (or acceptDefaults: true) to apply.
guidance.notWhen: At hive creation (pot:create seeds automatically). To re-adopt a newer version of an already-installed pack — learning_packs:upgrade.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { pot } first (what's installed); after install, learning.hive invalidates so the Learnings view refreshes.

tools.name: learning_packs:list
tools.description: List resolvable learning packs (builtin + Comb-installed) and, when `pot` is given, that hive's installed state: per-pack rows present/edited, enabled/disabled, and whether a newer pack version is adoptable.

guidance.when: Before learning_packs:install/upgrade (what's available + what's already in the hive), or when the user asks what learnings their hive carries.
guidance.notWhen: To read the actual learning texts — learning.hive backs the Learnings UI, and memory:list { hive_slug } returns the rows.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:install { pot, pack } to add one; learning_packs:upgrade when updateAvailable; learning_packs:set_enabled to mute a pack without uninstalling.

tools.name: learning_packs:publish
tools.description: List an exported learning pack on the Comb: resolves the member repo's GitHub coords, publishes a kind='learning-pack' listing (listing_ref = packId) with the operator's gh token + attestation. The listing lands PENDING (D-007) — an operator must approve it before anyone else sees it.

guidance.when: After learning_packs:export and the files are pushed to the GitHub repo.
guidance.notWhen: The pack files are not on GitHub yet — publish points at the repo; export first, push, then publish.
guidance.chaining: The response carries review_status pending — the submitter sees it on their own listing; operators approve at /admin/cupboard-moderation.

tools.name: learning_packs:set_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable one OR many learning packs' injection for a hive WITHOUT uninstalling them — the rows stay stored; agents just stop recalling them. Cheap to flip, fully reversible. Single: { pot, pack, enabled }. Many packs same hive: { pot, packs:[…], enabled }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ pot, pack, enabled }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, hive, pack, enabled? | error }], counts } — correlate by hive+pack, not by position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Trying out whether a pack helps, or quarantining one that seems to misdirect agents — before reaching for uninstall. Flip several at once via packs:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Permanently removing a pack — learning_packs:uninstall.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { pot } shows enabled state per installed pack. Bulk: single | items[] (or packs) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by hive+pack not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: learning_packs:sweep
tools.description: Re-run the conflict judge across a hive's whole shared memory pool and report contradiction pairs — catches conflicts that emerged AFTER install (pack learnings vs what the hive organically learned later). Read-only; capped at 200 rows per sweep.

guidance.when: Periodic hygiene (a Queen idle-turn task), after installing a pack into a hive with many organic learnings, or when agents seem to be following contradictory guidance.
guidance.notWhen: At install time — learning_packs:install runs its own per-item review.
guidance.chaining: Resolve a reported pair deliberately: memory:forget the wrong side, or memory:update it to reconcile.

tools.name: learning_packs:uninstall
tools.description: Remove a learning pack's rows from a hive's shared memory (provenance-driven). Rows the user edited since seeding are KEPT by default and reported; keepEdited: false removes those too. Organic (hive-learned) rows are never touched.

guidance.when: The user wants a pack gone from a pot, or before re-installing a pack from scratch.
guidance.notWhen: To temporarily mute a pack — learning_packs:set_enabled { enabled: false } keeps the rows and just stops injecting them.
guidance.chaining: learning_packs:list { pot } shows what remains; kept edited rows are listed in the response.

tools.name: learning_packs:upgrade
tools.description: Adopt a newer version of an installed learning pack: NEW items (no row in the hive's pool) are classified like an install and added per your resolutions; rows already present are never auto-modified. Call once for the plan, re-call with resolutions (or acceptDefaults: true) to apply.

guidance.when: learning_packs:list shows updateAvailable for an installed pack.
guidance.notWhen: First-time install — learning_packs:install.
guidance.chaining: The response reports installedVersions vs availableVersion + the adoptable-new-items review.

tools.name: lexicon:active_pack
tools.description: The active brand pack's full term→label map (every term key → singular/plural forms) plus the pack id. Resolved via the server-side lexicon twin so the `papercusp-the-hive` flag is respected. The single source of truth for any non-React/non-server surface (e.g. the Rust pui) that needs the live lexicon without duplicating the packs.

guidance.when: A client outside the React/server lexicon wiring (the pui TUI, a CLI) needs the active term labels; fetch once at startup and re-fetch on a flag change if a push rail exists.
guidance.notWhen: You are in React (use the useLexicon hook) or server code (import term() from the lexicon module) — those resolve in-process.

tools.name: locks:acquire
tools.description: Claim a set of files for exclusive editing. Returns ok+lock_id, or busy+contention details. On contention prefer wake_on_grant:true — queue a waiter + one-shot wake, return immediately; END YOUR TURN, re-invoked on grant (no polling, no held turn). Attach pending_edit for a small non-conflicting edit applied on grant, no wake needed. wait={max_sec:N} (≤300) is the legacy blocking wait for short same-turn needs. Paths must be repo-relative POSIX (no ./, .., //, trailing /, backslashes, absolute paths); resolve symlinks caller-side.

guidance.when: For a DELIBERATE multi-file claim held across several edits AND the commit — acquire once, release after committing. Before individual Codex writes only when that session lacks lock hooks; managed Codex/Claude/OMP homes hook apply_patch/Edit/Write automatically.
guidance.notWhen: Read-only inspection needs no claim. A single incidental edit in a hooked session needs no manual call — do NOT wrap every hooked edit in acquire/release. Explicit locks are the fallback for unhooked Codex.
guidance.chaining: On ok: edit → commit → locks:release { lock_id }. On busy: wake_on_grant:true → end your turn; the wake carries your lock_id + running TTL — edit, then release. Only block (wait) when you need the lock THIS turn and the holder is about to finish; events:cancel + locks:cancel_wait retracts a queued wake.

tools.name: locks:acquire_granular
tools.description: Acquire a multi-granularity intention lock on a path NODE (a file, a directory/subtree, or the harness root ""). mode "X" = own the subtree exclusively (a directory lock for a refactor, or a file write); "S" = read the whole subtree; "SIX" = read the subtree while writing one node; IS/IX are the intention modes (usually derived for you). The lock places the matching intention on every ancestor incl. the harness root, so a harness-exclusive (X on "") now conflicts with any descendant file lock. All-or-nothing — you get the whole lock-set or a conflict list. Release with locks:release_granular.

guidance.when: A directory/subtree refactor (X on a dir), reading a whole subtree (S), or coordinating file-vs-harness-level work when a single-file lock is too narrow. Use "" for the harness root.
guidance.notWhen: A single-file edit: rely on the per-edit hook or use locks:acquire. Cross-resource coordination (dev server, DB schema): use locks:acquire_resource. Not as a mutex for non-file operations like fleet setup or work-item/plan changes.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular → do the work → locks:release_granular. On conflict, inspect conflicts and pivot/retry.

tools.name: locks:acquire_resource
tools.description: Acquire a NAMED resource (must be registered; see locks:list). mode:"shared" = "I am using it" (many coexist); mode:"exclusive" = "I need to restart/mutate it" (granted only once shared holders drain to zero). For exclusive, set wait:{max_drain_sec:N} (≤300) to block while existing shared holders finish — new shared acquisitions are refused meanwhile. Release with locks:release_resource.

guidance.when: Before relying on a shared resource (mode shared), or before a destructive action on it like restarting the dev server (mode exclusive). Registered resources only — check locks:list.
guidance.notWhen: File edits — use locks:acquire only for deliberate multi-file claims or when hook diagnostics say the per-edit hook is unavailable. An unregistered ad-hoc name — register it first (locks are useless if names diverge).
guidance.chaining: shared: acquire_resource{mode:shared} → use it → release_resource. exclusive restart: acquire_resource{mode:exclusive,wait:{max_drain_sec}} → on ok+held do the restart → release_resource (signals it is back up).

tools.name: locks:cancel_wait
tools.description: Abandon a queued waiter ticket. Returns cancelled=true if the wait was active; cancelled=false means a grant raced (you now hold a lock you didn't want — call locks:release immediately).

guidance.when: Mid-wait, when the user redirects you to other work or you decide a different approach.
guidance.notWhen: After you've already received an ok response from locks:acquire — there's no waiter to cancel.
guidance.chaining: On cancelled=false → locks:release { all_mine: true } to free the lock you got handed.

tools.name: locks:check_command
tools.description: Check a raw shell command against the named-lock registry: does it touch a resource with an exclusive (restart/migration) in flight? Returns decision (allow | warn | block) + the matched resources. The verdict a raw-Bash gate consumes.

guidance.when: A hook (or you) wants to know if a destructive command would collide with an in-flight exclusive hold before running it.
guidance.notWhen: Acquiring a named-resource lock — use locks:acquire_resource. File edits — use locks:acquire.
guidance.chaining: block → wait / coordinate; warn → proceed with care; allow → run.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat
tools.description: Extend a held lock's TTL. Returns extended=true on success; extended=false means the lock had already expired or been stolen.

guidance.when: For edits expected to take >15 min, call once at the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: For short edits — the default 20-min TTL covers it. Heartbeating every minute is wasteful.

tools.name: locks:heartbeat_resource
tools.description: Extend a named-resource lease you hold (by lock_id) for another ttl_sec. Owner-checked; no-op if the lease already lapsed.

guidance.when: Holding a named resource longer than its TTL — heartbeat near the halfway mark.
guidance.notWhen: Short holds within one TTL window. Released locks need no heartbeat.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → (long work, heartbeat periodically) → locks:release_resource.

tools.name: locks:list
tools.description: List registered named resources (name, rule, enforcement level) and who currently holds each, with a draining flag. The authoritative discovery surface for resource locks — only registered names are acquirable.

guidance.when: Before acquiring a named resource (to learn the exact name + the rule), or to see who holds a resource / whether it is draining.
guidance.notWhen: File-lock contention — that is locks:queue.
guidance.chaining: locks:list → locks:acquire_resource { resource, mode }.

tools.name: locks:queue
tools.description: Read the active locks and pending waiters for a workspace. Optionally filter by paths (overlap) or owner. Pass include_completed=true to also return terminal waiters from the last 24h (diagnostics).

guidance.when: Diagnostics — "what are the other agents doing?" or "why am I blocked?". Cheap, MVCC read.
guidance.notWhen: Before every acquire — locks:acquire already returns busy context. Use queue when the user asks.

tools.name: locks:release
tools.description: Release one or many held lock sets. Single: pass lock_id (with optional paths filter) or all_mine=true. Many: pass lock_ids:[…]. Fires the grant cascade for waiting agents.

guidance.when: Immediately after the edit is committed. Release several selected lock sets at once via lock_ids:[…]. On context loss / restart, call with all_mine=true to release everything.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-edit. The lock should outlive the edit by enough that no other agent races between release and PR merge.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire → edit → locks:release { lock_id } or { lock_ids:[…] }. Or: session-end → locks:release { all_mine: true }.

tools.name: locks:release_granular
tools.description: Release one or many granular intention lock-sets you hold, by lock_id or lock_ids. Frees each leaf node + all of its ancestor intention locks. Owner-checked.

guidance.when: As soon as the subtree/directory work the lock guarded is done. Release several selected lock sets at once via lock_ids:[…].
guidance.notWhen: While still working under the lock. Release is owner-checked — you can only drop your own lock-set.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_granular → work → locks:release_granular { lock_id } or { lock_ids:[…] }.

tools.name: locks:release_resource
tools.description: Release one or many named-resource locks you hold. Single: pass lock_id (preferred) or resource. Many: pass lock_ids:[…], resources:[…], or items:[{lock_id|resource}].

guidance.when: As soon as you are done using a shared resource, or immediately after an exclusive action (e.g. the dev-server restart) completes. Release several selected resource locks at once via lock_ids/resources/items.
guidance.notWhen: While still using the resource. Do not release another agent's lock — release is owner-checked and only drops your own rows.
guidance.chaining: locks:acquire_resource → use/act → locks:release_resource { lock_id } or { lock_ids:[…] }.

tools.name: loop:arm
tools.description: Arm the tracked engine loop for your session (or another ownerId) — the durable replacement for Claude /loop. Each fire re-wakes that warm session after its prior turn settles; context carries across iterations. Observable via loop:status / fleet:assignments and stoppable with loop:end.

guidance.when: Use for an su/interactive session that should keep advancing a goal on a recurring cadence. Arm it last before ending your turn. Pass ownerId only to arm an already-running, wake-reachable session other than your own.
guidance.notWhen: Not for wall-clock schedules (plans:set-schedule), one-off wakes (events:await), or autonomous queen/bee/scout loops (pot:declare-wake / kettle:declare-wake). Do not use Claude /loop instead.
guidance.chaining: loop:arm { intervalSec, goal } → end turn → re-wakes each iteration → loop:status to inspect → loop:end to stop.

tools.name: loop:checkpoint
tools.description: Write (or clear) your su AUTO loop's carry-note — a compressed 'note to my next self' a COLD loop wake (reset / recycle) reconstructs its working state from (your transcript does NOT carry across a cold wake). Pass the structured fields { did, left, insight, next } (rendered to the canonical template) OR a raw { note }. Keyed by the loop's ownerId — stable across reset/recycle, so a cold successor reads the SAME note. Replace-on-write; blank/null clears — except { walls } rows (owner-gated commitments): they render into every wake until you pass walls:[]. Returns { ok, harness, ownerId, cleared, length, walls }.

guidance.when: Before you end a turn on a COLD loop (carry:'cold'): persist what the next cold wake needs to continue — what you did, what is left, the key non-obvious insight, and the single next action. Keep it COMPRESSED (facts, not a transcript). Until the first checkpoint exists a cold loop silently stays WARM (the P-006 no-anchor guard), and a cold loop that stops checkpointing keeps restarting from a stale note.
guidance.notWhen: A WARM loop (carry:'warm', the default) carries its live transcript across wakes and needs no carry-note. Not for work-item state — that is work_items:checkpoint.
guidance.chaining: loop:checkpoint { did, left, insight, next } as the last step before ending a cold-loop turn — but it is the WEAKEST continuity write: the carry-note is LOST if your session dies. So also refresh work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint } (a successor INHERITS it) and facts:assert any durable conclusion.

tools.name: loop:end
tools.description: End the loop on your own session (or another owner's, with `ownerId`) — stops the recurring warm wake. The routine is deactivated (history kept); re-arm anytime with loop:arm.

guidance.when: Stop a loop you armed with loop:arm — the goal is done, you are blocked on something external, or the user says stop. Better to loop:end than burn empty wakes spinning.
guidance.notWhen: Pause the WHOLE autoloop / routines engine — that is autoloop:control. End the autonomous hive loop — that is pot:pause.
guidance.chaining: loop:arm to start; loop:status to check; loop:end to stop.

tools.name: loop:soak-report
tools.description: Read the machine-checkable production-readiness gate for one hive over a rolling 12–24h window: bg-host stability, infra-curse rate, bee/queen/overwatch turn success, escalation backlog, green-checkpoint ratio, deploy latency, and context-burn telemetry (per-wake injected overhead, compactions/session, post-compaction error markers), plus a READY/NOT-READY verdict with reasons.

guidance.when: You need one deterministic "is this pot production-ready yet?" verdict backed by concrete operational metrics instead of a judgment call.
guidance.notWhen: You only need the next wake / subscriptions / placements summary — that is pot:status. Per-session loop state is loop:status.
guidance.chaining: Use with pot:status for the live wake/placements view, or the Learning tab panel for the same verdict in the UI.

tools.name: loop:status
tools.description: Inspect the loop on your own session (or another owner's, with `ownerId`): active?, interval, parked (turn in flight), next/last fire, cost-cap. Returns null when no loop exists for the owner.

guidance.when: Check whether your loop is still armed + when it next fires, or inspect another agent's loop.
guidance.notWhen: See the WORK a loop is producing — that is fleet:assignments (the self-assigned work_items). Whole-engine health — autoloop:status.
guidance.chaining: loop:arm to start; loop:end to stop.

tools.name: memory:forget
tools.description: Delete one OR many memory entries by id — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a not-found / timed-out id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest.

guidance.when: When the user explicitly says "forget X" / "don't remember that anymore" / "that's wrong, drop it". Pass every id to drop at once via `ids`. Always inform the user out loud ("Removed that from memory").
guidance.notWhen: To CORRECT a memory (replace its content), use memory:update — preserves history. Only use forget for outright removal.
guidance.chaining: memory:search / memory:list → memory:forget { ids:[…] } to drop several found memories in one call. Bulk: single | ids[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: memory:list
tools.description: List all memories for the current user. Supports filtering by kind and harness scope.

guidance.when: When the user asks to inspect their memory ("what have you stored about me?") or you need a filter-only query.
guidance.notWhen: For semantic lookup ("what did I say about X?"), use memory:search instead.

tools.name: memory:remember
tools.description: Store a STABLE fact about the user into persistent memory, kept VERBATIM as written. Use one of 4 kinds (user / feedback / project / reference). Write ONE tight, self-contained fact per call. For transient state, use coord — not memory.

guidance.when: When the user says "remember X" / "don't forget Y" / "next time…" / "from now on…", OR when YOU notice an error you made that would recur without persistence. ALWAYS inform the user out loud ("I'll remember that"). For project-specific facts, pass harness_slug — the fact then surfaces for anyone working in that harness. Write ONE self-contained fact per call, tightly phrased: it is stored EXACTLY as written (no server-side rewriting or condensing), so make it stand on its own, lead with the searchable terms/anchors (file paths, F-NNN, backticked symbols), and drop conversational preamble.
guidance.notWhen: Default scope is per-user. Do not pass harness_slug for personal preferences. For IN-FLIGHT / ephemeral state (what you are doing right now), use coord (coord:declare-intent / coord:send) — it is delta-delivered, not a semantic store.
guidance.chaining: After writing, the persona prompt will surface this entry on the next turn's pre-turn injection. No need to call memory:search to verify.

tools.name: memory:search
tools.description: Search the user's persistent memories by semantic similarity. Returns matched facts ranked by relevance.

guidance.when: When the user references specific context from past sessions ("what did I tell you about pricing?"). Pre-turn auto-injection covers most cases; only call this for targeted lookups.
guidance.notWhen: For lookups by exact metadata (kind), use memory:list — it's faster than vector search for filter-only queries.
guidance.chaining: Pair with memory:update / memory:forget when the user corrects something you recall.

tools.name: memory:update
tools.description: Edit one OR many memory entries: replace content and/or patch metadata (kind, workspaceId, scope/recall-pool) — preserving each id. Metadata patches are vec-safe (no re-embed). Single: { id, content?, kind?, … }. Many same patch: { ids:[…], kind?/scope?/… }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, content?, kind?, … }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; a not-found / timed-out id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: CONTENT: when the user corrects something you stored ("actually it's Daniel, not Dan") — pass `content`. METADATA HYGIENE: to re-tag a memory's `kind`, fix its `workspaceId`, or move it to the right recall `scope`/pool, pass those fields (no content needed); re-tag MANY at once via { ids:[…], kind } or items:[…]. Find the id via memory:search / memory:list first. For a content edit, tell the user ("Updating my memory: …").
guidance.notWhen: To REMOVE a memory entirely, use memory:forget. To ADD a new memory, use memory:remember. Do not change `scope` casually — it moves which queries can recall the memory.
guidance.chaining: memory:search → memory:update { ids:[…], kind } (bulk metadata hygiene). Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: messages:dismiss
tools.description:
When to use: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).

When NOT to use: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

guidance.when: Soft-hide a message you've handled — "ignore that note", "dismiss the comment on X". Reversible (status→archived, not deleted).
guidance.notWhen: For deleting a message, this isn't it — dismiss is reversible. For archiving a CHAT (multi-turn), use `agent_chats:archive`.

tools.name: messages:inbox
tools.description:
When to use: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.

When NOT to use: For sent items use `messages:outbox`. To soft-hide a handled message use `messages:dismiss`.

guidance.when: What's pending for me? Harness-level messages (directives, worker replies) — or pass `feature_id` for one feature's thread.
guidance.notWhen: For sent items use `messages:outbox`. To soft-hide a handled message use `messages:dismiss`.

tools.name: messages:outbox
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what did I send?", "did the message go through?", or you need to confirm a recent send.

When NOT to use: For incoming, use `messages:inbox`.

guidance.when: User asks "what did I send?", "did the message go through?", or you need to confirm a recent send.
guidance.notWhen: For incoming, use `messages:inbox`.

tools.name: messages:send
tools.description:
When to use: Forward a DURABLE note/directive to another agent (operator → "tell the worker to retry"). Feature-scoped: pass `to_feature_id` (+`from_feature_id`) to post on a feature's pipeline thread.

When NOT to use: A transient agent↔agent ping/handoff → `coord:send` (the live coord inbox); messages:send is the DURABLE supervisor→agent path (supervisor_notes), a SEPARATE inbox — don't cross-wire (coordination-unification-2026-06-23 P-010). Dispatch WORK via a `<spawn>` tag, not a message.

Chaining: Read replies with `messages:inbox`; soft-hide a handled one with `messages:dismiss`.

guidance.when: Forward a DURABLE note/directive to another agent (operator → "tell the worker to retry"). Feature-scoped: pass `to_feature_id` (+`from_feature_id`) to post on a feature's pipeline thread.
guidance.notWhen: A transient agent↔agent ping/handoff → `coord:send` (the live coord inbox); messages:send is the DURABLE supervisor→agent path (supervisor_notes), a SEPARATE inbox — don't cross-wire (coordination-unification-2026-06-23 P-010). Dispatch WORK via a `<spawn>` tag, not a message.
guidance.chaining: Read replies with `messages:inbox`; soft-hide a handled one with `messages:dismiss`.

tools.name: meta:define-datatype
tools.description: Declare a reusable entity TYPE (a "datatype" — bet, wager, forecast, position, …) into the workspace datatype registry, so blueprints can reference it via dependencies.datatypes and (generic-kind tier) work_items can be created with its kind. DEDUP-ONLY authority: a hard unique id + a soft semantic gate — if a similar datatype exists you get { ok:false, reason:"similar_exists", candidates } so you reuse it or pass force:true. Re-declaring the same name UPDATES it in place.

guidance.when: When a domain needs a shared, named entity TYPE that should be searchable / plannable / improvable like any Papercusp entity (D-001). Default tier generic-kind (a work_item kind + payload, zero migration). Use projection for money-truth/external-engine-owned types (read-only, authoritativeWriter:"engine:<name>").
guidance.notWhen: To define a TOOL (use meta:define-tool). To create an INSTANCE of an existing datatype (use work_items:create with the registered kind). A first-class (SQL-backed) datatype's migration does NOT ship here — it goes through the dogfood PR rail (tools:scaffold → platform:contribute).
guidance.chaining: meta:define-datatype { name, description, tier } → (generic-kind) work_items:create { kind } → search/plans/gym inherit it for free. A blueprint references it via dependencies.datatypes [name].

tools.name: meta:define-tool
tools.description: Create a NEW tool, routed by D-003 tier: composed (a DAG/recipe over EXISTING tools — mints no new capability, registers LIVE as a recipe you run via recipes:run) | sandboxed-imperative | elevated (genuinely new power — NOT registered; emits a reviewable skeleton for the PR rail + adversarial confinement proof → platform:contribute). Composed needs `script`; the dangerous tiers need group+verb+capability.

guidance.when: When a domain needs a new TOOL. Prefer composed (a recipe over existing primitives) — it is live and safe. Reach for sandboxed/elevated only for genuinely new power; those go through review, never runtime.
guidance.notWhen: To define a DATATYPE (meta:define-datatype). To run an existing composition (recipes:run). To only GENERATE a skeleton without the tier routing (tools:scaffold).
guidance.chaining: meta:define-tool { tier:"composed", script } → recipes:run. meta:define-tool { tier:"elevated", group, verb, capability } → implement the emitted skeleton → PR + platform:contribute.

tools.name: mode:get
tools.description: Read an agent's current modes: { agent? (default you), contracts? }. Returns active modes with axis, reason, who set them, owner-sticky flag, and (contracts:true) the full binding contract text.

guidance.when: Before redirecting a peer (is it owner-directed? then request, don't override) or to re-read your own binding contracts mid-session. Ambient visibility is already in coord:presence / coord:orient — reach for this for the detail.
guidance.notWhen: Fleet-wide mode surveys — read coord:presence once instead of N mode:get calls.
guidance.chaining: mode:get { agent } → mode:set { agent, mode, reason } (or a coord:send request when ownerDirected).

tools.name: mode:list
tools.description: The official mode catalog: id, axis (autonomy | work-source | overlay), one-liner, and which modes you have active. Same-axis modes exclude each other (mode:set auto-switches); cross-axis modes stack.

guidance.when: Orienting on what modes exist / which apply to a user ask, before offering one or calling mode:set.
guidance.notWhen: Reading a PEER’s modes — that is mode:get { agent } (or coord:presence ambiently).
guidance.chaining: mode:list → mode:set { mode, reason } → read the returned contract.

tools.name: mode:set
tools.description: Enter/exit an official session mode (auto | cold-auto | ideate | drain | grade) for yourself or a peer. { mode, reason, enabled?, agent?, ownerDirected? }. Same-axis modes AUTO-SWITCH (result carries switchedFrom); cross-axis modes stack. Peer-set: reason is delivered to the target with the mode contract; an owner-directed incumbent REFUSES a peer override (stickyConflict:true — downgraded to a request message). Self-set returns the full binding contract — read it. Audited in agent_mode_changes.

guidance.when: The user (or your judgment under AUTO) puts the session in a mode — "auto mode", "ideate", "drain the backlog", "grade X" — or you need to redirect a peer's operating posture with a reason they will see. Pass ownerDirected:true ONLY when the human owner explicitly instructed this mode — it arms the sticky guard peers cannot override.
guidance.notWhen: Transient per-task instructions that end with the turn — modes are standing session state. Never mode:set a peer to dodge coordination (the reason is delivered and audited); never pass ownerDirected on your own initiative.
guidance.chaining: mode:set → read the returned contract (self) · coord:orient re-injects active contracts each wake · mode:get { agent } to inspect anyone · exiting: mode:set { mode, enabled:false, reason }. A stickyConflict result means the incumbent is owner-directed: your reason was delivered as a REQUEST — do not retry, wait for the target/owner.

tools.name: network:board
tools.description: The aggregate Network board: one row per other-hive context across the capability-tier ladder — tier 1 this Swarm, tier 2 your own other hives, tier 3 shared-Hive peer Swarms (federated presence), tier 4 foreign Hives from the P2P directory (with their status beacon, your grants, and your outbound-ask traffic). Each row carries a tier + trust label; tier-specific fields (liveAgents/queueDepth/focus/wake/grants/asks) are present only where that tier supplies them. The data behind the dock Network tab.

guidance.when: You want a single cross-hive situational view — what every other hive context (own, federated peer, foreign) is and what we can see of it.
guidance.notWhen: Just the workspace-local hives — pot:list. Just the joinable P2P directory — discovery:pots. Per-bee placement detail — fleet:assignments. One hive in depth — pot:get.
guidance.chaining: discovery:pots → pot:cross_grant to admit a tier-4 peer; pot:get { slug } to drill into an own hive.

tools.name: new_subagent:approve
tools.description: BRAIN-ONLY: approve or deny a pending new_subagent spawn request. Resolves it + wakes the requester (which spawns on approve). Enforced at the dispatch layer — only the brain (operator principal) or a superuser may call it.

guidance.when: You are the brain and a new_subagent:request is pending; you have judged whether the spawn is worth it given open work + the live spawn headroom.
guidance.notWhen: You are a pipeline/worker agent — you cannot approve spawns (the gate denies you). To ASK for a spawn, use new_subagent:request.

tools.name: new_subagent:request
tools.description: Request the brain spin up a new sub-agent. Routes a typed, brain-only-approvable request; you then events:await the grant and spawn on approval. The BRAIN decides whether it is worth it (informed by the live spawn headroom + open work) — this is judgment, not a rules budget.

guidance.when: You want to spawn a sub-agent (a helper/specialist) as an autonomous initiative beyond your own role — a spawn worth a brain decision.
guidance.notWhen: You ARE the brain/operator (you allocate directly) OR this is already-decided pipeline work (the pipeline admits its own role progression) OR a human-initiated psu session (no request needed).
guidance.chaining: new_subagent:request → events:await { event: <await_event> } (end your turn) → on wake, if choice="approve", cup:spawn { role, harness, feature }.

tools.name: notifications:recent
tools.description: List recent toast notifications shown in the app (errors, warnings, info, success).

guidance.when: Read recent toast notifications shown to the user — for "did I miss anything?" / replay.
guidance.notWhen: For PERSISTENT inbox items, use `messages:inbox`. Notifications are ephemeral toasts.

tools.name: omp:config
tools.description: Read or update the local omp CLI config tree (get / set { key, value } / unset { key }).

guidance.when: Read or set an OMP CLI config key (model, paths, env tweaks). Used during installation / first-run flows.
guidance.notWhen: For OPERATOR runtime preferences (voice, scanner), use `operator:preferences`. omp:config is the CLI tool's config.

tools.name: omp:sessions
tools.description: List, search, read, and summarize local OMP session JSONL files.

guidance.when: Inspect local OMP session history: op='list' to find a session id, op='state'/'get' to read it — for continuing a compacted/handed-off session or debugging an overnight OMP agent. For CONTENT search prefer sessions:search (indexed, ranked, cross-client, with context windows); op='search' here is a raw substring grep over the local OMP JSONL archive, for the un-indexed tail or when the index is off.
guidance.notWhen: Searching transcript CONTENT across clients → sessions:search / search:* (indexed), not op='search'. For Papercusp harness runs stored in Postgres, use the harness/agent_chats/plans tools first. omp:sessions is specifically the local OMP JSONL transcript archive on this workstation.
guidance.chaining: op='list' → op='state' (compact structured state) or op='get' (bounded raw entries). For content search use sessions:search { query } (indexed) rather than op='search'.

tools.name: operator:audit
tools.description: Log a single operator-card lifecycle event (accepted / ignored / dispatched / dismissed / …) so the dashboard reconstruction sees it.

guidance.when: Operator-scoped audit feed — every operator action (scans fired, cards dispatched, mode flips).
guidance.notWhen: For workspace-wide audit including non-operator actors, use `audit:list`. operator:audit is the narrower operator-only stream.

tools.name: operator:budget
tools.description: Read or set the daily operator budget cap. Get is any role; set is operator only.

guidance.when: Read operator daily-spend status — todaySpendUsd, capUsd, exceeded flag.
guidance.notWhen: For voice-specific spend, use `operator:voice_spend_summary`. For raising the cap, use /settings/operator.

tools.name: operator:conv_voice
tools.description: Read or set the EL Conv AI agent voice (voice_id, optional model_id). Adds public voices to library if needed.

guidance.when: Read voice-conversation state (mode, engine, transcript). Diagnostic for the voice-converse pipeline.
guidance.notWhen: For voice PREFS (defaults), use `operator:voice_prefs`. conv_voice is runtime, not config.

tools.name: operator:converse
tools.description: Operator brain conversation turn. Self-contained: builds the prompt (role+memory+history+trigger), gates on budget, runs the LLM with agentmcp tools, records spend, post-turn mem0.add, dispatches <spawn> tags. Streams deltas + tool_calls.

tools.name: operator:credentials_status
tools.description: Masked credential status for voice providers (set/not-set + tail). Read-only — never returns raw keys.

guidance.when: Check which API credentials (EL, OpenAI, etc.) are configured + valid. Used in onboarding + diagnostics.
guidance.notWhen: For SETTING credentials, use the /settings UI directly — agents shouldn't paste secrets.

tools.name: operator:decisions
tools.description: Read recent operator_decisions rows for the active workspace (id, ts, actor, action, target, details).

guidance.when: Read the operator decision log — what flips, dispatches, and autoaccepts happened and why.
guidance.notWhen: For action audit (user-action style), use `actions:recent` or `operator:audit`. decisions is the operator-policy view.

tools.name: operator:dedup_check
tools.description: Check if a candidate title fuzzy-matches any card in `existing` above the threshold. Returns { match, threshold }.

guidance.when: Check whether a suggestion / scan candidate duplicates a recent one before committing it to the panel.
guidance.notWhen: For listing existing scans, use `operator:scans_list`.

tools.name: operator:multi_workspace
tools.description: Aggregation of every other workspace's last-scan snapshot (active workspace omitted).

guidance.when: List workspaces the operator can switch between — used by the workspace switcher.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT workspace's harnesses, use `harness:list`. multi_workspace is the workspace enumerator.

tools.name: operator:notes
tools.description: Read or append feature-scoped operator notes (Steer primitive). { op: read|append, slug?, featureId, content?, author? }.

guidance.when: Read or update the operator's free-form note buffer — long-running scratch the user adds via /settings.
guidance.notWhen: For cross-agent memory, use `memory:search` / `memory:remember`. Notes is operator-only, user-editable.

tools.name: operator:nudge
tools.description: Arbitrate a spoken nudge — returns { fired } indicating whether the per-kind dedup window allows speaking now.

guidance.when: Send a one-shot toast to the user — "checkpoint?", "smoke failed", etc. Use sparingly; chat is the primary channel.
guidance.notWhen: For conversation, just speak in your reply. nudge is for non-conversational status only.

tools.name: operator:paused
tools.description: Read the operator pause sentinel — true when scans are suppressed.

guidance.when: Read/set the global operator-pause flag — silences scans + scanner-triggered cards across the workspace.
guidance.notWhen: For per-harness autoloop pause, use `autoloop:control`. paused is operator-global; autoloop is harness-scoped.

tools.name: operator:preferences
tools.description: List / append / remove operator preference entries (provenance-tagged markdown).

guidance.when: Read or update operator-level preferences (scan cadence, autoAccept tier, persona name, etc.).
guidance.notWhen: For VOICE prefs specifically, use `operator:voice_prefs`. For workspace-level config, use `multi_workspace`/`papercusp:list_workspaces`.

tools.name: operator:preview_prompt
tools.description: Build the operator scanner prompt for a request without running it. Useful for debug + plugin-author validation.

guidance.when: Render the operator's assembled prompt for a given trigger — debug tool to verify what the model sees.
guidance.notWhen: Production code shouldn't depend on this; it's diagnostic only.

tools.name: operator:rate_limit_config
tools.description: Read or edit the live fleet rate-limit config: maxSimultaneousAgents (fleet-wide concurrent-agent cap), concurrencyFloor (the AIMD floor), providerFloors (per-provider cold-start {maxConcurrent,rpm} floors — the subscription rpm gate), and aimd (the response-curve: cleanTurnsPerStep + decreaseFactor). Edits persist + propagate with zero restart.

guidance.when: Throttle/open the fleet ("drop to 2 agents while I use Claude"), tune a provider's static rpm floor live (providerFloors.anthropic.rpm), or reshape the AIMD curve (slower recovery / gentler backoff) during a rate-limit incident — all without a deploy.
guidance.notWhen: READ the live pacing/pause/usage state — dev:rate_governor_status (this tool reads the persisted CONFIG, not the live bucket state). Per-TOOL call quotas → quota:set_tool.
guidance.chaining: After a set, dev:rate_governor_status shows the new floors/cap take effect; config:list-overrides shows every active override.

tools.name: operator:standing_approval_mark_shown
tools.description: Mark a standing-approval candidate as first-shown (timestamp gate for voice-approve eligibility).

guidance.when: Mark a standing-approval banner as shown so it doesn't re-flash. Internal UI bookkeeping.
guidance.notWhen: For listing approvals, use `operator:standing_approvals_list`. For deciding, `operator:standing_approvals_decide`.

tools.name: operator:standing_approvals_decide
tools.description: Approve or dismiss a standing-approval candidate. Approve writes a [STANDING-APPROVE] entry to operator preferences.

guidance.when: User answered yes/no to a standing-approval prompt — record the decision so the autoaccept rule applies / doesn't.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE-OFF dispatch confirmation, just call `panel_dispatch_card` after the user yes/nos verbally. standing_approvals_decide is for the persistent rule.

tools.name: operator:standing_approvals_list
tools.description: Standing-approval candidates: capability/target pairs the operator has silently dispatched ≥3× in 24h, eligible for "always allow".

guidance.when: List standing approvals — pre-authorized actions the user said "go ahead" to once.
guidance.notWhen: For one-off pending reviews, use `harness:pending_reviews`. Standing approvals are session-persistent autoaccepts.

tools.name: operator:stats
tools.description: 7-day operator KPIs: card counts, auto-dispatch rate, dismissal rate, escalation rate, median ack latency, spend.

guidance.when: Aggregate operator stats — scans/day, dispatches/day, mode-flip counts. For dashboards / status reports.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE state, use the specific dedicated tool. stats is historical aggregates.

tools.name: operator:trigger_state
tools.description: Read the workspace trigger-state fingerprint + raw state (used by background scanner to decide rescans).

guidance.when: Read scanner trigger state — when the next scan fires, what's pending.
guidance.notWhen: For LIVE scan results, use `operator:last_scan` or `operator:scans_list`.

tools.name: operator:voice_debug
tools.description: Read, append, or clear the process-local voice-debug ring buffer (same buffer as the agent-mcp/voice-debug route).

guidance.when: Debug snapshot of the voice engine state — engine in use, last connection, transcript queue. Diagnostic only.
guidance.notWhen: For voice preferences, use `operator:voice_prefs`. voice_debug is read-only diagnostic.

tools.name: operator:voice_prefs
tools.description: Read or partial-update operator voice prefs (engine selectors, feature toggles, agent ids).

guidance.when: Read/set voice preferences — engine, wake word, autostart, persona name.
guidance.notWhen: For runtime state of an active session, use `operator:conv_voice`. voice_prefs is user-set config.

tools.name: operator:voice_spend_summary
tools.description: Voice spend snapshot — el (Conv AI minutes), stt (today USD + caps), tts (per-K-char rate + caps), or all merged.

guidance.when: Read aggregated voice-engine spend (EL minutes, OpenAI tokens) for budget visibility.
guidance.notWhen: For operator daily budget across all surfaces, use `operator:budget`. voice_spend_summary is the voice slice.

tools.name: operator:voice_utterance_log
tools.description: Append a voice-utterance audit row (source/mode/length/persona-flags/modifications).

guidance.when: Read recent voice transcripts — what STT heard, what TTS spoke. Useful for "what did I just say?" / debugging mishears.
guidance.notWhen: For TEXT chat history, that lives in operator_turns. voice_utterance_log is voice-only.

tools.name: oracle:chat
tools.description: Single-turn Oracle assistant chat. Streams delta/tool_call/cost events; returns final assistant text.

tools.name: p2p:trace
tools.description: Assemble the cross-machine P2P timeline for a pot (optionally one offer): loud-refusal receipts from BOTH sides (federated p2p_receipts facts, M21 offer-id threaded) + the local M15 refused-op counter snapshot. Receipts with kind='excused-breach' are preemption-class interruptions (X8) — excluded from reliability signals.

guidance.when: Debugging a refused/silent-looking cross-peer action ("why did my offer/wake/spawn not run on peer X?"): pass the pot (and offerId when you have one) to see every receipt both sides produced, ordered by event time, plus the unauthenticated-refusal counters. The receipt names the EXACT missing capability/budget.
guidance.notWhen: Inspecting grant STATE (who may do what right now) — read the grants surface / checkP2pCapability instead; trace is the event TIMELINE, not the authorization table. General coord message history — coord:feed / coord:catch-up.
guidance.chaining: p2p:trace (you) → fix the named gap (grant a capability, raise a cap, re-attest a device) → retry the action.

tools.name: papercup:converse
tools.description: Sentinel brain conversation turn. The operator:converse brain loaded with the always-on, voice-first Sentinel persona (role=sentinel). Same lifecycle (prompt build, budget gate, LLM stream, spend, mem0); only the persona differs.

tools.name: papercusp:list_workspaces
tools.description:
When to use: Discovery helper for superuser shells — list all workspaces in the installation. Used when scope-switching.

When NOT to use: For the CURRENT workspace details, use the operator-state APIs. papercusp:list_workspaces is the cross-workspace enumerator.

guidance.when: Discovery helper for superuser shells — list all workspaces in the installation. Used when scope-switching.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT workspace details, use the operator-state APIs. papercusp:list_workspaces is the cross-workspace enumerator.

tools.name: pending_events:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what's queued up?", "what events are pending?", or you need to inspect the hook-event backlog.

When NOT to use: For approvals (plan reviews, escalations awaiting user yes/no), use `pending_reviews_list`. Pending EVENTS are hook plumbing; pending REVIEWS are user-facing decisions.

guidance.when: User asks "what's queued up?", "what events are pending?", or you need to inspect the hook-event backlog.
guidance.notWhen: For approvals (plan reviews, escalations awaiting user yes/no), use `pending_reviews_list`. Pending EVENTS are hook plumbing; pending REVIEWS are user-facing decisions.

tools.name: plan-item:await
tools.description: Sleep until a plan item flips to done (plan-item:done:<slug>:<id>) instead of polling plans:get. Then END YOUR TURN.

guidance.when: You are blocked on another plan item (a dependency P-NNN) finishing before you can proceed — arm this and end your turn instead of re-reading plans:get.
guidance.notWhen: Inspecting a plan once — plans:get. Waiting on a WORK item (WI-NNN) — work-item:await.
guidance.chaining: plan-item:await { slug, id: "P-014" } → end turn → on wake the item is done; continue.

tools.name: plan_items:adopt_name
tools.description: Adopt a stable agent-NAME for this session (e.g. "builder-1"). Assignment targets a NAME, not a session, so after adopting you can read your assigned items (plan_items:my_items) and claim them across interruptions. Idempotent; re-adopting overwrites this session's name.

guidance.when: At the start of a session that should act as a named agent — e.g. you were told "you are builder-1, go to your items". Adopt the name, then plan_items:my_items.
guidance.notWhen: Ad-hoc one-off work you are not coordinating by name — you can still claim unassigned pool items without a name.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:adopt_name { name } → plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim.

tools.name: plan_items:assign
tools.description: Push-assign one OR many plan items (P-NNN) to a stable agent-NAME. Durable intent — survives interruption; the named agent reads it via plan_items:my_items and claims it. Intra-user only: a name you own (a fresh name is claimed for you); a name owned by another user is refused (cross-user is pull-only). Single: { plan, item, assignee }. Many same plan+assignee: { plan, itemIds:[…], assignee }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, assignee, harness?, strategy?, note? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, assignment? | refused | error }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; one refusal never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are dividing your own plan work across your named agents — "builder-1 takes P-001..P-003". Assign several at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want to start working on an item right now — that is plan_items:claim (the live grip). Handing work to another USER's agents — they pull it (you cannot push onto their machine).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:assign { harness, plan, item, assignee } → the named agent: plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim.

tools.name: plan_items:claim
tools.description: Take the live, heartbeat-leased grip on one OR many plan items — what you call when you actually START them. Refused per item if it is assigned to a different agent-name, or unassigned in a plan whose work-group you have not joined. Single: { plan, item }. Many same plan: { plan, itemIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, intent?, mode?, ttl_sec?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, result (claim with claim_id + lease expiry), convertStatus?, workItem? }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; a refused/conflicted claim is that item's ok:false without failing the rest. Keep a claim alive with plan_items:heartbeat, drop it with plan_items:release.

guidance.when: You are about to begin work on item(s) (yours via assignment, or pulled from the pool). Claim several at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You only want to mark intent for later without starting — that is assignment, not a claim. Renewing an existing claim — that is plan_items:heartbeat.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim { harness, plan, item } → work → plan_items:heartbeat (per turn) → plan_items:release when done.

tools.name: plan_items:convert
