tools.description: Convert-at-pickup (D-015): pick up one OR many plan items by converting each to a work_item in one call — takes the policy-checked plan-item lease, mints (or idempotently resumes) the work_item with you as assignee, links it back (`implements` edge + payload stamp), and auto-flips the plan item to wip. Single: { plan, item }. Many same plan: { plan, itemIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, kind?, title?, brief?, … }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, status, workItem?, planItem? }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; a refused/conflicted convert is that item's ok:false without failing the rest. The work_item is then your execution record: work_items:complete on it reflects the plan item to done.

guidance.when: You are picking up plan item(s) to work them — this replaces a bare plan_items:claim: every worked item gets a tracked work_item (no untracked self-item). Pick up several at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You only want the lease without an execution record (rare; plan_items:claim). The item is already converted and you hold it — just keep working; re-converting is a harmless resume.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable:true } → plan_items:convert { plan, item } → work → work_items:complete { id, completion } (reflects the plan item to done) or work_items:release (returns it to todo).

tools.name: plan_items:heartbeat
tools.description: Renew your claim's lease on one OR many plan items. Send kind="activity" when you complete a unit of work (the turn-based pulse a SHARED harness needs), kind="extend" with a larger ttl_sec for a legitimately long single operation, or kind="keepalive" to prove liveness on a LOCAL harness. claim_id optional (resolved from your current claim). Single: { plan, item, kind? }. Many same plan+kind: { plan, itemIds:[…], kind? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, kind?, ttl_sec?, claim_id?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, renewed?, held?, … | note }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; holding no claim on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Periodically while holding a claim — ideally once per completed turn (kind="activity"), or kind="extend" before a long uninterrupted op. Pulse several held items at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You are done — that is plan_items:release. The claim has already lapsed — re-acquire with plan_items:claim (a lapsed claim cannot be heartbeated back to life).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim → plan_items:heartbeat { kind: "activity" } per turn → plan_items:release.

tools.name: plan_items:join_group
tools.description: Join a shared plan's work-group so your sessions may CLAIM unassigned items from its pool (cross-user pull-only — nobody push-assigns onto your machine). A plan with no work-group is open; declaring one gates pool pulls to members.

guidance.when: You want to help on a shared plan owned by another user — join, then pull unassigned items.
guidance.notWhen: It is your own plan / single-user — pool pulls are already open.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:join_group { harness, plan } → plan_items:status → plan_items:claim an unassigned item.

tools.name: plan_items:leave_group
tools.description: Leave a plan's work-group (stop being eligible to pull its unassigned items).

guidance.when: You are done helping on a shared plan.
guidance.notWhen: You still hold claims there — release them first (plan_items:release).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:leave_group { harness, plan }.

tools.name: plan_items:my_items
tools.description: List the plan items assigned to your agent-NAME (across all plans), each with its live claim state (active / assigned-idle). "Go to your items" resolves here. Adopt a name first (plan_items:adopt_name) or pass agent_name explicitly.

guidance.when: You were told to work on your assigned items — read them here, then claim the next idle one.
guidance.notWhen: You want unassigned pool items — those are not "yours"; see plan_items:status for the pool.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:adopt_name → plan_items:my_items → plan_items:claim { the next assigned-idle item }.

tools.name: plan_items:release
tools.description: Drop your live claim on one OR many plan items so each returns to your assignee status (if assigned) or the pool (if pulled). Does NOT clear the assignment — the item stays yours by name; you just stop holding it. claim_id is optional (resolved from your current claim). Single: { plan, item, claim_id? }. Many same plan: { plan, itemIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, harness?, claim_id? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, released? | note }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; holding no claim on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You finished (or are pausing) work on item(s) you claimed and want to free the live grip. Release several at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want to give up the item entirely — also plan_items:unassign it.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:claim → … → plan_items:release { harness, plan, item }.

tools.name: plan_items:status
tools.description: The merged per-item view of a plan: each item's disposition (pooled / assigned-idle / active / claimed-pooled / claimed-mismatch) combining the durable assignment with the live claim, plus any work-group members. The coherent answer to "who is doing what on this plan".

guidance.when: Deciding what to pick up, or auditing who holds what on a plan.
guidance.notWhen: You only want YOUR assigned items — plan_items:my_items is narrower.
guidance.chaining: plan_items:status { harness, plan } → claim a "pooled"/"assigned-idle"(yours) item.

tools.name: plan_items:unassign
tools.description: Release one OR many plan items' assignment so each returns to the unassigned pool. History persists (soft-release). Does NOT drop a live claim — release that with plan_items:release. Single: { plan, item }. Many same plan: { plan, itemIds:[…] }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ plan, item, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, plan, item, released? | error }], counts } — correlate by { plan, item }; a no-op (no active assignment) stays ok:true with released:null.

guidance.when: An assignment is no longer wanted — reassigning to nobody, or freeing item(s) back to the pool. Unassign several at once via itemIds:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You just want to stop actively working but keep the item assigned to you — that is plan_items:release (drops the live claim, keeps the assignment).
guidance.chaining: plan_items:status to see assignments → plan_items:unassign { harness, plan, item }.

tools.name: plans:add-decision
tools.description: Append one OR many new decisions to a plan. Allocates the next D-NNN id inside a lock (concurrent calls produce non-colliding ids). Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:. Single: { slug, title, body }. Many: items:[{ slug, title, body, refs?, affects? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, decisionId, propagated_to? | error }], counts } — each result embeds the NEW decisionId; correlate by id, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A decision-shaped output: trade-off resolved, scope ratified, choice made between options. Capture so a fresh agent doesn't relitigate. Add several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Adding work units — use plans:add-item. Flipping status — plans:set-status. Updating overall state — plans:set-now.
guidance.chaining: plans:add-decision → optionally plans:set-now referencing the new D-NNN in **State:**.

tools.name: plans:add-item
tools.description: Append one OR many new items to a phase. Allocates the next P-NNN id inside a lock. Creates the phase section if it doesn't exist. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:. Single: { slug, phase, text, importance }. Many to one phase: { slug, phase, importance, items:[{ text, blockedBy? }] }. Heterogeneous: items:[{ slug, phase, text, importance }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, createdPhase | error }], counts } — each result embeds the NEW itemId; correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: New work surfaces — a chunk to do, a verification step, a follow-up. Pick the right phase (or name a new one). Add several at once via items:[…] (the new ids come back per result).
guidance.notWhen: Updating an existing item — that's a direct edit, not an assisted write (the format is stable). Or status flip — plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:add-item → plans:set-status to flip newly added items off `todo` when work starts.

tools.name: plans:apply-plan-block
tools.description: Parse and apply a ```promote:plan fenced block: creates a new draft plan via plans:new → plans:set-now → plans:add-item × N → plans:add-decision × N.

guidance.when: The architect (or any agent) emitted a ```promote:plan block and the human accepted it. Pass the raw block content (everything between the fences, excluding the fence lines themselves).
guidance.notWhen: The plan already exists — use plans:set-content or the individual write verbs instead.
guidance.chaining: Returns { ok, slug }. Follow with plans:get to read the created plan.

tools.name: plans:arm-schedule
tools.description: Arm a scheduled plan so it starts firing runs on its cadence (materializes its routine + sets schedule_active). Authoring (plans:set-schedule) does not arm; this does. Autonomy-gated (schedule-arm category): the Queen escalates unless graduated; the owner arms directly.

guidance.when: Activating a plan you already scheduled (plans:set-schedule) so it begins firing runs.
guidance.notWhen: Authoring/editing the cadence (plans:set-schedule). Firing one run by hand (plans:run-now).
guidance.chaining: plans:set-schedule → plans:arm-schedule → the routine fires system:plan-run on cadence. plans:disarm-schedule stops it.

tools.name: plans:attention
tools.description: The Planning tab's unified attention feed: plan items + coord escalations + coord messages-to-human + smoke-fails + operator <report> turns, mapped to a single AttentionItem shape, grouped by plan (+ per-harness Alerts bucket), importance-sorted. Each source best-effort.

guidance.when: You want everything awaiting the human / pickable, in one importance-sorted feed — the Planning tab inbox, or to find the single most-urgent open thing.
guidance.notWhen: You only need plan items (use plans:items), or the full structure of one plan (plans:get). For the orchestrator DONE-gate use plans:items { needsHuman: true }.
guidance.chaining: plans:attention → act on an item via its kind (plans:set-status for plan items, coord:resolve for escalations).

tools.name: plans:backfill-revisions
tools.description: One-time, idempotent migration: seed the plan_revisions spine from git history — one synthetic revision per past commit (commit subject as a weak rationale, session_kind git_backfill, no session). A plan that already has revisions is skipped, so re-running is safe.

guidance.when: Once, after the revision spine ships, to give existing plans a history before their first live write — or to seed a single plan whose spine was never populated.
guidance.notWhen: Routine use. The spine is maintained automatically by every plans:* write verb; this is a migration, not an everyday tool.
guidance.chaining: plans:backfill-revisions → plans:revisions to confirm the chain.

tools.name: plans:disarm-schedule
tools.description: Disarm (pause) a scheduled plan so it stops firing runs — sets schedule_active=false + deactivates its routine. The authored schedule is kept; plans:arm-schedule re-arms it.

guidance.when: Pausing a scheduled plan so it stops firing, without discarding its schedule.
guidance.notWhen: Permanently removing the schedule — use plans:set-schedule { schedule: null }.
guidance.chaining: plans:disarm-schedule (pause) ↔ plans:arm-schedule (resume).

tools.name: plans:edit
tools.description: Edit a plan in place by exact string replace (old_string → new_string), like the file Edit tool — the surgical way to fix a citation, a line, or a paragraph without resending the whole document. old_string must match exactly once (or pass replace_all). Rejects: string_not_found, string_not_unique, a result that would degrade the plan to legacy, or a lint failure. Records a plan revision. expectedHash is optional — the exact match is the concurrency guard.

guidance.when: Correcting or rewriting a SPECIFIC part of a plan body the structured verbs cannot reach — a stale citation, a wrong line, a paragraph in `## Background` or a decision body. The default for small/targeted prose fixes.
guidance.notWhen: Replacing the whole Now block (set-now), appending a decision/item (add-decision / add-item), or flipping status (set-status) — use the structured verb. A wholesale rewrite of most of the document — use plans:set-content / set-content-chunk.
guidance.chaining: Read the current text (plans:get) → plans:edit { slug, old_string, new_string }. For several edits, call plans:edit repeatedly (each is CAS-safe on its own match).

tools.name: plans:export
tools.description: Produce a plan's canonical markdown on demand (plans are PG-canonical; markdown is rendered, not stored as tracked files). `{ slug }` returns one plan's markdown; `{ toDir }` re-materializes every plan as .md files under that directory.

guidance.when: You need the raw markdown of a plan to pipe/share, or want a one-off offline dump of all plans as files.
guidance.notWhen: You want the parsed structure (items/decisions/now) — use plans:get. You want to edit a plan — use the plans:set-* verbs (they write PG).
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:export { slug } for the markdown of any plan.

tools.name: plans:get
tools.description: Fetch the full parsed structure of one plan by slug: frontmatter, ## Now (state + next), items with effectiveStatus, decisions. Resolves archived plans too. ALWAYS pass `harness` on an operator/superuser-scoped call: use the plan's concrete harness slug (for example, 'papercusp' for Papercusp's own plans). `harness: 'all'` is only valid in an unscoped (--all-workspaces) session. Omitting it throws harness_required; a harness-scoped session supplies it automatically.

guidance.when: You have a slug from plans:list and need the plan contents. Pass `harness` on THIS call as the plan's concrete project slug (for example, `harness: 'papercusp'` for Papercusp plans) unless your session is already scoped to a harness. `harness: 'all'` is only valid in an unscoped (--all-workspaces) session; omitting harness at operator/superuser scope fails with harness_required.
guidance.notWhen: You don't know the slug — call plans:list first. Item-only queries across plans should use plans:items.
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:get { slug, harness } → optionally plans:items for cross-plan picks.

tools.name: plans:get-item
tools.description: Read ONE or MANY plan items (P-NNN) — each one's text, storedStatus + resolved effectiveStatus, importance, phase, blockedBy, and any blocking engineer-issues — from the PG-canonical structured index, WITHOUT loading + parsing the whole plan. Single: { slug, itemId }. Many of one plan: { slug, itemIds:[…] }. Cross-plan: items:[{ slug, itemId, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, item? | error }], counts } — correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; a missing item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Inspecting one or more specific P-NNN (their status / blockers / phase / importance) without pulling the whole plan. The targeted read between plans:items (many by status) and plans:get (the whole plan). Read several at once via itemIds:[…] (one plan) or items:[…] (cross-plan).
guidance.notWhen: You need the whole plan (Now / decisions / prose) — plans:get. Many items by status — plans:items.
guidance.chaining: plans:get-item { slug, itemId } → plans:set-status / plans:set-item-blocked-by / plans:set-item-phase to act on it.

tools.name: plans:get-template-data
tools.description: Read a plan's template TYPE + its STRUCTURED instance data (the `template_data` jsonb) — the structured read complement of plans:set-template-data, without parsing the markdown. Returns { template, templateData, version }; templateData is null until set. Read-only.

guidance.when: Reading a template-instance plan's structured data (e.g. a rubric instance's fields) to consume it programmatically — never scrape it out of the markdown.
guidance.notWhen: You need the whole plan (Now / items / decisions / prose) — plans:get. Writing the data — plans:set-template-data. Listing plans of a template type — plans:list { template }.
guidance.chaining: plans:get-template-data { slug } → plans:set-template-data { slug, data } to update it.

tools.name: plans:items
tools.description: Cross-plan item query. actionable=true returns pickable items (effectiveStatus="todo"). needsHuman=true returns the human's inbox. status filters by effectiveStatus. Legacy plans excluded. ALWAYS pass `harness` on an operator/superuser-scoped call (a concrete slug, or 'all' for cross-harness/Papercusp's-own-plans) — omitting it throws harness_required (a harness-scoped session supplies it automatically, so this only applies when calling from operator scope; EI-8823).

guidance.when: You want to find items by status across all plans — "what can I pick up", "what needs the human", or filter one plan's items.
guidance.notWhen: You want the full plan structure (Now block, decisions, prose) — use plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable: true } → plans:get { slug } for context on the picked item.

tools.name: plans:launch
tools.description: Launch an autonomous agent on a plan. Assembles the plan context bundle (plan doc + revision rationale), starts a resumable run, streams the agent, records it in plan_runs. Returns the run id + session id.

guidance.when: You want an agent to autonomously advance a plan — pick up its next actionable item and work it.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to read a plan (plans:get) or edit it yourself (the plans:set-* verbs). Resuming an existing run is a continue call, not a fresh launch.
guidance.chaining: plans:list / plans:get → plans:launch { slug } → the run streams; plans:runs lists past launches.

tools.name: plans:lint
tools.description: Validate plan files. Legacy plans are exempt. CI should fail on any error; warnings are informational. With `slug` or `slugs`: full per-plan reports in the standard bulk envelope. Without a slug: a BOUNDED summary across all plans (totals + per-code rollups + per-plan finding counts, with errors inlined) — warnings are collapsed to counts so the result never blows the agent size cap. Pass `full: true` for the complete per-plan dump (HTTP-safe; may overflow an agent caller on a large workspace).

guidance.when: You're editing a plan and want to verify it parses cleanly, or you're running the doc-tree health check.
guidance.notWhen: You just want to read plans — use plans:list/get.
guidance.chaining: All-plans summary flags a plan with errors → plans:lint { slug } for its full findings → plans:get { slug } for context.

tools.name: plans:list
tools.description: List SU plans under apps/operator/docs/plans/. One row per plan with title, status, item counts by effectiveStatus, and the ## Now next-action line. Legacy plans (no frontmatter) surface as status="draft" (flagged via isLegacy).

guidance.when: A directory of plans — "what plans exist / are active", or the entry point before plans:get. For RECENT plans, pass updatedSince/createdSince (ISO or "4d") + order:"updated" + limit — these filter SERVER-SIDE (PG), so do NOT fetch every plan and post-filter (that returns a huge result). For a fast scan that skips item-count resolution, add compact:true.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the plan slug and want full contents — call plans:get directly. For an ad-hoc/aggregate query no arg here exposes (group-by, joins), use dev:pg_query.
guidance.chaining: plans:list → plans:get { slug } (full plan) or plans:items { actionable: true } (pickable items across plans).

tools.name: plans:new
tools.description: Create a new plan in the plan STORE. This is the ONLY way to create a plan — never write a plan file on disk yourself (a raw file is not registered in the store and collides here). Pass `body` to author the whole plan in ONE call (frontmatter is generated for you); omit it for an empty starter template. Slug uniqueness enforced inside a lock.

guidance.when: Starting a new plan. The one-shot path: plans:new { slug, title, body } — pass the full markdown body (## Now / ## Background / ## Phase 1 items / ## Decisions) and it lands in one call, no set-content round-trip.
guidance.notWhen: You want to edit an existing plan — use plans:set-content / set-now / add-decision / add-item. Never create a plan by writing a .md file under docs/plans/ — it is not in the store; always use this tool.
guidance.chaining: Author-in-one: plans:new { slug, title, body }. Incremental: plans:new → plans:set-now → plans:add-item × N. Then plans:start to promote items to work-items.

tools.name: plans:pause
tools.description: Suspend orchestrator feature-picking for a plan. In-flight worker turns finish; no new features are picked until plans:start is called again. Returns { notStarted: true } if the plan was never started (op_status is null).

guidance.when: User pauses work on a plan from the UI, or an agent needs to suspend a plan without marking it done.
guidance.notWhen: The plan is done — use plans:set-run-status for run lifecycle. To mark the whole plan complete, update the frontmatter status to shipped.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to find the slug, then plans:pause { slug }. Resume with plans:start.

tools.name: plans:promote
tools.description: Promote a `plans:*` plan into a harness. Preview computes the per-feature covers mapping and lists assertions that would be extracted. Apply POSTs features to /features/import (server allocates F-AUTO-*), stores inline VAL-* assertions to harness_plan_assertions, and marks the plan's from_items as done. A wave declaring `spawn_child` is routed into a NEWLY-SPAWNED child harness instead (scaffold → auto-synthesized seed plan → import → start; preview reports the would-be child). Always emits a `plan_event` of kind=promoted.

guidance.when: A plan is ready to enter the harness — you and the human have settled the feature list and acceptance criteria.
guidance.notWhen: Routine plan edits — plans:set-now / plans:add-item already cover those. Mid-debate — promote only once the design is settled. ANTI-OVER-SPAWN (D-001, promote-spawn-child-harness): a `spawn_child` wave is justified ONLY when the work crosses a repo/worktree boundary or needs its own lifecycle/done-definition — same-repo sub-work stays as plain features in the current harness (the dispatcher already runs feature pipelines concurrently; a child harness buys no extra parallelism, only overhead). When in doubt, do NOT spawn.
guidance.chaining: spawn_child waves: re-run with apply:false first — the preview lists the child slug, seed plan, and feature count with zero side effects. A partially-failed spawn (see `spawned_children[].warnings`) is retried by simply re-promoting (idempotent: scaffold/seed/import/start all upsert or no-op).

tools.name: plans:resume
tools.description: Continue an existing plan-agent run. Sends a follow-up message into a run started by plans:launch, re-seeding the agent with the current plan and appending new turns to its transcript.

guidance.when: You want to continue a plan run — send a follow-up instruction to an agent already launched on a plan.
guidance.notWhen: Starting a fresh agent on a plan is plans:launch. Only reading a run’s past turns needs no agent at all.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:resume { runId, message } → the run streams further turns.

tools.name: plans:revision-diff
tools.description: Unified diff between a plan revision and its immediate predecessor — sourced from the plan_revisions snapshot pair, not git. Returns a `react-diff-view`-parseable patch string. Seq 1 returns the file-against-empty creation diff.

guidance.when: You have a revisionId from plans:revisions and want the patch — what exactly changed in that revision.
guidance.notWhen: You want a coarse git patch — that is plans:diff. The revision chain — plans:revisions. The current plan body — plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:revision-diff { revisionId } for any revision.

tools.name: plans:revision-transcript
tools.description: The conversation behind a plan revision — scoped: paginated by cursor, narrowable by query, never a whole-transcript dump. Returns turns from the plan-run transcript; revisions from a direct editor save or a git backfill report available:false.

guidance.when: You need the reasoning behind a specific revision — the raw conversation, drilled into around a decision via query/cursor.
guidance.notWhen: You want the revision list with rationales — plans:revisions. You want the plan body — plans:get. Never pull a whole transcript unscoped.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:revision-transcript { revisionId, query } → page with cursor.

tools.name: plans:revisions
tools.description: The revision chain for a plan, newest-first — one row per recorded plans:* write: seq, author (agent|human), the rationale, the session that produced it, a +/- diff-stat vs the prior revision, and timestamp. The conversation-linked counterpart to plans:history (git commits). Empty chain when the plan has no recorded revisions yet.

guidance.when: You need a plan's edit history with the *why* — what changed at each revision and the rationale behind it. The basis of the Revisions panel and of the context an agent launched from the plan is seeded with.
guidance.notWhen: You want raw git commit history of the file — that is plans:history. The current plan body — plans:get.
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions → plans:diff for a coarse git patch, or (Phase 2) the per-revision transcript verb for the conversation behind a revision.

tools.name: plans:run-now
tools.description: Fire one run of a scheduled plan immediately (a manual run), independent of its cadence — mints an instance plan + plan_runs row + run-scoped work items, like a scheduled fire.

guidance.when: Manually triggering a run of a scheduled plan now — testing the schedule, or an out-of-band run.
guidance.notWhen: Changing the cadence (plans:set-schedule). Launching a plan as an interactive chat session (plans:launch).
guidance.chaining: plans:set-schedule (author) → plans:run-now (fire one) → plans:runs (inspect the runs).

tools.name: plans:run-transcript
tools.description: A paginated slice of a plan run's transcript — turns ordered by seq; substring-filterable, never a whole dump. The data behind the Agents-tab run-detail view.

guidance.when: You want to inspect the back-and-forth of an existing run — e.g. find a specific turn before resuming.
guidance.notWhen: You want the run launches list (plans:runs), the conversation behind a plan revision (plans:revision-transcript), or to continue the run (plans:resume).
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:run-transcript { runId } → page with cursor.

tools.name: plans:runs
tools.description: The launch history for a plan, newest-first — one row per agent launched from it: run id, title, status, who launched it and when, the launch note, the seeded content hash, the session id, and a transcript turn count. Empty list when the plan has never been launched.

guidance.when: You want to see the agents launched from a plan — the past-runs list, or to find a runId to resume.
guidance.notWhen: You want to launch a fresh agent — plans:launch. You want to read the plan body — plans:get. The plan’s edit history — plans:revisions.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:resume { runId, message } to continue a run.

tools.name: plans:search
tools.description: Search across SU plans by keyword. Scopes: slug, title, now, items, decisions, prose. Includes archived + legacy by default. A slug (or slug fragment) finds the plan it names — not only plans that mention it.

guidance.when: You're looking for prior work, decisions, or items by topic and don't have a slug — or you have a slug fragment and want the plan it names.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the full exact slug — use plans:get (a direct PG key read). For full prose recall across the project (chats, escalations), use search:fulltext.
guidance.chaining: plans:search { query } → plans:get { slug } on the top hit.

tools.name: plans:set-content
tools.description: Replace a plan file wholesale, guarded by a compare-and-swap on `expectedHash`. For raw-prose edits the structured verbs cannot make. Rejects a stale write (file changed since load), a write that would strip a real plan back to legacy, and a write that fails lint. A successful write is recorded as a plan revision; pass `rationale` to capture the why. For large plan bodies, use plans:set-content-chunk instead so the provider sends multiple small tool calls.

guidance.when: A human is editing the raw markdown of a plan — prose sections the assisted verbs (set-now / set-status / add-decision / add-item) do not cover. Use only for small-to-medium bodies that fit comfortably in one tool call.
guidance.notWhen: A structured edit — flipping an item, replacing the Now block, appending a decision/item — use the assisted verb. Converting a legacy plan — use plans:set-frontmatter. Writing a large plan body — use plans:set-content-chunk begin → append* → commit.
guidance.chaining: plans:get { slug } → carry `contentHash` → plans:set-content { slug, content, expectedHash: contentHash }. For large bodies: plans:set-content-chunk begin → append* → commit.

tools.name: plans:set-content-chunk
tools.description: Stage a large plans:set-content rewrite through small chunks. Use begin with expectedHash, append each markdown chunk, then commit. Commit validates/lints/CAS-writes exactly like plans:set-content and records one revision. Use this instead of plans:set-content for large plan bodies that may trip provider/tool-call limits.

guidance.when: Writing or rewriting a large plan body. If the plan markdown is more than a few screens, use begin → append* → commit with chunks under 24k characters instead of sending one huge plans:set-content call.
guidance.notWhen: Small raw-prose edits — plans:set-content is simpler. Structured edits — use plans:set-now / plans:set-status / plans:add-decision / plans:add-item.
guidance.chaining: plans:get { slug } → plans:set-content-chunk { op:"begin", slug, expectedHash: contentHash, chunk:firstPart, rationale } → append remaining chunks → commit. If commit returns stale, plans:get again and restart the draft.

tools.name: plans:set-decision-body
tools.description: Replace an existing decision's body — preserves the `### D-NNN — title` head and the `Date:` line, replaces everything else with the new body. Inside the plan lock, records a revision. The structured editor decisions lacked (plans:add-decision could only append; editing meant a plans:edit string-replace).

guidance.when: A decision's body needs revising — a correction, a clarification, an added caveat — keeping its id, title, and date. The structured alternative to a plans:edit on the decision block.
guidance.notWhen: Recording a NEW decision (plans:add-decision). Changing a decision title (plans:edit — title lives on the head line). A whole-document rewrite (plans:set-content).
guidance.chaining: plans:get (the decision body) → plans:set-decision-body → plans:get to confirm.

tools.name: plans:set-frontmatter
tools.description: Convert a legacy plan (no valid frontmatter) into a first-class plan by writing a complete `title`/`slug`/`created`/`updated`/`status`/`owner` block. Body untouched. Refuses a plan that already has valid frontmatter.

guidance.when: Promoting a legacy plan — one with no/malformed frontmatter — to a tracked plan, e.g. from the Plans admin tab triage screen.
guidance.notWhen: Editing a plan that already has valid frontmatter — that would clobber keys this verb does not model; use plans:set-content for a deliberate raw edit. Routine status flips on items use plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:list (isLegacy: true rows) → plans:set-frontmatter per plan → plans:get to confirm.

tools.name: plans:set-frontmatter-field
tools.description: Set or clear an ARBITRARY plan frontmatter key (e.g. `template`) — surgical (other keys preserved), inside the plan lock, records a revision + refreshes the plans list. The generic setter custom fields lacked (vs a raw plans:edit string-replace). Pass value:null to clear. RESERVED keys (slug/title/status/created/updated/owner/co_owners/initiative) are rejected with a pointer to their dedicated setter. Refuses a legacy plan — convert with plans:set-frontmatter first.

guidance.when: Setting a custom/template frontmatter field that has no dedicated setter (e.g. template:rubric) — the structured alternative to a plans:edit string-replace on the frontmatter.
guidance.notWhen: A reserved/managed key — use its dedicated setter (status→plans:set-plan-status, owner/co_owners→plans:transfer-owner, initiative→plans:set-initiative, slug/title/created→plans:set-frontmatter). A whole-document edit — plans:set-content. Converting a legacy (no-frontmatter) plan — plans:set-frontmatter.
guidance.chaining: plans:get (mode:meta) to see current frontmatter → plans:set-frontmatter-field → plans:get to confirm.

tools.name: plans:set-importance
tools.description: Change one OR many items' importance (urgent|high|normal|low). Adds/replaces the trailing `importance:` keyword; setting `normal` removes it. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:. Single: { slug, itemId, importance }. Many of one plan: { slug, itemIds:[…], importance }. Heterogeneous: items:[{ slug, itemId, importance }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, … | error }], counts } — correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An item's importance changes — escalating a stuck or aging item, or correcting a level set wrong at creation. Re-rank several at once via itemIds:[…] (one plan) or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Setting importance when creating an item — that's plans:add-item's required arg. Changing lifecycle status — plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:items (sorted urgent→low) → plans:set-importance to re-rank what the human sees first.

tools.name: plans:set-initiative
tools.description: Set or clear a plan's `initiative` grouping label — a single free-text frontmatter field that groups related plans (surfaced as a filter facet in the plans list). Surgical frontmatter edit (other keys preserved), inside the plan lock, records a revision + refreshes the plans list. Pass `initiative: null` to clear. Refuses a legacy plan — convert it with plans:set-frontmatter first.

guidance.when: Grouping a set of related plans under one initiative label so they filter together in the plans list — or clearing/renaming that label.
guidance.notWhen: Transferring ownership / co-owners — plans:transfer-owner. Converting a legacy (no-frontmatter) plan — plans:set-frontmatter. A whole-document raw edit — plans:set-content.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to see existing initiative labels → plans:set-initiative per plan → plans:list to confirm the facet.

tools.name: plans:set-item-blocked-by
tools.description: Set or clear one OR many items' `blocked-by:` dependency list — surgical (only the target item line's keyword changes; status/text/importance preserved), inside the plan lock, records a revision. Pass blockedBy:[] to clear. Single: { slug, itemId, blockedBy }. Many of one plan: { slug, itemIds:[…], blockedBy }. Heterogeneous: items:[{ slug, itemId, blockedBy }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, from, to | error }], counts } — correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An item's dependencies change — a new prerequisite surfaced, or a blocker cleared (blockedBy:[] to un-block). The structured alternative to a plans:edit on the item line. Set several at once via itemIds:[…] (one plan) or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Flipping lifecycle status (plans:set-status) or importance (plans:set-importance). Moving an item to another phase (plans:set-item-phase).
guidance.chaining: plans:get-item { slug, itemId } to see current blockers → plans:set-item-blocked-by.

tools.name: plans:set-item-phase
tools.description: Move one OR many items to a different phase — relocates the whole item line under the target `## Phase …` heading (an item's phase is positional, not an inline keyword), every token preserved. Creates the phase section if it doesn't exist. No-op when already there. Inside the plan lock, records a revision. Single: { slug, itemId, phase }. Many of one plan: { slug, itemIds:[…], phase }. Heterogeneous: items:[{ slug, itemId, phase }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, fromPhase, toPhase, moved, createdPhase | error }], counts } — correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An item belongs under a different phase — re-sequencing work across phases, or correcting a mis-placed item. The structured alternative to manually cutting + pasting the line with plans:edit. Move several at once via itemIds:[…] (one plan) or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Adding a NEW item (plans:add-item — it takes the phase directly). Changing status/importance/blockers (their dedicated setters). Renaming a phase heading itself (plans:edit / plans:set-content).
guidance.chaining: plans:get-item { slug, itemId } to see the current phase → plans:set-item-phase.

tools.name: plans:set-now
tools.description: Replace the `## Now` block atomically. The Now block is the cold-resume anchor — the single most-read field, NOT a log: keep State ≤2000 chars + Next ≤800 (trim hard; long-form backlog/history/design detail belongs in the plan body via plans:set-content / set-content-chunk, not the Now block). Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:.

guidance.when: Plan state advances meaningfully — phase boundaries, blocking discovery, finishing a chunk of work, picking up a new direction.
guidance.notWhen: Per-item flip — that's plans:set-status. Or a decision — that's plans:add-decision.
guidance.chaining: plans:set-status to flip current item → plans:set-now reflecting the new state. Keep State ≤2000 chars / Next ≤800 — if either overflows, trim it and offload the detail to plans:set-content / set-content-chunk rather than retrying a too-long Now.

tools.name: plans:set-plan-status
tools.description: Flip a plan's lifecycle status (draft→ready approve, ready→draft demote, →shipped, →superseded reject). Plan-level frontmatter, not an item's status. Also the Queen↔Scout DEPRECATE handler: pass `learnings` with status='superseded' to also emit a salvage observation into Scout's digest (no dead ends) — see guidance.

guidance.when: Moving a whole plan through its lifecycle: approving a reviewed draft (draft→ready, which unlocks Start), demoting an approved plan back to draft, shipping it, or rejecting it (→superseded). DEPRECATING a Mug↔Blender draft that won't reach ready: status='superseded' + `learnings:{tried,stalled,salvageable}` — one atomic call deprecates AND records the salvage observation (don't file a separate improvements:capture).
guidance.notWhen: Flipping a P-NNN item's status — use plans:set-status. Converting a legacy plan that has no valid frontmatter — use plans:set-frontmatter first (this verb refuses it with no_status_line). `learnings` on a non-superseded status is ignored (it is a deprecate-only field).
guidance.chaining: plans:get (read current status) → plans:set-plan-status { slug, status: 'ready', expectedCurrent: 'draft' } to approve. Approving is optional before plans:start — starting a draft auto-approves it (draft→ready). Deprecate: plans:set-plan-status { slug, status:'superseded', learnings:{…} } → the returned learningsObservation reports the emitted observation.

tools.name: plans:set-priority
tools.description: Set the cross-plan dispatch priority for a started plan. Lower = dispatched first. The drag-to-reorder UI calls this automatically; agents can also call it when explicit ordering matters.

guidance.when: User drags a started plan to a new position in the Plans rail, or explicitly asks "do plan A before plan B".
guidance.notWhen: For pausing a plan, use plans:pause. For the run lifecycle, use plans:set-run-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to see started plans and their current priorities.

tools.name: plans:set-run-status
tools.description: Manually transition a plan run's status — archive it (set aside, still resumable), mark it done (deliberately concluded), or set it idle (un-archive / reopen). A run that is currently running is rejected. Distinct from plans:set-status, which is for plan items.

guidance.when: You want to archive a finished run, mark a run done, or un-archive one — a deliberate lifecycle change a human/agent makes.
guidance.notWhen: The run is mid-turn (let it settle, or resume it). Flipping a plan *item* status is plans:set-status. Continuing a run is plans:resume.
guidance.chaining: plans:runs → plans:set-run-status { runId, status }.

tools.name: plans:set-schedule
tools.description: Author or clear a plan's schedule — make it recurring (RRULE or cron), one-shot (scheduledAt), and/or give it an expiry. Validates the RRULE. Does NOT arm it (arming is the autonomy-gated flow); pass schedule:null to un-schedule.

guidance.when: Turning a plan into a scheduled/recurring one, editing its cadence/expiry, or clearing its schedule.
guidance.notWhen: Arming a saved schedule so it starts firing — that is the autonomy-gated arm step, not authoring. Flipping plan/item status uses plans:set-plan-status / plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:set-schedule → (arm, autonomy-gated) → the routines engine fires system:plan-run; plans:run-now to fire one manually.

tools.name: plans:set-status
tools.description: Flip one OR many items' stored status. Writes the exact bytes a human would type. Auto-bumps frontmatter updated:. Flipping to `wip` AUTO-CLAIMS the item for you; flipping to done/dropped releases your claim AND clears the item's assignment. Both are rejected with a per-item claim_conflict if a LIVE peer holds the item (you cannot claim or close someone else's in-flight work — coordinate or let the holder close it). Single: { slug, itemId, status }. Many of one plan: { slug, itemIds:[…], status }. Heterogeneous: items:[{ slug, itemId, status }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, slug, itemId, oldStatus, newStatus, … | error }], counts } — correlate by { slug, itemId }, not position; a claim_conflict (or any failure) on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: An item's status changes — picking up (todo→wip, which also claims the item as yours), completing (wip→done, which releases it), gating on a human (→needs-human), or recording external blockage (→blocked). Flip several at once via itemIds:[…] (one plan) or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want to add a brand-new item — use plans:add-item. Or to change scope of the work — edit the item text directly in the file.
guidance.chaining: plans:items { actionable: true } → plans:set-status { itemId, status: "wip" } when picking up (the wip flip claims it — no separate plan_items:claim needed). On a per-item claim_conflict: coord:send the holder or pick another item.

tools.name: plans:set-template-data
tools.description: Write a plan's STRUCTURED template instance data (the `template_data` jsonb), validated against its template TYPE's code-registry zod schema on write (validate-on-write). The plan must already declare a `template:` type (plans:set-frontmatter-field). Rejects fail-loud on an unknown type (no schema registered) or a schema violation — never silently strips. Advisory-locked, version-bumped, and recorded as a plan revision. Agents read/write the instance data structured here, never as markdown.

guidance.when: Writing/updating a template-instance plan's structured data (e.g. a rubric instance's fields) — the validated, revisioned setter for the `template_data` jsonb.
guidance.notWhen: Declaring WHICH template type a plan is (the `template:` frontmatter) — use plans:set-frontmatter-field. Editing the plan's prose/items — plans:set-content / the assisted verbs. Reading the data back — plans:get-template-data.
guidance.chaining: plans:set-frontmatter-field { key:"template", value:"<type>" } (declare the type) → plans:set-template-data { slug, data } → plans:get-template-data to confirm.

tools.name: plans:start
tools.description: Mark a plan as started so the orchestrator will pick features promoted from it. Starting is itself the approval signal — a still-draft plan is auto-advanced to 'ready'. Starting an already-started plan is a no-op. Use plans:pause to suspend work without losing started state.

guidance.when: User clicks 'Start Plan' in the harness UI, or an agent is asked to begin work on a specific plan.
guidance.notWhen: The plan is already started. Use plans:pause to suspend, plans:set-run-status for run lifecycle.
guidance.chaining: plans:list to find the slug, then plans:start { slug }.

tools.name: plans:summarize-revision
tools.description: Fill in a revision's missing rationale by summarising the conversation behind it on the haiku model. Best-effort and idempotent — a revision that already has a rationale, or has no plan-run transcript, is reported back unchanged.

guidance.when: A revision from a plan-run session has no rationale and you want the "why" filled in — for the Revisions panel or a richer launch-context digest.
guidance.notWhen: The revision already has a rationale. The revision is a direct editor save or a git backfill (no conversation to summarise).
guidance.chaining: plans:revisions (spot a rationale-less row) → plans:summarize-revision { revisionId }.

tools.name: plans:transfer-owner
tools.description: Transfer a plan's ownership (set `owner`) and/or its `co_owners` list — the explicit, first-class handoff verb. Surgical frontmatter edit (other keys preserved), inside the plan lock, records a revision + refreshes the plans list. Pass `to` (new owner email) and/or `coOwners` (replaces the list; [] clears). Refuses a legacy plan — convert it with plans:set-frontmatter first.

guidance.when: Explicitly handing a plan to another user, or setting its co-owners, in a shared hive — so ownership is unambiguous instead of an opaque set-content edit.
guidance.notWhen: Converting a legacy (no-frontmatter) plan — plans:set-frontmatter. A whole-document raw edit — plans:set-content. Flipping an item status — plans:set-status.
guidance.chaining: plans:get { slug } to see the current owner first; plans:list to confirm the transfer landed on the rail.

tools.name: platform:contribute
tools.description: Send a local improvement UPSTREAM from a platform-mode install. kind:'learning-pack' exports the self-hive's organic learnings + lists them on the Comb (lands PENDING — operator-moderated); kind:'pr' pushes the change to the USER'S FORK and opens a human-reviewed PR fork→canonical Papercusp (never a direct push). Root-only, reason-audited. By default it PREPARES but does not send: the live push/PR/publish fires ONLY with confirm:true AND credentials/remote present, else returns {ok, prepared:true, needs:[...]}.

guidance.when: The user explicitly wants to contribute a platform-mode improvement UPSTREAM to Papercusp — publish a learning-pack to the Comb, or open a fork→canonical PR. Requires platform:enable first (the self-hive must be standing).
guidance.notWhen: Enabling platform mode / standing up the self-hive — platform:enable. Publishing a pack for an ARBITRARY (non-platform) hive — learning_packs:export + learning_packs:publish. Opening a PR for a normal harness feature — the orchestrator fork-PR hook.
guidance.chaining: platform:enable (stand up the self-hive) → set the self-hive member's fork_remote (for kind:'pr') → platform:contribute (prepared) → review the plan/needs → platform:contribute { confirm:true } to send.

tools.name: platform:dogfood_verify
tools.description: Assert the internal fork→PR dogfood loop round-tripped for a contributed PR: reads the WI↔PR producer row, the agent-review report, the merged state, and the completion_ref ship-stamp, and returns {ok, stages, featureId, gaps}. `ok` is true iff every required leg (prTracked, merged, shipped, linked) passed; the agent-review leg is optional. Read-only.

guidance.when: After a member fork→PR contribution (platform:contribute) has been reviewed + merged, to confirm the whole loop closed — the WI shows shipped + linked PR. The brief's Done check.
guidance.notWhen: Opening the PR — platform:contribute. Listing PRs — the PRs tab. Tidying forks — platform:fork_gc.
guidance.chaining: platform:enable → platform:contribute {kind:'pr'} → (the system:pr-poll daemon reviews/merges) → platform:dogfood_verify { prUrl } to assert ok:true.

tools.name: platform:enable
tools.description: Opt INTO platform mode ("Papercusp inside Papercusp"): flip the PLATFORM_IMPROVEMENT_LOOPS knob on for this install, stand Papercusp's OWN repo up as a self-managed shared Hive (kind:'hive') via fetch-on-enable from the public repo, and arm the layer-3 platform-improvement loops (seeded DARK — arm each via the gym/routines UI). The self-hive inherits its own gym+scout loop. Root-only, reason-audited. Returns {ok, flagEnabled, selfHive, armedLoops, summary}.

guidance.when: The user explicitly opts into platform mode / "Papercusp inside Papercusp" / wants this install to improve Papercusp-the-platform itself (layer 3). One call stands up the self-hive + arms the loops.
guidance.notWhen: Onboarding an ARBITRARY repo as a hive — pot:create_from_repo. Just flipping a flag without standing up the self-hive — flags:set. Contributing an improvement UPSTREAM (open a PR / publish a learning-pack) — platform:contribute (the separate, gated path).
guidance.chaining: platform:enable → improvements:learning_loops to see the armed (dark) layer-3 loops → arm the watchdog via the routines admin → platform:contribute to send an improvement upstream.

tools.name: platform:fork_gc
tools.description: Collect ABANDONED contribution forks under the operator's account (the fork→PR path forks the upstream and never tears it down). KEEP-on-merge + stale-fork GC: never deletes an active fork (open PR) or a recently-pushed one, never another account's repo. DRY RUN by default — pass confirm:true to actually delete (needs the gh delete_repo scope). Root-only. Returns {ok, dryRun, evaluations, wouldCollect|collected, errors}.

guidance.when: The operator wants to clean up dormant forks left behind by the fork→PR contribution path (e.g. after dogfooding, or on a periodic tidy). Default (no confirm) just REPORTS the abandoned forks.
guidance.notWhen: Opening/merging a PR — that is the fork-PR hook / prs review route. Removing a hive membership — hive tooling. Deleting a repo you actively contribute to — this never collects a fork with an open PR.
guidance.chaining: platform:fork_gc (dry-run report) → review wouldCollect → platform:fork_gc { confirm:true } to delete the abandoned forks.

tools.name: plugins:fire_event
tools.description: Fire a free-form plugin event or typed lifecycle hook via the in-process host. Diagnostic — architect/operator only.

guidance.when: Synthetically fire a hook event so the registered plugin / role pipelines run their handlers. Useful for replaying / testing event-driven flows.
guidance.notWhen: For NORMAL flow, events fire from real actions (commit, plan-approved, etc.); only use this when you need to manually trigger them. For listing PENDING events, use `pending_events:list`.

tools.name: plugins:invoke_action
tools.description: Invoke a plugin action via the in-process registry. Diagnostic — architect/operator only.

guidance.when: Invoke a named action a plugin exposes (publish, sync, etc.). Use the action name from `plugins:runtime_status`.
guidance.notWhen: For TOOLS the plugin exposes (callable as MCP names), call them directly via their mcp__ prefix. Actions are plugin-lifecycle verbs; tools are the catalog.

tools.name: plugins:runtime_status
tools.description: Read the plugin host runtime status (loaded plugins, registered actions, mounted api routes).

guidance.when: You need to know which plugins are loaded + healthy in the current operator process (per-harness or workspace-level).
guidance.notWhen: For the plugin CATALOG (everything installable), use the marketplace endpoints. plugins:runtime_status is the runtime view.

tools.name: plugins:tui_panes
tools.description: List the capability-gated tui-pane UI contributions for a harness (pluginName, slug, label, command, cwd). The pui opens these in a zellij pane.

guidance.when: The pui (or an agent) needs the TUI panes (type:'tui-pane' UI contributions) a harness's enabled plugins offer, to open one in a terminal pane.
guidance.notWhen: For desktop UI surfaces (react/iframe) or the full plugin runtime status, use plugins:runtime_status.

tools.name: pot:add-member
tools.description: Wire an existing harness in as a MEMBER of a local pot (sets its hive_slug so its work federates within the pot and surfaces in the Mug's member-scoped pot:survey). Registry edit only — never moves the harness folder or run data; best-effort seeds the member's git-sync routine. Idempotent (re-adding is a no-op success). Use this to remediate a member-less pot whose Mug surveys workspace-wide and escalates out-of-scope debris.

guidance.when: A pot has no members so pot:survey falls back to workspace-wide scope (frontier empty / Mug-unresolvable escalations) — wire the real harness in. Also the producer for shared-pot federation membership.
guidance.notWhen: Adding a person/device to a pot (that is admission, a separate concern). Removing a member (re-point via the registry / pot:leave for a joined remote pot). Nesting a pot home as a member (rejected — pots compose as peers).
guidance.chaining: pot:list / pot:get to find the pot home + the member slug → pot:add-member → pot:start (or pot:wake) so the Mug surveys the now-scoped frontier → pot:survey to confirm members[] is non-empty + scope is pot-local.

tools.name: pot:ask
tools.description: Initiate a cross-Pot ASK to a peer Pot (by pubkey): a question the peer Pot owns the answer to. The envelope is signed, sent store-and-forward, and recorded in this Pot's ask ledger; the peer's answer arrives asynchronously — events:await the returned answeredEvent key. Requires an outbound grant to the peer.

guidance.when: The Mug/owner needs an answer another Pot is the authority on (it owns that domain). Find the peer via discovery:pots, then pot:ask, then events:await the returned answeredEvent.
guidance.notWhen: Handing the peer WORK to do (use pot:request_work). Within-Pot questions (coord:ask / conversations). Granting a peer to send asks INTO this Pot (that is the inbound pot:cross_grant).
guidance.chaining: discovery:pots (find the peer Pot pubkey) → pot:ask { pot, peerPotPubkey, subject, body } → events:await { event: <answeredEvent> }. Review outstanding asks with pot:asks.

tools.name: pot:asks
tools.description: List this Pot's cross-Pot ask ledger: the requests it initiated to peer Pots (and inbound ones with direction:'in'), with each row's peer, kind, subject, correlation id, state (queued|sent|answered|declined|expired) and reply. Filter by state / direction / peer / kind.

guidance.when: Reviewing the status of cross-Pot asks/work-requests — what is still pending, what was answered/declined — or deduping before initiating a new ask to a peer that already owns one.
guidance.notWhen: Inbound admission policy (pot:cross_grant list shows who may send INTO this Pot). Within-Pot work status (work_items:* / harness:status). Blocking on one specific pending ask (events:await its answeredEvent — do not poll this list).
guidance.chaining: pot:ask / pot:request_work create rows here; pot:asks { pot, state: "answered" } reviews the replies.

tools.name: pot:ban_member
tools.description: OWNER bans a member for repeat abuse: records the ban in the owner-signed policy (denies re-join, keyed on the stable github id) AND revokes their devices (write-block now; a READ cut-off at the next C-001 re-key epoch). Pass unban:true to lift. Requires holding the Pot key. revoke:false bans (policy-only) without revoking.

guidance.when: A member is a confirmed repeat abuser (see pot:moderation_queue) and you (the owner) want them removed AND unable to re-join.
guidance.notWhen: Hiding one piece of content — that is pot:takedown. Revoking your OWN device — substrate:revoke_self_device.
guidance.chaining: pot:moderation_queue → pot:ban_member → pot:moderation_resolve (mark actioned). The read cut-off completes when the C-001 re-key op-path lands.

tools.name: pot:beacon_consent
tools.description: Manage whether THIS Pot publishes a live status beacon (active agents, queue depth, focus, last-completed) onto the directory gossip — the owner-consent gate, default-OFF (D-002). Pass `consent` to set it (true = publish, false = stop); omit `consent` to read the current state. The consent federates to every Swarm of the Pot and gates B-06's beacon publisher. The beacon only rides a PUBLISHED (public/invite) pot's re-announce — enabling it on a private pot has no effect until the pot is published.

guidance.when: Enabling, disabling, or checking this Pot's status-beacon publishing — the same consent the desktop publish-flow asks for, managed from the agent surface. Pass consent:true to opt a published pot into the beacon, consent:false to withdraw it, or omit consent to read the current value.
guidance.notWhen: Directory visibility (public/invite/private) — that's discovery:set_pot. Cross-Pot ask/work-request grants — pot:cross_grant. Within-Pot coordination — coord:* / topics.
guidance.chaining: discovery:set_pot { visibility:'public' } (make the pot discoverable) → pot:beacon_consent { pot, consent:true } (opt the now-public pot into the live beacon).

tools.name: pot:control_policy
tools.description: Read or set the pot placement-watchdog thresholds: breakerThreshold (failed placements → cursed-item breaker), recoveryDebounceMs (min gap between recovery wakes for one stalled unit), dormancyGraceMs (post-dormancy recovery-sweep grace), infraBreakerThreshold (bounded infra-loss breaker). Replaces the PAPERCUSP_HIVE_PLACEMENT_* env gates; set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune the placement watchdog live — e.g. raise breakerThreshold to give a flapping unit more recovery attempts before cursing it, or shorten recoveryDebounceMs to re-place stalled work faster during an incident.
guidance.notWhen: For placement AFFINITY weights use pot:set-steering (D-005). For stale-claim reclaim use work_items:reclaim_config; for session reaping use coord:session_reaper_config.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: pot:create
tools.description: Stand up a NEW local pot (root-only): provision a home harness running the pot (kind:'hive') blueprint, stamp it harness_kind:'hive', and optionally wake the Mug. Composes the harness-provision primitives + pot:wake, transactional with rollback. NOT callable from a cup/parented agent — pots are peers, never nested. Cloud placement is a separate step (deploy:pot).

guidance.when: Standing up a NEW local pot (its home harness + Mug) in one call. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Deploying an EXISTING pot to a cloud frame — deploy:pot. A plain non-pot harness — harness:create. From a cup — not allowed (spin a kind:harness subharness instead).
guidance.chaining: pot:get { slug } to inspect; pot:declare-wake to set the cadence; deploy:pot to place it on a Swarm; pot:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: pot:create_from_repo
tools.description: Create a pot FROM a GitHub URL: repo→Pot lookup first (an existing Pot returns a JOIN OFFER, zero side effects), then clone, blueprint detect + test-verify, pot home + first member harness, upstream coords stamped, auto-publish. Visibility is derived from the repo: public repo → discoverable directory listing; private repo → Private (invite-only, hidden, secret-gated). Returns {ok, existing?} or {ok, created:{potSlug, memberSlug, memberPath}, publish}.

guidance.when: Onboarding a GitHub repository as a NEW pot in one call — the paste-a-URL creation flow. Also the backend the CreateHarnessPicker GitHub-URL entry drives.
guidance.notWhen: The repo may already have a Pot and you only want the answer — lookup happens inside, but a read-only check is the picker flow. An existing LOCAL repo — harness:generate-from-repo. A repo-less pot — pot:create. Adding a repo into an EXISTING pot — harness:create { pot } after cloning (the into-pot picker mode).
guidance.chaining: pot:create_from_repo { githubUrl } → on {existing} drive the join (POST /api/harness/join-link per member link) → on {created} pot:get / discovery:set_pot to edit the listing.

tools.name: pot:cross_grant
tools.description: Owner-managed cross-Pot grants: grant/revoke/list which peer-Pot pubkeys may exchange which kinds (ask | work-request) with this Pot. DIRECTED: 'in' admits a peer's traffic INTO this Pot; 'out' lets THIS Pot send to a peer (required before the Mug can ask another Pot). Default-deny both ways; grants are quota-capped (maxPerHour/maxBodyBytes, defaults 60/hr + 64KiB), optionally expiring (expiresInHours), and federate to all of this Pot's Swarms.

guidance.when: Setting this Pot's cross-Pot policy — grant 'in' (admission) or 'out' (egress; owner-gated before the Mug's first pot:ask to a new peer), list, or revoke. maxPerHour/maxBodyBytes/expiresInHours tune quota/expiry.
guidance.notWhen: Within-Pot coordination (coord:*/topics) or Swarm work placement (work_items:co_locate) — this is only the sovereignty boundary between Pots.
guidance.chaining: discovery:pots (peer pubkey) → pot:cross_grant {action:"grant", direction, peerPotPubkey, kinds}; "out" before pot:ask / pot:request_work.

tools.name: pot:declare-wake
tools.description: Declare the pot operator's next wake (REPLACE semantics — omitted parts are cleared): a time (`at` ISO / `inSeconds`), event subscriptions (`events: [{on, when?, note?}]`), both, or nothing (`mode:'none'`). The time is clamped to a wake floor; event wakes fire pot:wake when the subscribed tool-event matches.

guidance.when: You are the pot/operator ending a turn — ALWAYS declare your next wake (a time, events, or explicitly none). Also when the user asks to schedule or re-schedule the operator.
guidance.notWhen: To fire the pot right now — that is pot:wake.
guidance.chaining: pot:status to inspect the current declaration; pot:wake for an immediate manual fire.

tools.name: pot:dissolve
tools.description: Tear down a local pot (root-only, destructive — pass confirm:true): clear the Mug's wake so it won't re-wake, cancel every live cup + its subtree, and deregister the home harness. Optionally drop the harness PG schema (default keep). Idempotent. Does NOT destroy a deployed cloud frame — that is deploy:teardown_pot.

guidance.when: Permanently tearing down a local pot — stop the Mug, cancel its cups, deregister it. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Destroying a deployed cloud frame (the Mug/member execution planes) — deploy:teardown_pot. Pausing a pot without tearing down — pot:declare-wake { mode:none }. From a cup — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: pot:get { slug } to inspect before; deploy:teardown_pot first if the pot is deployed to a Swarm.

tools.name: pot:get
tools.description: The full state of one pot: its home harness + deployment + wake schedule (scheduled?, next/last fire, event subscriptions), its live cups with {doing, queued, load}, and its todo-work frontier depth. Composes resolvePot + fleet:assignments + work_items — the one call for "how is pot X doing".

guidance.when: You want one pot in depth: is the Mug scheduled to wake, who are the cups and how loaded, how much work is queued.
guidance.notWhen: A list of all pots — pot:list. The raw per-agent fleet view across the workspace — fleet:assignments.
guidance.chaining: pot:list to find the slug; pot:wake to fire the Mug now; pot:declare-wake to change the cadence; pot:dissolve to tear it down.

tools.name: pot:get-steering
tools.description: Read the current owner steering for the pot — the focus `directive`, `eligiblePlans` (plans the Mug may pick up now), and pause state (`pauseNewWork` / `pausedUntil`) the Mug reads on every wake. An un-steered pot returns the default (no directive, no plan restriction, not paused). Also returns `inconsistent: true` (EI-8277) when the directive text reads like the pause was lifted but `pauseNewWork` is still true — a drift nothing else catches; reconcile with pot:set-steering if the owner meant to resume. The READ twin of pot:set-steering.

guidance.when: Checking what the Mug is currently steered toward — before changing it, or to confirm a pot:set-steering write landed.
guidance.notWhen: Changing steering — pot:set-steering. Reading the whole pot status — pot:status.

tools.name: pot:leave
tools.description: Leave a shared pot you JOINED (root-only, pass confirm:true): stop federating (leave the swarm topic), delete the member git-sync routines, drop local presence rows, and deregister the remote_hive view + its member clones. Idempotent + best-effort. Clone dirs are kept by default — deleteClones:true also removes them. NOT for a local pot you own — that is pot:dissolve.

guidance.when: A joiner cleanly leaving a shared pot they joined — stop federating, deregister the joined view + members, kill their git-sync routines. Operator/user only.
guidance.notWhen: Tearing down a LOCAL pot you OWN (stop its Mug, cancel its cups) — pot:dissolve. Pausing federation without leaving — there is no pause; leave + re-join. From a cup — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: pot:list / pot:get to find the joined pot (remote_hive) view slug before; re-join via the pot directory join flow if you change your mind.

tools.name: pot:list
tools.description: The workspace-local pots (kind:'hive' harnesses — the Pots): each with its home slug, deployment target, wake (scheduled? next/last fire), and a live-agent count. The local-lifecycle view; for joinable network hives use discovery:pots, for per-cup placement detail use fleet:assignments, for one pot in depth use pot:get.

guidance.when: You want the workspace-local pots (the Pots) and their wake/load at a glance.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing joinable hives across the P2P network — that is discovery:pots. The raw per-agent fleet view — fleet:assignments. One pot in depth — pot:get.
guidance.chaining: pot:get { slug } to drill into one; pot:create to add one; pot:dissolve to tear one down.

tools.name: pot:membership_decide
tools.description: OWNER decision on one OR many pending-join requests for a Pot: approve (trust-admit the joiner + their captured devices) or deny (never admitted). Pass a single `{ githubUserId, decision, reason? }` for one or `items:[{ githubUserId, decision, reason? }]` for several. Requires this Swarm to hold the Pot key (the owning Swarm). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, githubUserId, … | error }], counts } — correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: Joiner(s) are pending under approval-mode membership (see pot:membership_pending) and you (the owner) want to admit or reject them. Clearing a queue? Pass them all via `items:[{ githubUserId, decision }]`.
guidance.notWhen: Banning an already-admitted member for abuse — use pot:ban_member (revoke + re-key teeth). Setting the membership mode itself — that is pot policy.
guidance.chaining: pot:membership_pending (review the queue) → pot:membership_decide (per joiner, or all at once via items[]). Bulk: correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: pot:membership_pending
tools.description: List a Pot's pending-join requests (the approval-mode admission queue). Under membership:'approval' a joiner stays pending until the owner approves; this is the owner's review queue. Read-only — decide with pot:membership_decide.

guidance.when: The Pot's membership policy is 'approval' and you (the owner) want to see who's waiting to join. Pair with pot:membership_decide to approve/deny.
guidance.notWhen: For the trust roster (already-admitted members) use pot:get / harness:membership. Setting the membership MODE is pot policy (the policy authoring surface), not this.
guidance.chaining: pot:membership_pending (review) → pot:membership_decide (approve/deny each).

tools.name: pot:moderation_queue
tools.description: The owner's moderation queue — list member-filed reports for a Pot (default the open ones). Read-only. Act on a report with pot:moderation_resolve (action/dismiss), pot:takedown (hide content), or pot:ban_member.

guidance.when: You (the owner) want to review reports members filed via pot:report.
guidance.notWhen: Filing a report (that is pot:report, member-side).
guidance.chaining: pot:moderation_queue → pot:takedown / pot:ban_member / pot:moderation_resolve.

tools.name: pot:moderation_resolve
tools.description: OWNER resolves one OR many moderation reports: 'actioned' (you took action — e.g. a takedown/ban) or 'dismissed' (no action). Pass a single `{ reportId, status }` for one or `items:[{ reportId, status }]` for several. Federates the resolutions back. Requires holding the Pot key. Does NOT itself hide content or ban — use pot:takedown / pot:ban_member for that. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, reportId, report? | error }], counts } — correlate by reportId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You reviewed report(s) (pot:moderation_queue) and want to mark them resolved. Clearing a queue? Pass them all via `items:[{ reportId, status }]`.
guidance.notWhen: You want to actually hide content (pot:takedown) or ban a member (pot:ban_member) — do that first, then resolve.
guidance.chaining: pot:moderation_queue → (pot:takedown / pot:ban_member) → pot:moderation_resolve. Bulk: correlate by reportId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: pot:mug_efficiency
tools.description: The Mug's per-wake prompt efficiency: cache-hit ratio (Win-1 frozen-prefix cache), avg turns/wake (Win-2 round-trip elimination), token + cost totals, and cachedWakes (the 'cache is real' signal, P-003). Scoped to a pot home, or workspace-wide when no harness is given. Read-only.

guidance.when: To inspect the LIVE Mug's per-wake efficiency — is the frozen-prefix cache paying off (cacheHitRatio / cachedWakes) and is the precomputed brief cutting round-trips (avgTurns)? The B-06 measurement read.
guidance.notWhen: For a SCENARIO run’s efficiency score — that is the pot-eval efficiency class (it scores these per run). This tool is the ad-hoc live-Mug read.
guidance.chaining: pot:status for wake/placement state; pot:survey for the frontier.

tools.name: pot:obliterate
tools.description: Completely delete a local pot as if it never existed (root-only, destructive — pass confirm:true). Runs pot:dissolve {dropSchema} and then hard-DELETEs the pot's leftover rows from the SHARED harness_shared schema that dissolve leaves behind (work_items, plans, revisions, hive_settings, …), retracts its harness-scoped facts, drops a same-named fleet's membership rows, and removes its on-disk app tree, checkpoint worktree, and launch-context file. The purge is atomic — it rolls back rather than half-clear. Large append-only audit/telemetry logs are excluded unless purgeLogs:true. Irreversible.

guidance.when: The owner wants a pot GONE — not just torn down. Use after (or instead of) pot:dissolve when `work_items:list {harness:<slug>}` must return [] and no trace should remain.
guidance.notWhen: A reversible teardown — pot:dissolve (keeps the shared rows). Freezing a pot — pot:pause. Destroying a deployed cloud frame — deploy:teardown_pot (run that FIRST if the pot is deployed). From a cup — not allowed.
guidance.chaining: deploy:teardown_pot first if deployed; loop:end first if you have a monitor loop on it. Verify after: pot:get {slug} → hive_not_found, work_items:list {harness:slug} → [].

tools.name: pot:pause
tools.description: PAUSE the pot: persist hive_started=false (disarms the liveness watchdog), set the global wake-mode to manual (autonomous wakes are STAGED for review instead of firing — the one freeze seam, D-005), and clear the Mug's pending time wake. Optionally drain live cups gracefully. Resume with pot:start.

guidance.when: The user clicks Pause Pot / asks to freeze autonomous operation, or you need the fleet quiet (incident, review, cost control).
guidance.notWhen: To stop ONE cup — fleet:drain / fleet:cancel. To pause one plan — plans:pause. Pausing does not kill running turns; they finish and their follow-on wakes stage.
guidance.chaining: pot:pause { drainCups:true } for the harder stop → coord:wake-queue to review staged wakes → pot:start to resume.

tools.name: pot:report
tools.description: File a moderation report against content or a member in a Pot. The report federates to the owner's moderation queue. Requires the owner to have enabled reporting (moderation.reportable in the Pot policy); otherwise reporting is off and this no-ops.

guidance.when: You are a member of a Pot with reporting enabled and want to flag abusive content or a member to the owner.
guidance.notWhen: You ARE the owner taking action — use pot:takedown (hide content) / pot:ban_member (ban a member). Reporting is the member→owner signal, not the owner action.
guidance.chaining: pot:report (member flags) → owner reviews pot:moderation_queue → pot:moderation_resolve / pot:takedown / pot:ban_member.

tools.name: pot:request_work
tools.description: Initiate a cross-Pot WORK-REQUEST to a peer Pot (by pubkey): ask the peer to do something in its domain. The envelope is signed, sent store-and-forward, and recorded in this Pot's ask ledger; it becomes a work_item in the peer's backlog that THEIR Mug prioritizes. The peer's response arrives asynchronously — events:await the returned answeredEvent key. Requires an outbound grant to the peer.

guidance.when: The Mug/owner wants a peer Pot to take on a piece of work in its domain. Find the peer via discovery:pots, then pot:request_work, then events:await the returned answeredEvent.
guidance.notWhen: Asking a QUESTION (use pot:ask). Placing work on your OWN Swarm (work_items:* / fleet:*). Granting a peer to send work-requests INTO this Pot (that is the inbound pot:cross_grant).
guidance.chaining: discovery:pots (find the peer Pot pubkey) → pot:request_work { pot, peerPotPubkey, subject, body } → events:await { event: <answeredEvent> }. Review outstanding requests with pot:asks.

tools.name: pot:set-steering
tools.description: Set the owner steering the Mug reads on every wake (the 👑 Mug tab writes through this): a focus `directive`, `eligiblePlans` / `eligiblePots` (what it may pick up + the placement scope NOW — eligibility ≠ lifecycle status), `pauseNewWork`/`pausedUntil`, the P-006 THROTTLE knobs (`cadenceFloorSec`, `maxCups`, `idleActivities`, `autoScaleOut`, `modelTiers`/`tierCeilings`, `decomposition`), and the federated Blender priming override `federatedPriming` (`foreignElites` / `crowded` / `empty`). Writes the owner-steering:* hive_settings, refreshes the panel, AND wakes the Mug so the change takes effect immediately. `clear:true` wipes all steering; omitted fields are unchanged (null/[] clears one field). See each arg description for detail.

guidance.when: Steering the Mug from the owner surface — focus it on specific plans, give a directive, or pause new work (incident / cost / review). The 👑 Mug tab is the UI for this.
guidance.notWhen: Freezing the WHOLE pot (all autonomous wakes) — pot:pause. Per-plan lifecycle (draft/ready/shipped) — plans:*. Stopping ONE cup — fleet:drain / fleet:cancel.
guidance.chaining: pot:set-steering { eligiblePlans:[...], directive:"only these plans" } → the Mug wakes + honours it next placement. pot:set-steering { pauseNewWork:true } → it drives existing work to terminal then idles. pot:get-steering reads the current state; clear:true resets.

tools.name: pot:start
tools.description: START the pot (the global control, distinct from a per-plan Start): persist hive_started=true, re-affirm the Mug's default event-wake subscriptions (plan-started / work-item-created / escalation), set the global wake-mode to auto, and wake the Mug now (floor-debounced). The liveness watchdog holds "a wake is always armed" from here until pot:pause.

guidance.when: The user clicks Start Pot / asks to boot the fleet, or you are bringing a paused pot back to autonomous operation.
guidance.notWhen: To wake the Mug once without changing the started state — pot:wake. To start one plan — plans:start. To create a pot — pot:create.
guidance.chaining: pot:status to verify (started, subscriptions, next wake); pot:pause to suspend.

tools.name: pot:status
tools.description: The Pot operator's current state: started/paused (the Start-Pot bit), the pending time wake (one-shot routine), event subscriptions + live rule ids, last wake, the floor, and the watchdog health signal (fallback fires in 24h). Read-only.

guidance.when: To see when/whether the operator will wake next, or to verify a pot:declare-wake landed.
guidance.chaining: pot:declare-wake to change the declaration; pot:wake to fire now.

tools.name: pot:survey
tools.description: The Mug's plan-aware placement survey: started plans ranked (which plan to pour cups into) AND the unplaced work-item frontier ranked (which ready item to place), across EVERY member harness — one ranker, two views. Read-only; call it at the top of a placement wake.

guidance.when: You are the Mug starting a placement wake — survey what to work on next (which plan matters, which ready items to place) across all member harnesses.
guidance.notWhen: You already hold a specific work-item id and just need to place it — go straight to cup:spawn / the batch placement.
guidance.chaining: pot:survey → place the top frontier items (cup:spawn / batch placement) and steer plan order (work_items:set_priority / plans:set-priority); pot:status to inspect the wake declaration.

tools.name: pot:takedown
tools.description: OWNER takedown: hide a piece of content across the Pot by adding its ref to the owner-signed moderation.takedownList (re-signed + federated; honest peers honor it as a tombstone, no resurrection). Pass restore:true to un-hide. Requires holding the Pot key.

guidance.when: A member reported content (pot:moderation_queue) that you (the owner) want hidden on every honest peer.
guidance.notWhen: Banning the AUTHOR for repeat abuse — that is pot:ban_member (revoke + re-key teeth). Takedown hides content; ban removes a member.
guidance.chaining: pot:moderation_queue → pot:takedown (hide) → pot:moderation_resolve (mark actioned).

tools.name: pot:update
tools.description: Edit a pot's config: its deployment target (execution plane) and per-instance config overrides (maxCostUsd, parallelWorkers, …). A thin registry writer — no agent-lifecycle effects (never wakes/cancels). Cannot change harness_kind (a pot cannot reclassify). Root-only.

guidance.when: Changing a pot's deployment target or its per-instance config overrides (budget/parallelism knobs).
guidance.notWhen: Waking/pausing the Mug — pot:wake / pot:declare-wake. Placing/removing cups — fleet:*. Deploying to a cloud frame — deploy:pot.
guidance.chaining: pot:get { slug } to see the current config; deploy:pot to act on a changed deployment target.
