tools.name: pot:wake
tools.description: Fire the Pot operator immediately (launches the pot blueprint via the invoke route). Floor-debounced: a wake within the floor window of the previous one is skipped unless force:true. The target of event-wake reaction rules and the manual user override.

guidance.when: The user asks to wake/kick the operator now, or an event-wake rule fires (it targets this tool automatically).
guidance.notWhen: To schedule a future wake — that is pot:declare-wake.
guidance.chaining: pot:status to see the last/next wake; pot:declare-wake to schedule.

tools.name: pot_git:integration_requests
tools.description: Owner: the multi-owner integration-requests queue — below-steer-tier member heads the integrator queued instead of auto-merging (the code-plane twin of the coord quarantine). Actions: list {potSlug?, repoKey?, devicePubkey?, state?, limit?} (default state omitted = all) | ratify {potSlug, repoKey, devicePubkey, headSha} — the ONE call that marks a queued head ratified so the NEXT integrator pass merges it. Ratification is PER-SHA (a newer head from the same below-tier device queues again — you ratify the code you saw, not the author's future pushes). Local-only, never federated: this is the receiving owner's own trust judgment about the sender, not a peer-influenced decision.

guidance.when: A member's below-steer-tier head is stuck in the integration-requests queue (visible via {action:'list'}) and you've reviewed its content and want it merged on the next integrator pass — {action:'ratify', potSlug, repoKey, devicePubkey, headSha}. Check {action:'list', state:'pending'} first to see what's actually queued before ratifying.
guidance.notWhen: Granting a member's comms REACH into your agents (trust:comms) or auto-run of their verified work (trust:add) — those are separate trust axes. Raising the member's comms tier to 'steer' permanently (pot:set-steering / the pot policy) instead of a one-off per-SHA ratify.
guidance.chaining: {action:'list', state:'pending'} → review the head → {action:'ratify', potSlug, repoKey, devicePubkey, headSha} → the next integrator pass (git-sync tick) merges it.

tools.name: probe:emit
tools.description: Emit a self-verifying federation probe: stamps required federation keys (workspace_id, harness_slug) and REFUSES LOUDLY (never silently) when the target harness cannot federate — fixes 2026-07-10 cause #10, where every prior ad-hoc "v2t" marker probe was unstamped and green was unreachable for ~6h with nothing saying so. Tracked durably with a `captured` hop stamped; later hops (drain/replicate/merge/member_guard/project) are DESIGNED to land via probe:record-hop but no pipeline stage calls it yet (WI-3962) — read with probe:get { expectedHops:["captured"] } for a trustworthy verdict today.

guidance.when: Proving a federation/replication claim is REAL, not just "looks green" — verifying a fresh 2-machine rig federates content, diagnosing a "rosters but no content" stall, or replacing an ad-hoc marker write (the v2t convention) with something that cannot be emitted unstamped.
guidance.notWhen: Routine coord messaging or an ordinary content write (features/issues/plans) — a probe is diagnostic, not a deliverable. Not a substitute for events:emit/events:await (in-process wake, not a federation-pipeline check).
guidance.chaining: probe:emit → probe:get { probeKey } to read the verdict; pipeline-stage code calls probe:record-hop as the op is observed at each stage.

tools.name: probe:get
tools.description: Read a probe:emit-created federation probe: its per-hop receipts (captured/drained/replicated/merged/member_guard/projected) and a derived verdict that NAMES the exact hop it is stalled at, rather than just "still red". Auto-marks the probe acked once every expected hop has landed. ⚠ WI-3962: no pipeline stage calls probe:record-hop yet, so a default (unnarrowed) verdict WILL read "stalled" past capture for every probe, forever — that reflects a missing observation, not a broken pipeline (response carries an instrumentationCaveat saying so). Pass expectedHops:["captured"] to get the real, trustworthy signal today; check substrate_outbox/merge-cursor state for actual federation health.

guidance.when: Checking whether a probe:emit'd probe has round-tripped the federation pipeline, or diagnosing exactly which hop a stalled one is stuck at.
guidance.notWhen: You never called probe:emit for this key — there is nothing to read.
guidance.chaining: probe:emit → (wait / other work) → probe:get { probeKey }, repeat if verdict is pending/stalled.

tools.name: probe:record-hop
tools.description: Stamp that a federation probe (from probe:emit) has been OBSERVED at a later pipeline hop (drained/replicated/merged/member_guard/projected). Idempotent — re-stamping an already-landed hop is a no-op, so a retried observation can never move a receipt backwards. A hop can only be recorded while the probe is still `pending` (a refused/acked/timed_out probe is terminal).

guidance.when: You are pipeline-stage code (or a diagnostic script on a live rig) that just watched a specific federation_probe op pass a named stage — e.g. the outbox drain wrote it, a replicator delivered it, the merge loop admitted it, member-content-guard passed it, or projection applied it.
guidance.notWhen: You are the emitter (probe:emit already stamps `captured`) or you only SUSPECT a hop happened — this must be a real observation, never a guess.

tools.name: processes:kill
tools.description: Send SIGTERM (or SIGKILL) to one OR many tracked OS pids in ONE call — pass `pid` for one or `pids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, pid, kind, signal | error }], counts } — correlate each result by its pid, not by position; a protected/absent pid fails only itself.

guidance.when: User says "kill that process", "stop the runaway harness" — sends SIGTERM (then SIGKILL after timeout) to tracked OS process(es). Killing several at once? Pass them all via `pids`.
guidance.notWhen: For SPAWNED agents, use `orchestrator.cancel`. For DELEGATES, use the delegate-cancel endpoint. processes:kill is the OS-level escape hatch.

tools.name: projects:get
tools.description: Fetch a single project detail (spec, feature counts, last spec revision summary). Returns null when not found.

guidance.when: User names a specific project and wants its full record (spec, status, metadata).
guidance.notWhen: For SPEC revisions / history, use `projects:spec_revisions`. For the runtime harness state, use `harness:get`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `projects:list` for the slug.

tools.name: projects:list
tools.description: List projects relevant to a harness (filtered to those with at least one feature in the given slug). Includes feature counts.

guidance.when: User asks "what projects do I have?" or you need a project id before calling `projects:get`. Workspace-level project enumeration.
guidance.notWhen: For HARNESSES (work running inside a project), use `harness:list`. Projects ⊇ harnesses; the slug overlap is intentional but the surfaces are different.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `projects:get` for detail, or `projects:spec_revisions` for the spec history.

tools.name: projects:spec_revision
tools.description: Fetch one project spec-revision in full (includes the spec body). Returns null when not found.

guidance.when: User names a specific revision id and wants its full body — what the spec looked like at that point.
guidance.notWhen: For the CURRENT spec, use `projects:get`. For the list of revisions, use `projects:spec_revisions`.
guidance.chaining: Follow `projects:spec_revisions` for the id.

tools.name: projects:spec_revisions
tools.description: List spec-revision summaries for a project (newest-first; full spec body lives on projects:spec_revision).

guidance.when: User asks "how has the spec changed?", "when did we update X?", or you need a list of spec revision ids before reading one.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE revision's body, use `projects:spec_revision`. For the current spec, use `projects:get`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `projects:spec_revision` to read a specific revision.

tools.name: prompt:role_override
tools.description: Read/set/clear a per-(harness, role) prompt override (the harness_prompt_overrides store, read live by the orchestrator; cleared ⇒ falls back to the committed repo prompt). ops: get | list | set | clear (clear with no role wipes all of the harness's overrides). set/clear are audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness.

guidance.when: Specialize or correct a role's prompt for a running harness without a deploy (e.g. sharpen the validator persona for this mission), or clear an override to revert to the committed default. get/list to inspect.
guidance.notWhen: For the shared-base nudges across ALL roles (FRICTION_TRIPWIRE etc.) use P-017 prompt:set_fragment. A set REPLACES the whole role prompt for that harness; it does not merge.
guidance.chaining: get/list first to see the current override; clear to revert to the committed prompt.

tools.name: provisioner:detect_hardware
tools.description: Probe this machine's GPU vendor/VRAM and platform (nvidia-smi / rocm-smi / sysctl — all read-only, never touches a GPU's resident memory). Returns {ok, hardware:{platform,arch,ramGB,gpu,notes}}.

guidance.when: First-run provisioning, or re-checking hardware after a driver/GPU change.
guidance.notWhen: You already have a recent detectHardware() result and just need a recommendation — that's provisioner:recommend, which detects internally.
guidance.chaining: provisioner:detect_hardware → provisioner:recommend (or call recommend directly, it re-detects) → provisioner:plan_install → provisioner:install.

tools.name: provisioner:install
tools.description: Plan + apply the provisioner flow: write the recommended backend's systemd user-unit + register it in the gateway's local-backend pool. Default: no start, no GPU touch — pass `start:true` to enable+start + health-check it (loads the model onto the GPU). `provisionBinary:true` (WI-1617) resolves a real `llama-server` binary first; `pullVllmImage:true` (WI-1618, vLLM combos only) pulls the pinned vLLM image first; `pullWeights:true` pulls missing llama-server weights first — each can take real minutes and fails the call outright rather than silently falling back. Returns {ok, plan, result:{wroteUnit,registered,started}}; `plan.blocked` non-null refuses the apply with `result.error`.

guidance.when: Actually provisioning a local inference backend after reviewing provisioner:plan_install's output.
guidance.notWhen: A GPU-resident process may already be running — check coord:presence / coord:ask before `start:true`. Config-write + registry-registration alone (start omitted/false) is always safe. To preview without committing to a download/build, use provisioner:plan_install.
guidance.chaining: provisioner:plan_install (review) → provisioner:install (start:false default; add provisionBinary:true / pullVllmImage:true on first run) → once verified idle, provisioner:install again with start:true, or start the unit manually.

tools.name: provisioner:plan_install
tools.description: Dry-run the full provisioner flow: detect hardware → recommend a combo → resolve its weights against the local ollama blob store → render its backend config. Performs NO writes (not the systemd unit, not the gateway registry) — this is provisioner:install's plan, without applying it. Returns {ok, plan:{hardware,recommendation,weights,unitFileContent,unitFilePath,gatewayRegisterInput,blocked}}. `blocked` non-null means it cannot be applied as-is yet (no combo fits, or weights need `ollama pull` first).

guidance.when: Previewing exactly what provisioner:install would write, before committing.
guidance.notWhen: You just want the recommendation without the weights/config detail — that's provisioner:recommend (cheaper, no filesystem probe).
guidance.chaining: provisioner:plan_install → (if blocked is null) provisioner:install.

tools.name: provisioner:recommend
tools.description: Detect this machine's hardware and recommend a catalog combo for it (D-005 catalog — entries may be `status:'provisional'` until the P-006/P-007 certification battery lands). Returns {ok, hardware, recommendation:{entry,tier,reason}}. `entry:null` means no local combo fits (surfaced in `reason`, e.g. no GPU → cloud gateway).

guidance.when: Deciding what to install before committing to a plan/apply.
guidance.notWhen: You're ready to actually write config — that's provisioner:plan_install (does the same detect+recommend, plus weights resolution + rendered config).
guidance.chaining: provisioner:recommend → provisioner:plan_install → provisioner:install.

tools.name: quota:set_tool
tools.description: Read/set/clear a runtime per-(tool,role) quota override (perChunk/perRun/perDay), merged over the tool's baked rolesQuota at the dispatch quota step. Raise a tool's cap for a role for a planned burst, or tighten it mid-incident — live, no deploy. set/clear audited + one-call-revertible; empty override ⇒ baked cap (byte-identical).

guidance.when: A specific tool is throttling a role (raise its perRun/perChunk for that role), or a tool is being hammered and you want to tighten its cap — without editing the rolesQuota literal + deploying. op:get to read the active overrides.
guidance.notWhen: To change WHICH tools a role may call use the capability/envelope tools (quota is call-COUNT rate-limiting, downstream of capability). To change fleet-wide rate limits use operator:rate_limit_config.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active tool-quota-overrides; config:reset-overrides reverts them to the baked caps.

tools.name: rationale:feed
tools.description: The "why" of a subsystem-topic: the decisions, work-items, and insights relevant to it, projected from the plans/work-items/insights — indexed, no full search, never stale. Each entry carries a `ref` to drill into via plans:get / docs:get.

guidance.when: Before working in a subsystem (e.g. `coordination-substrate`), to load the rationale behind it — why it is the way it is — without searching everything.
guidance.notWhen: You want the cross-object work-stream / status of an area (topics:feed), the list of topics (topics:list), or messages waiting for you (coord:inbox).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → rationale:feed { topic } → plans:get / docs:get on an entry’s `ref` for the full text.

tools.name: rationale:reproject
tools.description: Re-derive a source (plan / work-item / insight) into the topic-keyed rationale index, or backfill all of them. Idempotent. Normally fired automatically by the event engine; call directly to backfill (kind:"all") or force a resync.

guidance.when: To backfill the rationale index (kind:"all") on a fresh DB, or force-resync one source after an out-of-band change. Routine maintenance is automatic.
guidance.notWhen: To READ the projection — that is rationale:feed.

tools.name: recipes:candidates
tools.description: Deterministic graduation worklist for code:run RECIPES: ranked PROMOTE candidates (recipes worth building into a tool, scored by run-frequency + distinct-agent reuse + success-rate + tool-set cohesion, 1-tool/duplicate ones excluded) + near-duplicate MERGE clusters. No LLM — counting only; YOU decide promote/merge. Read-only.

guidance.when: The Queen calls this in her cadence to find recipes worth promoting to a tool or merging. It returns deterministic signals + a rubric promotionScore per active recipe in the hive — promote a top candidate by filing a work-item ("implement <recipe> as a defineTool"), and review each merge cluster for consolidation into one recipe.
guidance.notWhen: To browse or run recipes (recipes:list / recipes:search / recipes:run) — this is the graduation review, not the reuse path. It does NOT promote or merge anything itself; it surfaces candidates for you to act on via your plan/work-item system (the gate is the normal coding pipeline).
guidance.chaining: recipes:candidates → (for a promote candidate) work_items:create "implement <id> as a defineTool" → (for a merge cluster) recipes:get each id to inspect, then consolidate. recipes:get { id } to read any candidate's script first.

tools.name: recipes:get
tools.description: Fetch one OR many reusable code:run RECIPEs by id — including the full script — so you can inspect what they do before recipes:run-ning them. Pass `id` for one or `ids` for several. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, recipe? | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest. Read-only.

guidance.when: When you have one or more recipe ids (from recipes:list / recipes:search / a code:run result's similarRecipes) and want to read their script + metadata before reusing. Pass every id at once via `ids`.
guidance.notWhen: To EXECUTE the recipe — use recipes:run (it runs the script under YOUR role-scoped envelope). To discover recipes by intent — recipes:search.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search / recipes:list → recipes:get { ids:[…] } (inspect) → recipes:run { id } (reuse). Bulk: single | ids[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: recipes:list
tools.description: List reusable code:run RECIPES for your hive (most-run first). A recipe is a saved code:run script other agents authored; browse them to reuse instead of re-authoring. Low-value (≤1-tool / auto-titled) recipes are hidden by default — pass includeTrivial to see all. Read-only.

guidance.when: Before authoring a multi-step code:run, to see what reusable recipes already exist in your hive — the hot ones surface first. If one fits, recipes:run it instead of re-writing the script.
guidance.notWhen: When you already know the recipe id (recipes:get), or to find a recipe by intent (recipes:search ranks by semantic + tool-set similarity). This is the plain most-run-first browse.
guidance.chaining: recipes:list → recipes:get { id } to inspect the script → recipes:run { id } to reuse it.

tools.name: recipes:merge
tools.description: Consolidate near-duplicate code:run RECIPES into one survivor: each duplicate flips to status=merged (pointing at the survivor) and its run_count/success_count are folded onto the survivor so it reflects the cluster's total usage. One transaction; never merges a recipe into itself; ids outside your workspace are skipped. Reversible (a status flip).

guidance.when: After reviewing a near-duplicate MERGE CLUSTER from recipes:candidates and deciding which one survives — pass the keeper as survivorId and the rest as duplicateIds to collapse the cluster into one recipe whose counts reflect all of them.
guidance.notWhen: To retire a stale one-off (recipes:sweep) or to promote a recipe to a tool (file a work-item). Do not merge recipes that are genuinely distinct just because they look similar — the dedup score is a worklist, the merge decision is yours. Inspect each script with recipes:get first.
guidance.chaining: recipes:candidates (mergeClusters) → recipes:get { id } per member to confirm they're truly duplicates → recipes:merge { survivorId, duplicateIds }.

tools.name: recipes:run
tools.description: Run one OR many saved code:run RECIPEs by id — the reuse path. Each recipe's script executes under YOUR role-scoped tool envelope (NOT the author's — no privilege travels with a recipe); returns only each script's summary. Use dryRun:true to preview write-effect mutations. Single: { id, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }. Many same options: { ids:[…], dryRun? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, dryRun?, timeoutSec? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, result? | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not by position; one recipe failing never fails the rest.

guidance.when: When a recipe already does what you need (found via recipes:search / recipes:list, or a code:run result's similarRecipes) — run it by id instead of re-authoring the same script. Run several at once via ids:[…] or items:[…]. Each runs under YOUR envelope, so you can only reuse recipes whose tools you may call.
guidance.notWhen: When no existing recipe fits — author a fresh code:run (which also auto-captures + dedups). Preview a recipe's mutations with dryRun before a committing run.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search { query } → recipes:get { ids:[…] } (inspect) → recipes:run { id, dryRun:true } → recipes:run { id }. Bulk: single | items[] (or ids) → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by id not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: recipes:search
tools.description: Search reusable code:run RECIPES by intent (hybrid BM25 + embedding + tool-set overlap). Use BEFORE authoring a multi-step code:run to find a recipe that already does it. Read-only.

guidance.when: BEFORE writing a multi-step code:run — describe what you want to do and this ranks the recipes in your hive that already do something similar (semantic + tool-set match). If a high-similarity recipe fits, recipes:run it instead of re-authoring.
guidance.notWhen: To browse all recipes most-run-first (recipes:list), or when you already hold the id (recipes:get / recipes:run). code:run still auto-surfaces similarRecipes after the fact — this is the BEFORE-you-author check.
guidance.chaining: recipes:search { query } → recipes:get { id } (inspect the top hit) → recipes:run { id } (reuse).

tools.name: recipes:sweep
tools.description: Retire the stale long-tail of never-reused one-off code:run RECIPES (active, last run older than staleDays AND run_count <= maxRunCount). NEVER retires a hot, recently-run, promoted, or merged recipe. dryRun (DEFAULT TRUE) previews the candidates without changing anything — pass dryRun:false to actually retire. Reversible (a status flip).

guidance.when: Periodic hygiene (a Queen idle-turn task) to clear the long tail of one-off recipes that were authored on a single run and never reused. ALWAYS run it once with the default dryRun:true to review the candidates, then dryRun:false to retire them.
guidance.notWhen: To merge near-duplicates (recipes:merge) or to find promote candidates (recipes:candidates). Don't lower staleDays/raise maxRunCount aggressively — that risks retiring recipes still finding their audience; the conservative defaults (30 days, <=1 run) target only true one-offs.
guidance.chaining: recipes:sweep { dryRun: true } (review the would-retire list) → recipes:sweep { dryRun: false } (commit). recipes:get { id } to inspect any candidate before committing.

tools.name: release:checkpoint-config
tools.description: Read or set the green-checkpoint / release thresholds: stallReds + stallAgeMs (held-gate STALLED alert), chronicFlakeCount + flakeNotifyCooldownMs (chronic-flake quarantine nudge), deployBackoffMs (re-deploy backoff after a failed/rolled-back deploy of the same target). set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tune the release pipeline live — e.g. shorten deployBackoffMs to re-deploy a fixed target sooner during an incident, or raise stallReds/stallAgeMs to quiet a noisy stall alert.
guidance.notWhen: For the placement watchdog use pot:control_policy; for migrations use db:migrate-policy. vitest forks / suite-timeout (green-checkpoint.ts) and the health-probe timing are not covered here (separate consumers — follow-up).
guidance.chaining: /admin/git shows the pipeline; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: release:checkpoint-run
tools.description: FIRE the green-checkpoint NOW — run the full gate suite against current staging on demand (instead of waiting for the hourly cron tick), and if it's green, advance the green pin so release:deploy can ship it. The gate's VERDICT producer had no manual lever (only routines:set cron/pause) — the same gap git-sync:run closed for the commit routine. Use it after you've fixed or quarantined the reds to force a fresh verdict instead of waiting up to an hour. Detached (the suite runs up to ~55 min) + self-locked against a concurrent tick (won't OOM). Watch /admin/git for the verdict, then release:deploy { op:status } → op:trigger.

guidance.when: You've fixed or quarantined the reds and want a FRESH green verdict now rather than waiting for the next hourly green-checkpoint. Or the gate looks stale and you want to re-run the suite on demand.
guidance.notWhen: To retune/pause the checkpoint cadence use routines:set. To SHIP an already-green pin use release:deploy op:trigger (checkpoint-run produces green; it does not deploy). To force an UN-green deploy use release:deploy op:force.
guidance.chaining: fix/quarantine reds → release:checkpoint-run → (watch /admin/git for advanced/green) → release:deploy { op:status } → op:trigger { confirm:true }.

tools.name: release:deploy
tools.description: Manually FIRE / TRIGGER / RUN-NOW / deploy-on-demand: the manual lever to push a committed, green change LIVE to :3070 now instead of waiting for the ~half-hourly timer, plus "why isn't my change live?" diagnosis. (This is the DEPLOY trigger; git-sync, the auto-commit/push routine, has no fire-now verb.) op:status (read-only — gate red/green/stalled, release-fixer status, how far :3070 is behind the green pin, + a recommendation; call FIRST when a gate-clean change isn't live). op:trigger (expedite a GREEN-but-stalled deploy; refuses unless green code is ahead; dry-run unless confirm:true; audited). op:force (operator/queen/architect ONLY, loud+audited: deploy an UN-GREEN commit past a red gate — needs acknowledgeRedTests + reason; rare no-users-window escape). Fired DETACHED.

guidance.when: A committed, gate-clean change isn't live on :3070 — {op:status} to see why. GREEN-but-stalled → {op:trigger,confirm:true} (safe; only ships the green pin). Gate RED on UNRELATED tests → FIX the reds first (even out of lane).
guidance.notWhen: Never force as a reflex to "get my change out" — force ships KNOWN-BROKEN code (route-around-the-broken-thing); owner/operator-gated, no-users window only. Prefer fix-reds > quarantine-a-confirmed-unrelated-red-by-hand > owner-force; never silently wait. Threshold tuning → release:checkpoint-config; per-path probe → dev:pipeline_position.
guidance.chaining: dev:pipeline_position{path} → release:deploy{op:status} → {op:trigger,confirm:true} (green-but-stalled) OR fix the reds.

tools.name: resource:delegate
tools.description: Delegate this host's resources to a fleet (the /res board write, D-004): kind 'account'|'gpu' with a share-% cap (autonomous-loop capacity), or 'agent_slot' — N × model·effort agent seats on a gateway account (account 'AUTO' = draw from the fleet's allocated accounts). Re-delegating the same (fleet, kind, ref) UPDATES the cap (idempotent upsert); remove:true revokes. Allotments are LOCAL to this machine (M19); an agent_slot delegation ALSO auto-publishes a standing seat-offer to the fleet owner over P2P (D-005 offer store — best-effort, the account id stays local). Returns {ok, action, allotment|removed} or a typed store refusal.

guidance.when: Handing a fleet capacity: 'join fleet X and assign 5 xhigh opus seats' → resource:delegate { fleetSlug:'x', kind:'agent_slot', model:'opus', effort:'xhigh', count:5 } (account omitted = AUTO). Account pools / GPUs take sharePct instead of count. Also the revoke path (remove:true — the /res chip's ×).
guidance.notWhen: READING current allotments — the /res board or the p2p.allotments sync query. Spawning agents that CONSUME delegated seats — the Phase-2 launch path (fleet:launch-on-plan). Registering/editing gateway accounts themselves — accounts:*.
guidance.chaining: fleet:create / fleet:join → resource:delegate { kind:'agent_slot', model, effort, count } → the launch-from-seats path consumes them (P-005). Delegate the fleet's account pools FIRST if its slots use account 'AUTO' (D-003: AUTO draws from what the fleet was given).

tools.name: roles:firing_on
tools.description: Return role manifests whose `firesOn` array includes the given hook event.

guidance.when: You need to know which roles are configured to fire on a given hook event before firing it (avoids no-op fires).
guidance.notWhen: For the hook-event ENUM itself, use `hooks:known`. For role details, use `roles:get`.

tools.name: roles:get
tools.description: Fetch one role manifest by id, scoped to a harness slug (or global when slug omitted).

guidance.when: User names a specific role and wants its full definition (system prompt, allowed tools, quotas).
guidance.notWhen: For the role list, use `roles:list`. For the known-role enum (static), use `roles:known`.

tools.name: roles:known
tools.description: Static well-known role-id allowlist (kernel set; plugin-registered roles extend this).

guidance.when: Static enum of role names the runtime supports — use to validate a role string before passing it elsewhere.
guidance.notWhen: For the workspace's ACTUAL roles (may be a subset), use `roles:list`. known is the universe; list is what's configured.

tools.name: roles:list
tools.description: List role manifests (id, source, fires-on, etc.) for a harness, or globally when no harness given.

guidance.when: You need the set of agent roles configured in the workspace (architect, worker, validator, …) before spawning or dispatching.
guidance.notWhen: For agents currently RUNNING, use `agents:list`. roles:list is the static configuration; agents:list is the live processes.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `roles:get` for one role's definition.

tools.name: routines:list
tools.description: List the scheduled system routines in this workspace (git-sync, green-checkpoint, release-trigger, improvement-watchdog, …): name, install slug, cron, target role, active flag, next/last fire. Read-only.

guidance.when: See the system routines and their cadence/active state before retuning or pausing one (e.g. inspect the git-sync / green-checkpoint / release-trigger schedule).
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE a routine, use routines:set. For a harness blueprint autoloop, use autoloop:status.
guidance.chaining: routines:set to retune or pause a routine you find here (use its exact name + installSlug).

tools.name: routines:set
tools.description: Retune or pause/resume a scheduled system routine (git-sync, green-checkpoint, release-trigger, …) without raw SQL: change its cron and/or active flag (active:false = PAUSE, active:true = RESUME). Audited + one-call-revertible via the control harness; an invalid cron is rejected. On a cron change, next_fire_at is recomputed.

guidance.when: Pause git-sync during a delicate manual operation (active:false), resume it (active:true), retune a routine's cadence (cron), or patch a routine CONFIG value (triggerConfig — e.g. the bee-transcript-cap caps) on a running system — the safe alternative to the raw UPDATE harness_shared.routines the playbook forbids.
guidance.notWhen: For a harness blueprint autoloop, use autoloop:control. To just SEE routines, routines:list. (These routine rows are their own store; they do not appear in config:list-overrides.)
guidance.chaining: routines:list first to get the exact name + installSlug; routines:list after to confirm the change.

tools.name: rubrics:get
tools.description: Read one OR many rubrics in full — each rubric's criteria (key + model + method + drift markers + optional rating scale), default rating scale, and method_ref runbook. Pass `rubricId` for one or `rubricIds` for several. Grade against these: a structured observation's `ratings` is a Record keyed by criteria[].key here (ratings[criteriaKey] = { rating, evidence }). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, rubricId, rubric? | error }], counts } — correlate by rubricId, not by position; a missing id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You have one or more rubric_ids (from rubrics:list/search) and need their full criteria to grade against — e.g. Kettle emitting the pot-coordination-health scorecard, or filing a structured observation. Pass every id at once via `rubricIds`.
guidance.notWhen: Scanning many — rubrics:list (summary rows).
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list → rubrics:get { rubricIds:[…] } → grade each criterion (observation `ratings` is a Record keyed by criteria[].key) in your observation. Bulk: single | rubricIds[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by rubricId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: rubrics:list
tools.description: List rubrics (shared standards for a system characteristic) — active first, then proposed. Filter by status / characteristic. A rubric carries the model (how it should work), method, rating scale + drift markers, and per-characteristic criteria that agents grade STRUCTURED OBSERVATIONS against. Returns summary rows; use rubrics:get for full criteria.

guidance.when: Before filing an observation — check whether an ACTIVE rubric fits the characteristic you are assessing, so you can file a structured (rated) observation instead of free-text. Kettle/Blender: discover the rubric set to grade against.
guidance.notWhen: You already have the rubric_id and want the full criteria — rubrics:get. Free-text keyword lookup — rubrics:search.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "active" } → rubrics:get { rubricId } → file a structured observation.

tools.name: rubrics:propose
tools.description: Propose a rubric (the shared standard for a system characteristic) → status "proposed". Any agent may propose — typically on noticing a cluster of free-text observations about one characteristic with no rubric. The Queen/owner ratifies it active (rubrics:ratify). Idempotent on rubric_id (re-propose updates the content).

guidance.when: You see a recurring characteristic worth grading consistently and no rubric covers it. Author the criteria (each: model + how-to-investigate + drift markers); reference an agent-insights runbook via methodRef for the long-form method.
guidance.notWhen: A one-off finding — file a free-text observation instead. Activating an existing proposed rubric — rubrics:ratify. Check rubrics:search first to avoid a duplicate.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:search (dedup) → rubrics:propose → rubrics:ratify (Mug/owner).

tools.name: rubrics:ratify
tools.description: Ratify one OR many proposed rubrics → status "active" (D-001: the Mug/owner gate — an active rubric becomes the shared definition every agent grades against). Single: { rubricId }. Many: { rubricIds:[…] }. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, rubricId, rubric? | error }], counts } — correlate by rubricId, not by position; a not-found id never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are the Mug/owner reviewing proposed rubric(s) and judge them sound shared standards. Activating one makes every agent grade structured observations against it. Ratify several at once via rubricIds:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Authoring or revising content — rubrics:propose. You are not the ratifying authority — leave it proposed and flag the Mug.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "proposed" } → rubrics:get → rubrics:ratify { rubricIds:[…] }. Bulk: single | rubricIds[] → { ok, results, counts }; correlate by rubricId not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: rubrics:search
tools.description: Full-text search rubrics by id / characteristic / title / description. Use before rubrics:propose to avoid a duplicate, or to locate an existing standard by keywords.

guidance.when: Before proposing a rubric (dedup), or to find a standard covering a characteristic by keyword.
guidance.notWhen: You want a filtered list by status/characteristic — rubrics:list. You have the id — rubrics:get.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:search → rubrics:get (use the existing one) / rubrics:propose (if none fits).

tools.name: rubrics:trend
tools.description: Qualitative health TREND for a rubric — aggregates the Overwatch scorecard rating time-series per criterion: direction (improving | worsening | stable | unknown), rating distribution, first/latest ("queen-placement-health: degraded, worsening over 5 ratings"). Chronological series returned as compact RLE runs only when includeSeries=true. Also a `staleness` signal (P-011): criteria persistently rated "unknown" (unassessable — the model may have drifted; re-ratify via the queen↔scout loop). Unknowns with `idle:`-prefixed evidence (the stage did not run) are excluded from staleness. Reads scorecards (P-013) — no new data.

guidance.when: You want to see how a rubric's criteria have trended OVER TIME — is a characteristic improving or worsening? which criteria are degrading across recent wakes? Or whether the rubric ITSELF is STALE (its model drifted — `staleness.stale`). The qualitative health-over-time view, vs a single point-in-time scorecard.
guidance.notWhen: You want the raw recent scorecards (point-in-time standing + completeness via missingKeys) — scorecards:list. You want the rubric DEFINITION (criteria/model/method) — rubrics:get. You want the cross-corpus ideation rollup — curation:state-of-pot.
guidance.chaining: rubrics:list { status: "active" } → rubrics:trend { rubricRef, since } → drill a worsening criterion via scorecards:list { rubricRef, since } → work_items:get on a scorecard issueId. If `staleness.stale`, re-ratify the rubric via the queen↔scout loop (revise template_data → plans:set-plan-status).

tools.name: saved_prompts:list
tools.description: List cross-client saved prompts for a scope: omit harness_slug for workspace-global prompts, or pass a harness slug for that harness. Returns the canonical PG rows (name, body, description, arg_hint) that materialize to the /name slash-commands in Claude / Codex / OMP.

guidance.when: When you need to inspect which saved `/name` prompts exist for a workspace or harness (e.g. to answer "what prompts are defined?" or before suggesting one).
guidance.notWhen: To create/edit/delete a prompt — that is the dashboard settings UI (POST /api/agent-mcp/saved-prompts). This tool is read-only.

tools.name: schedule:inventory
tools.description: Central read-only inventory of EVERY scheduled/recurring thing in the operator host regardless of cadence: DBOS scheduled workflows (durable tier), harness_shared.routines (durable tier), live managedSetInterval timers + in-process-periodic health sweeps (ephemeral tier), and bespoke separate-process timers (external-process: the inference gateway, its watchdog, the psu-launcher — listed for visibility, live fire-state pending federation). One row shape {source,scope,tier,category,name,cadence,armed,lastFire,nextFire,lastError}. Read-only.

guidance.when: See ALL cadences in one place — what runs on a schedule and how often (DBOS crons, system routines, in-process sweeps) — before tuning/pausing one or diagnosing a missing tick.
guidance.notWhen: To CHANGE a routine use routines:set; for DBOS execution rows (status counts/recent runs) use the /admin/dbos view; for routine-only detail use routines:list.
guidance.chaining: routines:set to retune a routine row you find here; routines:list for routine-only detail.

tools.name: scheduler:get_claim_spec
tools.description: Read the CURRENT claim spec for a cup or fleet: { source, spec, revision, updatedBy, updatedAt, harnessSlug, fleetSlug? }. `source` tells you which row actually answered — "bee" (a per-bee spec, always wins), "fleet" (inherited via membership, no per-bee override), or "default" (neither exists — DEFAULT_CLAIM_SPEC/oldest-first applies). The read counterpart to scheduler:set_claim_spec — confirm a re-steer landed before relying on it, instead of grepping source or guessing.

guidance.when: You just called scheduler:set_claim_spec and want to confirm the write landed (right revision, right filter/rank) — or you want to know WHAT spec a bee/fleet is currently running under before re-steering it. Pass exactly one of cupId | fleet.
guidance.notWhen: Setting/replacing a spec — scheduler:set_claim_spec. What is executing right now under which spec (the live-execution view across many bees) — scheduler:running. Full fleet roster / orphaned-claim detection — fleet:assignments.
guidance.chaining: scheduler:get_claim_spec (confirm current) → scheduler:set_claim_spec (re-steer) → scheduler:get_claim_spec (confirm the bump landed).

tools.name: scheduler:get_next
tools.description: Self-select via your claim SPEC (issued by your queen or fleet leader): atomically claim the next eligible work-item — the global floors (ready/blocking, lease, admission, dedup) AND your spec.view.filter, ordered by spec.rank, SKIP LOCKED. No spec set ⇒ default ordering (== work_items:claim_next) + an advisory `warning` (EI-8579). Returns the claimed item + the spec revision that selected it, or null.

guidance.when: You are a SELF-PULLING agent picking up your next item — a coding-pot cup (role="cup"), or an su fleet MEMBER pulling its lane (su-loop-capability-parity). Call this instead of scanning the raw frontier or self-prioritizing: scheduling is your Mug's / fleet leader's judgment expressed as your claim spec; the pickup is yours. NOTE the contrast: the coding-FACTORY is a different model — a scoper→architect→worker PUSH pipeline whose roles are HANDED a FEATURE_ID and never call get_next. So a claim-spec self-pulling worker is a cup or an su fleet member, NOT a scoper.
guidance.notWhen: You are a coding-FACTORY pipeline role (scoper/architect/worker/validator/…): you are PUSHED a FEATURE_ID by the orchestrator spine and do NOT self-pull — never call get_next. Claiming a SPECIFIC item by id — that is work_items:claim. Plain oldest-first self-select with NO per-agent spec — work_items:claim_next.
guidance.chaining: scheduler:get_next → work_items:set_state (progress) → work_items:release. Your queen or fleet leader re-steers you via scheduler:set_claim_spec (the spec revision bumps; you pick it up on your next get_next).

tools.name: scheduler:running
tools.description: The live-execution view of BEE RUNS: every live bee run (a bee executing a claimed work-item) with its bee, current item, claimed-since, lease, heartbeat, last progress, the derived idle/blocked reason, and the claim-spec specId@revision it runs under (null = DEFAULT ordering / no spec). Read off the live fleet state — "what is the fleet executing now, under which scheduling spec". A bee run, not a workflow (D-007).

guidance.when: You (Mug / Kettle / a human) want to see what the fleet is actively executing RIGHT NOW and under which scheduling spec — the live-execution view of the scheduler. Filter by { harness } or { bee }.
guidance.notWhen: Full fleet roster / bee load / orphaned-claim detection across ALL claim kinds (plan-item leases, assignments, presence) — use fleet:assignments. Claiming work — scheduler:get_next. Steering a bee — scheduler:set_claim_spec.
guidance.chaining: scheduler:running (what is executing) → fleet:assignments { agent } (drill into a bee) → scheduler:set_claim_spec (re-steer it).

tools.name: scheduler:set_claim_spec
tools.description: Steer a SELF-PULLING agent — a coding-hive bee, the queen, or an su fleet member — by setting/replacing its versioned claim spec (view.filter + rank). The agent's scheduler:get_next then pulls deterministically per this spec within the global floors. Re-steer a running puller by setting a new spec (the revision bumps; it's picked up on the next get_next) — not by micro-dispatching. Validates the spec; returns { ok, errors, revision, warning? } (EI-6079: a `warning` can flag the bee as not currently wakeable — the spec still stored, but a warm-inject wake to it may return woken:0).

guidance.when: Steer a SELF-PULLING agent that calls scheduler:get_next: a coding-hive bee, the queen, or an su fleet member. Set a property-filtered view plus rank for a standing lane; use `id in [...]` only for a static pinned wave. Re-steer by bumping the spec, not by micro-dispatching.
guidance.notWhen: A coding-FACTORY push role (scoper/architect/worker/validator): it is handed a FEATURE_ID and never calls get_next, so a spec is inert. Not for hand-picked micro-dispatch, or for overriding global floors (blocked/ready/dedup/cursed) — the resolver enforces those.
guidance.chaining: scheduler:set_claim_spec → the puller applies it on the next scheduler:get_next.

tools.name: scorecards:freshness
tools.description: Has the Overwatch emitted a COMPLETE scorecard for a rubric since a given time (its last wake)? The emission-freshness check (monitor-the-monitor): returns status = fresh (a COMPLETE scorecard landed in-window) | partial-only (scorecards landed but ALL incomplete — a silent truncation) | stale (NOTHING landed — a silent emission gap), plus emitted / complete / count / partialCount, lastEmittedAt, lastCompleteAt, and latestMissingKeys (what is unrated right now). Reads scorecards:list (P-013); a "complete" scorecard rates every rubric criterion.

guidance.when: You want to know whether the Overwatch is actually emitting COMPLETE scorecards, not just whether it emitted anything — monitor-the-monitor. Did a complete pot-coordination-health scorecard land since the last wake (status fresh), or is it silently skipping (stale) / truncating to partials (partial-only)? Pass `since` = the last wake for a precise check.
guidance.notWhen: You want the scorecard ROWS + their ratings — scorecards:list. You want a criterion's rating TREND over time — rubrics:trend. You are FILING a scorecard — improvements:capture { lane: "observation", observation: { rubricRef, ratings } }.
guidance.chaining: scorecards:freshness { rubricRef: "pot-coordination-health", since } → status stale/partial-only ⇒ the Overwatch missed or truncated → scorecards:list { rubricRef, since } to see what (if anything) it emitted, or check latestMissingKeys for which criteria were dropped.

tools.name: scorecards:list
tools.description: Read rubric SCORECARDS back — rubric-graded observations (rubricRef + per-criterion {rating, evidence}). Filter by rubricRef + sourceHive + since; newest-first. ⚠ SYNTHESIZED floors (turn-end backstop / scheduled-pulse) are EXCLUDED by default — pass includeSynthesized:true for the "is the data layer alive at all?" read (e.g. while overwatch is paused). Rows carry ratings, synthesized, nKeys, missingKeys (completeness).

guidance.when: You want to SEE the rubric scorecards that have been emitted — e.g. did the Overwatch emit a COMPLETE pot-coordination-health scorecard recently (missingKeys empty)? what is one criterion's rating over time? is there an emission gap? The data substrate for trend/freshness/self-comparison monitoring.
guidance.notWhen: You want the RUBRIC definition (criteria/model/method) — rubrics:get / rubrics:list. You want the cross-corpus meta-pattern rollup incl. rubric ratings grouped for ideation — curation:state-of-pot. You are FILING a scorecard — improvements:capture { lane: "observation", observation: { rubricRef, ratings } }.
guidance.chaining: scorecards:list { rubricRef: "pot-coordination-health", since } → inspect missingKeys for completeness / ratings for the latest standing → drill into a row via work_items:get { id: issueId }, or rubrics:get { rubricId: rubricRef } for the criterion definitions.

tools.name: search:fulltext
tools.description: Search workspace prose (escalations, brainstorm notes, older operator turns, and — with scope:["work_item"] — bug/change/task issue titles+bodies) by keyword match (BM25-style). Ranked by relevance. Returns excerpts.

guidance.when: User references prose past the chat history budget ("remember when we decided pricing", "the X discussion from last week"), or asks about content in escalations/brainstorm where the right SQL filter is not obvious. Returns ranked snippets. Also: BEFORE filing a new bug/change work-item, pass scope:["work_item"] to dedup-check against existing EI-* issues by title/body keyword — cheaper and more scalable than work_items:list + grep past ~500 items.
guidance.notWhen: For STRUCTURED queries on harness state, features, tasks, or messages — use the dedicated tools (harness:status, tasks:list, etc). They are faster and more precise when the schema matches the query. For CODE recall, use `gitnexus:query`. For tasks/goals/projects text, use `search:query`. `scope:["work_item"]` only covers the ISSUE family (bug/change/task, engineer_issues) — feature-family (F-NNN) work-items are not in this corpus.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a returned hit; pair `scope:["work_item"]` hits with `work_items:get { id }` for the full record. The result `excerpt` is just the first 200 chars for ranking display.

tools.name: search:query
tools.description:
When to use: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.

When NOT to use: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

guidance.when: User asks an open-ended question that could match anything in the workspace ("anything about auth?", "find references to budget guard"). Cross-resource full-text search over tasks, goals, projects, audit, messages.
guidance.notWhen: For a SPECIFIC resource type, use the dedicated list/get tool — search is broader but ranked less precisely. For code-graph queries, use `gitnexus:query`.

tools.name: search:semantic
tools.description: Semantic recall over workspace prose using embedding similarity. mode=hybrid combines with BM25 (search:fulltext) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion for best of both keyword and meaning. Falls back to BM25 if embeddings unavailable.

guidance.when: User asks about a concept by paraphrase rather than the exact keyword used in the recorded text. Examples: "when did we talk about authentication strategy" (could match "login flow", "auth approach", "JWT decision"). Prefer mode=hybrid for best recall.
guidance.notWhen: When the user knows the exact keyword they want. `search:fulltext` is faster + cheaper there (no embedding API call). For structured queries (tasks/goals/projects rows by title), use `search:query`.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `harness:escalation` or `harness:plan_reviews` to fetch the full row of a hit.

tools.name: service:await-up
tools.description: Sleep until a monitored service transitions back to HEALTHY (service:up:<name>) instead of re-polling dev:service_health. Then END YOUR TURN.

guidance.when: A service you depend on is down and you need it back before proceeding — arm this and end your turn instead of re-polling dev:service_health.
guidance.notWhen: A one-shot health check — dev:service_health. Restarting the service yourself — the systemctl/dev:restart path.
guidance.chaining: service:await-up { name: "inference-gateway" } → end turn → on wake it is healthy; resume.

tools.name: session:request-compaction
tools.description: Compact THIS session now, at a clean stopping point (near your soft compaction limit). The harness types /compact into your own TUI; it runs after this turn ends. Pass focus to name what to preserve this compaction.

guidance.when: You are near your compaction limit AND at a clean stopping point (a finished unit of work — tests green, an edit landed, a decision logged).
guidance.notWhen: Mid-task — reach a stopping point first. To change WHEN this fires — config:set-compaction-limit.

tools.name: sessions:list
tools.description: List indexed agent sessions across ALL clients (claude/omp/codex/harness chats) — newest first, with turn counts, owner, cwd, and time range. Filter by owner (self), source_kind, cwd substring, or time.

guidance.when: "What sessions has agent X had", "find my session from yesterday", or picking a session id for sessions:read. Covers the whole fleet, not one client.
guidance.notWhen: Searching CONTENT — sessions:search. Live "who is on what" — coord:presence / fleet:assignments.
guidance.chaining: session_id → sessions:read / sessions:search { session }.

tools.name: sessions:read
tools.description: Read a bounded window of turns from one indexed session transcript — around a turn (a sessions:search hit's readMore), a from/to range, or the tail. session:'self' reads YOUR OWN current session (pre-compaction turns included).

guidance.when: Following a sessions:search hit for more context, or reading where a session left off. Pass around=<turn_idx> (from the hit's provenance) or nothing for the tail.
guidance.notWhen: Finding WHERE something was said — sessions:search. Raw un-indexed files — dev:claude_session op=read (being absorbed here).
guidance.chaining: provenance.turn_idx from sessions:search hits → around.

tools.name: sessions:search
tools.description: Search agent session transcripts (claude/omp/codex + harness chats) and get each hit WITH its surrounding turns in one call. mode=verbatim finds exact quotes; mode=hybrid (default) finds by meaning. session:'self' searches YOUR OWN current session — including pre-compaction turns (they survive on disk and are re-indexed at read time).

guidance.when: "Which session did agent X say Y" / "we discussed this earlier — where?" / after a compaction, "I said something before the summary — recover it" (session:'self', mode:'verbatim'). Filters: owner/fleet/speaker/session/source_kind/since/until.
guidance.notWhen: Recall over escalations/brainstorm/decisions/work-items — search:fulltext / search:semantic. Distilled facts — memory:search. Reading a known session sequentially — sessions:read.
guidance.chaining: Each hit carries readMore args for sessions:read (a wider window). fleet:<slug> resolves EVER-members from the membership ledger — postmortem-safe.

tools.name: sessions:timeline
tools.description: Merged activity timeline for ONE agent: what it said (transcript turns), did (tool calls), and told peers (coord messages), newest-first over a time window. owner:'self' = the caller.

guidance.when: "What did agent X actually do yesterday" — a postmortem / handoff-archaeology read joining speech + tool calls + coord traffic by owner and time.
guidance.notWhen: Searching for specific content — sessions:search. Live state — coord:presence / fleet:assignments (this is HISTORY).
guidance.chaining: turn entries carry session_id + turn_idx → sessions:read for the surrounding conversation.

tools.name: setup:complete
tools.description: Mark onboarding finished (writes setup_wizard_state.finished_at). The app then boots to its normal surface. Idempotent unless force.

guidance.when: ONLY at the end of the onboarding tutorial (graduation), after the required setup steps verify ok via setup:status. Tell the user what it means: the app now opens normally; the tutorial stays available via the Papercusp Tutorial icon.
guidance.notWhen: Mid-tutorial, or to "skip" onboarding on the user's behalf without asking — graduation is the user's moment, not a shortcut.

tools.name: setup:save_integration_key
tools.description: Save a third-party integration API key (anything OTHER than the 4 platform keys openai/anthropic/zeroentropy/github_pat — e.g. a weather-widget provider key) into the encrypted operator_integration_credentials store, keyed by a caller-chosen SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE name. Returns the key MASKED.

guidance.when: The user hands over an API key/secret for a third-party integration or widget that is not one of the 4 platform provider keys. Choose a stable, descriptive name (e.g. WEATHERAPI_API_KEY) so the feature that consumes it can read it back by the same name.
guidance.notWhen: The 4 platform provider keys (openai/anthropic/zeroentropy/github_pat) — use setup:save_key for those. Never write ANY secret into a repo file.

tools.name: setup:save_key
tools.description: Save one provider API key (openai_api_key — also used for embeddings —, anthropic_api_key, zeroentropy_api_key, or github_pat) into the operator credentials store. Returns the key MASKED.

guidance.when: Onboarding/tutorial: the user pasted a key for a provider (the OpenAI key notably powers embeddings — better search + agent memory). Never echo the raw key back; the result is already masked.
guidance.notWhen: Agent-CLI sign-ins (claude/codex/omp OAuth) — those run their own login flows in the terminal, not the credentials store.

tools.name: setup:set_git_identity
tools.description: Write user.name + user.email to the GLOBAL git config — the identity stamped on every commit the agents make for this user.

guidance.when: Onboarding/tutorial: the user told you the name + email they want on commits. Confirm the exact values out loud first, then verify with setup:status (git flips to ok).
guidance.notWhen: Repo-local identity overrides — this writes --global only.

tools.name: setup:set_telemetry
tools.description: Record the telemetry consent decision (anonymized diagnostics + crash reports). Both true AND false count as "decided" — the setup step is satisfied either way.

guidance.when: Onboarding/tutorial: AFTER asking the user an explicit yes/no consent question. Never set it without asking — this is a consent record, not a default.
guidance.notWhen: Flushing or inspecting telemetry itself — that is the telemetry:* group.

tools.name: setup:set_tutorial_progress
tools.description: Checkpoint tutorial progress (last section id + completed section ids). The next tutor session reads it from its launch context to resume instead of restarting.

guidance.when: Onboarding tutor, at every chapter boundary and after each delivered section — checkpoint {last_section_id, completed_ids} so an interrupted tutorial resumes where it left off. Also when the user jumps chapters (record the new position).
guidance.notWhen: Recording SETUP steps (telemetry, channel, keys — those have their own setup:* verbs), or engineering work-item progress (work_items:checkpoint).

tools.name: setup:set_update_channel
tools.description: Choose the desktop app's release channel: alpha (freshest), beta, or stable.

guidance.when: Onboarding/tutorial: the user picked a channel (offer stable unless they want fresher builds). Verify with setup:status afterwards.

tools.name: setup:status
tools.description: Auto-detected setup state: every Setup-Wizard step status (ok / needs-attention / unknown) plus the per-runtime agent breakdown (claude / codex / omp). Same detection read the GUI wizard uses.

guidance.when: Onboarding/tutorial flows: read BEFORE offering a setup step (skip what is already ok) and RE-READ after acting — never tell the user a step is configured without this re-read.
guidance.notWhen: Per-provider sign-in token detail (expiry, refresh) — that lives on the /desktop/agent-auth-status route, not here.

tools.name: slash:dispatch
tools.description: Fire a slash-exposed tool command AT another running agent: renders the same instruction a typed slash command yields and delivers it as the target's next turn via deliver-and-wake. The target executes the tool over its OWN session with its own gates; a manual-wake-mode target stages the command for owner review instead. For tip [Apply] buttons, wake-board actions, and agent-to-agent command dispatch.

guidance.when: You want ANOTHER agent to run a specific tool command — applying a coord:glance tip to the mug, a UI 'run this on that agent' action, a mug placing a precise command (not prose) onto a cup.
guidance.notWhen: Running the tool YOURSELF — just call it directly (the slash layer adds nothing in-session). Free-form coordination prose — coord:send. Reviewing what a manual-mode target staged — coord:wake-queue.

tools.name: storage:prune
tools.description: Delete a storage category's rows/entries older than N days (or all). Local-only safe categories only; federated categories are refused. Bloat tables also VACUUM FULL to reclaim disk. Pass dryRun to preview count + estimated reclaim.

guidance.when: The owner (or the Storage settings page) deliberately trims a local-only category — telemetry tables, the drained federation outbox, or on-disk session/scratch/flight-recorder stores.
guidance.notWhen: To read sizes use storage:usage. Federated categories (plans/features/issues/coord) are refused — trimming would change what peers see.
guidance.chaining: storage:usage → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays, dryRun: true } → review reclaim → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays }.

tools.name: storage:usage
tools.description: Live storage usage by category (PG tables grouped by federation class + on-disk stores), each with total size, an age distribution, and whether it is safe to trim. Read-only.

guidance.when: Inspecting what is consuming local storage, or before a trim, to see per-category size + the age distribution and which categories are federated (read-only).
guidance.notWhen: To actually delete, use storage:prune (with dryRun first). This never deletes.
guidance.chaining: storage:usage → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays, dryRun: true } → storage:prune { category, olderThanDays }.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_contributor
tools.description: OWNER action: revoke another contributor by adding their device pubkeys to a revocation set. Scope is per-HARNESS (`harnessSlug`) or per-HIVE (`potSlug` — revokes from the whole Hive's federation at once, P-006). Every peer honors it on the next admission re-verify and drops them from live federation. Harness scope requires a repo-admin token; Hive scope requires holding the Hive key.

guidance.when: OWNER action: revoke ANOTHER contributor by adding their device pubkeys to a revocation set. Pass `harnessSlug` to drop them from ONE harness's federation (repo-admin token), or `potSlug` to drop them from the WHOLE Hive's federation in one action (P-006 — requires this Swarm to hold the Hive key). Use when a contributor is a confirmed bad actor, their account is compromised, or they must be removed from the shared federation entirely.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking your OWN device — use `substrate:revoke_self_device` instead. For harness scope, not when the token lacks GitHub admin on the shared repo. For Hive scope, not when this Swarm does not hold the Hive private key (only the owning Swarm may revoke Hive-wide).
guidance.chaining: Resolve the contributor's githubUserId from the Contributors tab, `dev:dogfood_substrate_status`, `harness:membership`, or `pot:get` first — githubUserId is the stable numeric GitHub user id, not the login.

tools.name: substrate:revoke_self_device
tools.description: Revoke one of your own device pubkeys from a harness (lost or rotated device). Adds the pubkey to revoked_pubkeys in your contributor row, replicates to peers, and drops the device from the booted substrate immediately.

guidance.when: Revoke ONE of your OWN device keys from a harness (a lost or rotated device) so peers stop admitting it.
guidance.notWhen: Revoking ANOTHER contributor's key / kicking out a bad actor — not supported (self-revocation only, v2 for owner-revocation).
guidance.chaining: Resolve the device pubkey from the contributor's own device_attestations first (e.g. via dev:dogfood_substrate_status or the Contributors tab).

tools.name: tasks:create
tools.description:
When to use: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.

When NOT to use: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.

Chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

guidance.when: User asks to add a task / TODO / item to track. Always confirm the title out loud before calling — task creation isn't silent.
guidance.notWhen: For asking the harness to DO work (write code, run validation), use `<spawn role="worker" />` instead — tasks track intent, spawns execute it.
guidance.chaining: After creating, mention the task id in your reply so the user can refer back.

tools.name: tasks:get
tools.description:
When to use: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.

When NOT to use: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.

Chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

guidance.when: User names a specific task ("the auth task", "task ABC-123") and you need its full body.
guidance.notWhen: For a list of tasks, use `tasks:list` first. Don't call `tasks:get` speculatively across many ids — list returns enough for most "what's the gist" questions.
guidance.chaining: Follow `tasks:list` to find the id.

tools.name: tasks:list
tools.description:
When to use: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.

When NOT to use: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.

Chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

guidance.when: User asks "what tasks do I have?", "what's on my plate", or you need a task id before calling `tasks:get`/`tasks:update`/`tasks:close`.
guidance.notWhen: For ONE task by id, use `tasks:get`. For creating a task, use `tasks:create`. For PROJECTS / FEATURES (work the harness is doing), use `harness:*` — tasks are separate from harness features.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `tasks:get` for detail on a specific row.

tools.name: telemetry:set_buffer
tools.description: Read/set/reset the dispatch telemetry-buffer sizing (maxPending / debounceMs / maxBatch) at runtime, merged over the baked defaults. Raise maxPending to ride out a PG-stall burst without shedding telemetry, or tune debounce/batch — no deploy. Empty override / kill-switch off (papercusp-telemetry-buffer-config) = byte-identical. set/reset audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Telemetry rows are being dropped under burst (the "telemetry queue overflow" warning) — raise maxPending; or tune flush debounce/batch for PG load. get to inspect the effective config + override.
guidance.notWhen: Not for quota/rate limits (operator:rate_limit_config), nor for retention (storage settings). This only sizes the in-memory telemetry flush queue.
guidance.chaining: config:list-overrides shows the active telemetry-buffer override; config:reset-overrides reverts it. The kill-switch papercusp-telemetry-buffer-config (default ON) forces the baked defaults when OFF.

tools.name: templates:get-guide
tools.description: Read a Cupboard app-template's build knowledge: its GUIDE.md (the composition prompt in MUST/SHOULD/FREE tiers) + COMPONENT_CATALOG + template.yaml (checks + pinned components), fetched from the public mirror. Pass `template` as the ref (e.g. "papercusp-webapp") or the listing id. Returns { ok, template:{id,ref,title,category?,scope?}, branch, guide, componentCatalog?, manifest?, guideTruncated }. This is the build-time knowledge a building agent follows — read it before templates:new-app, or to answer 'how do I build from <template>'.

guidance.when: You have a template ref (from templates:list, or the user named one like "papercusp-webapp") and need to read HOW to build from it — the GUIDE.md is the composition prompt.
guidance.notWhen: You just want to start building now → templates:new-app materializes the template AND hands the GUIDE to a builder in one step. Browsing what templates exist → templates:list.
guidance.chaining: templates:list → templates:get-guide { template } → templates:new-app { template, slug }.

tools.name: templates:list
tools.description: Browse the app-template storefront — the official "Papercusp Official: …" templates a NEW app is composed from (whole-app: papercusp-webapp, desktop-app, agentic-desktop-app; aspect: data-sync, search, ui, release-pipeline, data-layer, …). V1: these ship BUNDLED and are listed from the local store (works offline). Returns { ok, reachable, count, source, templates:[{ id, ref, title, description, category?, scope?, githubUrl }] }. `ref` (e.g. "papercusp-webapp") is the handle you pass to templates:get-guide / templates:new-app.

guidance.when: A user asks to build/scaffold an app (or "use the papercusp-webapp template") and you need to discover which official templates exist before building. The entry point to the app-template flow.
guidance.notWhen: You already know the template ref → skip to templates:get-guide (read the build guide) or templates:new-app (materialize + start building). Installing a blueprint/plugin (that is the Cupboard install path, not a template). A plan/rubric template — that is plans:*-template-data, unrelated.
guidance.chaining: templates:list → templates:get-guide { template } → templates:new-app { template, slug }.

tools.name: templates:new-app
tools.description: Materialize an app-template into a NEW pot (its own Hive home — a plan-capable project, created IDLE + local-only) and (by default) kick off a building agent seeded with the template GUIDE. V1: first-party templates ship BUNDLED, so this copies them from the local store (works offline). Composes pot:create + agent_chats. Args: `template` (ref e.g. "papercusp-webapp" or listing id), `slug` (new harness + folder name), `parentDir?` (default <~/.papercusp>/apps), `kickoffBuilder?` (default true), `builderRole?` (default "architect"). Returns { ok, harnessSlug, path, filesCopied, template, guideBranch, builder:{spawned,chatId?} }. This is the "build from a template NOW" verb — the write complement of templates:get-guide.

guidance.when: The user picked a template (from templates:list, or named one) and wants to START building the app — this scaffolds the harness AND hands the GUIDE to a builder in one call.
guidance.notWhen: Just browsing what exists → templates:list. Only reading how a template builds (no new harness) → templates:get-guide. Creating a harness from a blueprint (not a template) → harness:create.
guidance.chaining: templates:list → templates:get-guide { template } → templates:new-app { template, slug }.

tools.name: testing:flakiness
tools.description: Rank test files by cross-run flip-rate (pass<->fail flips across consecutive harness_shared.test_runs rows) over a lookback window — "is this red MINE or a known flake" in one call instead of an anecdotal rerun. Optionally auto-files a `change` quarantine-candidate work item (evidence table + a mandatory de-quarantine follow-up note) for files crossing the flip-rate/run-count bar, deduped by file path against an existing open one.

guidance.when: A test file is red and you want its recent flip history before treating it as a genuine regression vs a known flake — or triaging the green-checkpoint gate and want the ranked flaky-file list.
guidance.notWhen: A single ad-hoc rerun to check "is it green now" — just rerun the test. This reads cross-run history, not a live probe.
guidance.chaining: testing:flakiness → a red matching a high flipRate row here is a known flake (cite it in your completion) rather than a fresh investigation; autoFile:true files/dedupes the quarantine-candidate tracking item.

tools.name: testing:prune-orphan-runs
tools.description: Find (dry-run default) or DELETE (confirm:true) harness_shared.test_runs rows whose file no longer exists in that harness's staging worktree, or whose path is known non-signal (_retired/, .papercusp/scratch/tdg-*, sibling papercup-checkpoint/papercusp-checkpoint/papercup-staging prefixes). Groups by (harness_slug, file_path); returns row counts. Runs on the live operator's own DB connection (the only safe write path — the papercusp-workspace DB has no external psql/dev:pg_query write access).

guidance.when: A latest-status-per-file / raw test_runs diagnostic shows a red or green for a deleted/renamed file, preserved _retired code, tdg scratch dir, or sibling checkout path.
guidance.notWhen: The Tests-tab UI itself — it already glob-walks the filesystem and never shows a deleted file; this tool is for the raw test_runs table's own hygiene, not a user-facing symptom.
guidance.chaining: Dry-run (omit confirm) → review the groups → confirm:true to delete.

tools.name: tools:find
tools.description: Find tools by INTENT across the full ~550-tool catalog (hybrid lexical + semantic) AND activate the matches for your session so you can call them. Returns the best-matching tool names with descriptions. Use when you need a capability that is not in your core toolset — e.g. tools:find("feature flag") or tools:find("spawn a worker"). On a seeded (small-surface) session the matched tools are added to your live tool list on the fly, so after this call you can call the one you want directly.

guidance.when: You need a tool that is not in your loaded/core set and you do not know its exact name — search by what you want to DO ("set a feature flag", "list open plans", "spawn a worker bee"). The intent-aware replacement for guessing names.
guidance.notWhen: When the tool is already in your core set or you know its exact name — just call it (in omp, if a direct call reports not-found, tools:invoke {name, args} runs it server-side). For a full permission-annotated dump use agent_tools:list.
guidance.chaining: tools:find("<intent>") activates the matches for your session → call the top tool directly. If the direct call errors "tool not found", do NOT guess name variants: call tools:invoke {name:"<tool>", args:{...}} — it runs any catalog tool without loading. tools:invoke works on every client (claude/codex/omp) and never needs a separate load step.

tools.name: tools:invoke
tools.description: Call ANY tool in the full ~550-tool catalog by name, even one not in your loaded tool list. Pass the exact tool name (colon form, e.g. "flags:set") and its arguments object. The call is dispatched server-side and gated exactly as a direct call would be. Pair with tools:find: tools:find("<intent>") to get the name + arg schema, then tools:invoke({ name, args }) to run it. Use this when a tool you need is not in your loaded set and your client has not surfaced it directly.

guidance.when: You know (or just discovered via tools:find) the exact name of a tool that is NOT in your loaded set and you want to call it once — the universal way to reach the long tail of the catalog.
guidance.notWhen: When the tool IS already in your loaded set / core spine — call it directly (lower overhead, the model constructs the call natively). This meta-tool adds a layer of indirection; prefer a direct call whenever the tool is reachable.
guidance.chaining: tools:find("<intent>") → take the top hit's name + argSchema → tools:invoke({ name, args: {…} }).

tools.name: tools:scaffold
tools.description: Generate a REVIEWABLE skeleton for a new MCP tool — a defineTool file (+ index import line, + a migration stub for first-class table-backed tools) returned as TEXT. Writes nothing, runs nothing, mints no capability: the handler is a not_implemented stub. composed tier → mergeable after review; sandboxed-imperative/elevated → review-gated (D-003: prove confinement, then platform:contribute).

guidance.when: When a domain needs a NEW tool (not just a datatype). Scaffold the skeleton here, implement the handler, and land it through review. This is how the elevated/sandboxed tiers reach the codebase (D-003 PR rail).
guidance.notWhen: To define a DATATYPE (meta:define-datatype). To run an existing composition (recipes:run). This does NOT register or execute a tool — it only emits source for review.
guidance.chaining: tools:scaffold { group, verb, name, tier } → implement the handler → add the import to agent-tools/index.ts → npm run gen:tool-catalog → (review-gated tiers) PR + platform:contribute.

tools.name: topics:create
tools.description: Create a coordination topic: a short slug + one-sentence description. Prefer an existing topic (topics:list) over a near-duplicate. Notifies new_topic subscribers; re-creating an existing slug is a no-op.

guidance.when: No existing topic fits a relevance area you (and likely others) will want to follow. Keep the slug to a word or two; the description to one sentence.
guidance.notWhen: A close-enough topic already exists in topics:list — subscribe/tag to that instead. Near-duplicates get merged with topics:merge.

tools.name: topics:feed
tools.description: Read everything tagged with one OR many topics — across issues, conversations, features, and plans — the whole work-stream of an area. Each item carries its title + current state. Single: { topic }. Many: { topics:[…] } or items:[{ topic }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, count, items | error }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; a topic that fails to read never fails the rest.

guidance.when: To understand all current work in a relevance area before you start in it, or to see what is happening with e.g. `zero-cache` across every object kind. Read several areas at once via topics:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want messages waiting for you (coord:inbox) or just the list of topics (topics:list).
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:feed { topic } → work_items:get / conversations:get on an item.

tools.name: topics:list
tools.description: List coordination topics (tag + one-sentence description) and your own active topic subscriptions. A topic = a relevance area you can follow to have its updates injected into your context.

guidance.when: At the start of work, to see the shared topic taxonomy before tagging/subscribing — and to prefer an existing topic over creating a near-duplicate (D-004).
guidance.notWhen: You want the messages already waiting for you — that is coord:inbox, not this.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe (follow a relevant area) or topics:create (only if nothing fits).

tools.name: topics:merge
tools.description: Merge topic `from` into `into`: aliases the slug (tags resolve to the target) and re-points the merged topic’s subscribers onto the target. The dedup for accidental near-duplicate topics.

guidance.when: topics:list shows two topics that mean the same thing — fold the lesser-used into the better one.
guidance.notWhen: The two topics are genuinely distinct areas — keep both.

tools.name: topics:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to one OR many topics so their updates are injected into your inbox — the named sugar for watch(topic,{wake:false}). mode = full | digest | mention (D-006 noise tiering). Subscribe to the built-in `new_topic` to learn of new topics as they appear. Idempotent — re-subscribing updates the mode/TTL. Single: { topic, mode?, ttl_sec? }. Many same mode: { topics:[…], mode?, ttl_sec? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ topic, mode?, ttl_sec? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, subscription? | error }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A topic in topics:list is relevant to your current work and you want its updates pushed to you. Pick digest for high-churn areas, mention to stay quiet. Subscribe to several at once via topics:[…] or items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You only need a one-time look — just topics:list. To follow a specific object (one thread/issue), that is the object’s own subscribe, not a topic.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:subscribe; topics:unsubscribe to stop.

tools.name: topics:tag
tools.description: Tag one OR many coordination objects (issue / conversation / feature / plan) with a topic so each appears in that topic's feed and its changes reach the topic's subscribers. Pass remove:true to untag. Single: { object_kind, object_ref, topic, remove? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ object_kind, object_ref, topic, remove? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, object, topics? | error }], counts } — correlate by topic (not position); one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You want a feature/plan/issue/conversation to be visible to everyone following a relevance area — tag it with the topic. Tag several at once via items:[…].
