guidance.notWhen: The topic does not exist yet — topics:create it first (prefer an existing one). For an issue you can also use work_items:tag.
guidance.chaining: topics:list → topics:tag { object_kind, object_ref, topic } → topics:feed { topic }.

tools.name: topics:unsubscribe
tools.description: Unsubscribe from one OR many topics. Idempotent — unsubscribing from a topic you do not follow is a no-op. Single: { topic }. Many: { topics:[…] } or items:[{ topic }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, topic, error? }], counts } — correlate by topic, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A topic you followed is no longer relevant and its updates are noise. Drop several at once via topics:[…].
guidance.notWhen: You want to mute briefly — set the subscription to mention mode via topics:subscribe instead of dropping it.

tools.name: trust:add
tools.description: Add one OR many GitHub user ids to the owner's LOCAL trust list — a SECURITY GRANT: a VERIFIED-author remote work item from a trusted user may then auto-run on the owner's install (across every hive the owner is in), bypassing per-item screening. Pass `githubUserId` for one or `githubUserIds` for several. Owner-scoped, local-only, never federated. Audited. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, githubUserId, trusted? | error }], counts } — correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: The owner deliberately trusts GitHub user(s) so their verified remote work auto-runs without screening. Pass the numeric github_user_id(s) (match hive_members.github_user_id) — several at once via `githubUserIds`.
guidance.notWhen: To see who is trusted use trust:list; to revoke use trust:remove. This grants auto-run privilege — only the owner grants trust (an unverified or self-claimed author is never auto-admitted regardless).
guidance.chaining: trust:list (who is trusted) → trust:add { githubUserId, note? } | { githubUserIds:[…] }. Bulk: correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: trust:comms
tools.description: Owner: per-user COMMS-TRUST tiers (observe<message<wake<steer) — what a hive member's agents may do to YOUR agents across machines. Below 'message': quarantined; below 'wake': delivered but never re-invoked; 'steer': unlocks handoffs. Actions: set{githubUserId,tier,note?,expiresAtMs?} | remove | list | gate{githubUserId,granted} (DG-4 gate-trust, separable) | requests{githubUserId?} (quarantined messages) | grant{githubUserId,tier?} (one-call: raise tier + clear backlog). Local-only, never federated, audited; overrides hive policy comms.defaultTier per user.

guidance.when: Granting/downgrading a member's reach: 'wake' lets their mug re-invoke your cups; 'steer' for handoffs; 'observe' mutes a noisy member below the policy default. expiresAtMs makes a grant probationary. action:'gate' (P-047) grants/revokes gate-trust (do their shard verdicts count toward green?) — separable from steer. action:'requests' surfaces a below-tier member's quarantined messages; action:'grant' is the one-call approve for that queue.
guidance.notWhen: Auto-RUN of their verified work — trust:add. The hive-wide DEFAULT tier — author comms.defaultTier. A plain tier bump with no backlog to clear — action:'set' suffices; 'grant' only helps when there IS a quarantine backlog to drain.
guidance.chaining: {action:'requests'} → {action:'grant', githubUserId, tier:'message'} (or {action:'set', tier:'wake'} to bump only) — picked up within ~30s. {action:'gate', granted:true} → DG-5 counts their verdicts next round.

tools.name: trust:list
tools.description: List the owner's trusted GitHub user ids — the LOCAL, owner-scoped trust list the admission gate consults so a VERIFIED trusted author's remote (federated) work may auto-run without per-item screening.

guidance.when: Show who the owner trusts to auto-run foreign/federated work — the owner-scoped, local-only trust list (shared-hive-trust-admission).
guidance.notWhen: To grant or revoke trust use trust:add / trust:remove. This is read-only.
guidance.chaining: trust:list → trust:add { githubUserId } / trust:remove { githubUserId }.

tools.name: trust:remove
tools.description: Remove one OR many GitHub user ids from the owner's LOCAL trust list — revokes the auto-run privilege; their verified remote work returns to per-item screening. Pass `githubUserId` for one or `githubUserIds` for several. Owner-scoped, local-only. Audited. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, githubUserId, removed | error }], counts } — correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: The owner revokes trust in GitHub user(s) (their remote work should no longer auto-run). Revoking several at once? Pass them all via `githubUserIds`.
guidance.notWhen: To grant trust use trust:add; to view the list use trust:list.
guidance.chaining: trust:list → trust:remove { githubUserId } | { githubUserIds:[…] }. Bulk: correlate by githubUserId, not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: tui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a control intent to a running pui (terminal workbench) and wait for the result. Built-in intents: get_state ({}) → snapshot of the pui AppState (active tab, selections, counts, chat state, live panes); set_tab ({tab:"Operator"|"Plans"|"Sessions"|"Fleet"|…}); set_harness ({slug}); select ({list:"plans"|"roster"|"inbox"|"features"|"issues"|"docs", index}); open_chat ({}) → focus the operator chat pane; focus_pane ({pane_id}) → focus a worker's zellij pane (ids from get_state.panes). client_id targets the pui instance (its workbench owner key, $USER@$HOSTNAME by default).

guidance.when: You need to drive or read a running pui terminal workbench — switch its tab, change its active harness, move a selection, or read its current state. Side-effect tool: writes a tui_intents row the pui consumes over SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For the browser/desktop UI use `ui:dispatch`. For showing a question + choices use `chat:ask_choice`. For delegating work use `<spawn>` — tui:dispatch is UI control, not work delegation.

tools.name: turn:interrupt
tools.description: End a peer agent's CURRENT turn (the dual of a wake). mode:'cooperative' injects a high-priority `yield` so the peer reaches a safe checkpoint, saves partial state, releases locks, and ends its turn (the polite default; DEFERS if the target holds file locks). mode:'force' ends the turn NOW, mid-thinking — Ctrl+C to a managed-pty session or SIGINT to a headless one (the turn ends; the session stays resumable). reason is REQUIRED + audited; storm-rate-limited so it can't be used to halt the fleet.

guidance.when: A peer is doing the wrong thing / working on something now-obsolete / looping, and you need its current turn to STOP. Prefer cooperative (it wraps up cleanly + saves); use force only when it must stop mid-thinking and cooperative was ignored or there's no time.
guidance.notWhen: To wake an IDLE peer, use coord:send {wake:true} — interrupt is for a RUNNING peer. To hand work over, coord:handoff. Don't force a peer that holds file locks unless necessary (it can orphan a half-written edit) — cooperative defers exactly to avoid that.

tools.name: ui:dispatch
tools.description: Dispatch a UI intent to a browser tab and wait for the result. Defaults client_id to ctx.uiClientId (the tab that spawned the agent). Built-in intents: set_url ({path?:"/route", params:{...}} — path switches the route, params merge into the query string), snapshot ({selector?,mode?}), read_visible_text, focus, scroll_into_view, click. Pages can register additional intents via useUiIntent(name, handler).

guidance.when: You need to make something happen in the user's browser tab — open the panel, navigate, focus a card, etc. Side-effect tool: writes a ui_intents row the tab consumes via SSE.
guidance.notWhen: For showing a question + choices in the chat, use `chat:ask_choice` (renders inline buttons). For asking the operator brain to delegate work, use `<spawn>` — `ui:dispatch` is for UI side effects, not work delegation.

tools.name: ui:get_state
tools.description: Read the URL state of a browser tab (defaults to the tab that spawned the agent via ctx.uiClientId). Returns { url, pathname, params, title, last_seen_at }. Use to answer "what is the user looking at?" — nuqs serializes panel/tab/filter/selection state to the URL, so the params object reflects most UI state.

guidance.when: User asks "what am I looking at?", "what page am I on?", or you need to verify a panel state before acting ("is the panel already open?").
guidance.notWhen: Tool calls ARE idempotent — `panel_open` when already open is fine. Don't pre-check just to skip a call; the persona rule is "always call". Use `ui:get_state` only when you need to BRANCH on what the user is looking at.

tools.name: ui:list_clients
tools.description: List open browser tabs (UI clients) with active presence. Each entry is { client_id, workspace_id, url, title, last_seen_at, opened_at, is_self }. is_self=true when the client matches ctx.uiClientId (i.e., the tab that spawned the agent).

guidance.when: You need to know which browser tab(s) the user has open before calling `ui:dispatch`. Returns client ids the operator can target.
guidance.notWhen: In the operator-converse path, ctx.uiClientId is already populated — you can target the user's current tab directly via `ui:dispatch`. Only list when you need to choose between multiple tabs.
guidance.chaining: Pair with `ui:get_state` to see what each tab is on, then `ui:dispatch` to act.

tools.name: voice:agent
tools.description: Voice agent peer: toggle channel listening (STT) or the converse BRAIN (auto-reply), report status, or speak text (TTS) into the active channel.

guidance.when: Toggle the agent's ears ({op:'enable'|'disable'}), its auto-reply brain ({op:'brain', on}), read {op:'status'}, or speak into the channel ({op:'say', text}).
guidance.notWhen: Joining/leaving the channel itself is `voice:join`/`voice:leave`; this controls only the agent's listen/think/speak behaviors on top.
guidance.chaining: voice:join → voice:agent {op:'brain', on:true} (ears + auto-reply: peer speech → operator-converse → spoken reply). For manual control use {op:'enable'} then {op:'say', text:'…'}.

tools.name: voice:channels
tools.description: List/create/remove P2P voice channels (the durable registry; a channel maps a name to a swarm topic).

guidance.when: Manage the voice-channel registry — list what channels exist, create one before joining it, or remove a stale one.
guidance.notWhen: To enter/exit a channel use `voice:join` / `voice:leave`; for who's in a channel right now use `voice:status`.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'create'} → voice:join {channel} → voice:status.

tools.name: voice:delegate_deep
tools.description: Delegate a HARD-THINKING question (analysis/research/deep comparison) to an ephemeral background agent. The answer comes back into your pane as `[deep-answer WI-NNN] …` — present + speak it then. Capped at 2 in flight.

guidance.when: The user asked something that needs REAL investigation (minutes of reading code/state/docs) and expects an ANSWER back in conversation. Delegate it, voice:say a short ack ("digging into that — I'll come back to you"), and stay responsive. When the [deep-answer WI-NNN] message arrives in your pane, present it: voice:say the speakable core + show the detail.
guidance.notWhen: Trivia you can answer now (just answer). Buildable WORK ("build X", "fix Y") — that's a Mug handoff, not a deep dive. More than 2 in flight — the tool refuses; tell the user one is already cooking.
guidance.chaining: voice:delegate_deep { question } → voice:say the ack → (later) the [deep-answer] arrives as pane input → voice:say the answer. Check progress via work_items:get on the returned workItemId.

tools.name: voice:join
tools.description: Join a P2P voice channel by id or name — starts the voice swarm, announces the topic, connects to peers.

guidance.when: Enter a voice channel (by id or name from `voice:channels`). One active channel at a time; joining another leaves the current one.
guidance.notWhen: Don't poll this — `voice:status` reads the live state; the local voice socket pushes status events to UI clients.
guidance.chaining: voice:channels {op:'list'} → voice:join → speak via the local voice socket (pui/desktop) → voice:leave.

tools.name: voice:leave
tools.description: Leave the active P2P voice channel (drops peer connections, releases the swarm topic).

guidance.when: Exit the current voice channel. Safe no-op when not in one.
guidance.notWhen: Removing a channel from the registry is `voice:channels {op:'remove'}` — leaving only ends THIS node's participation.

tools.name: voice:say
tools.description: Speak a short line ALOUD to the local app user via the desktop's TTS (the Sentinel's voice-out). LOCAL app user only — not the P2P voice channels.

guidance.when: You are the voice-first Papercup and want the user to HEAR something — call voice:say with the spoken words (short: one or two sentences). The user hears ONLY what you pass here.
guidance.notWhen: Don't speak internal tool steps, long detail, or code aloud. For multi-peer P2P voice use voice:join, not this.

tools.name: voice:status
tools.description: Live voice state: active channel, mute, and in-channel peers (id/label/muted/speaking).

guidance.when: Read who's in the active voice channel right now (presence is in-band — liveness IS the peer connection).
guidance.notWhen: The durable channel LIST is `voice:channels {op:'list'}` — status only covers the channel this node is in.

tools.name: voice:transcript
tools.description: Read live speech transcripts from the active voice channel: enable buffering (turns the ears on), then read the most-recent utterances or the delta since a cursor. The OBSERVE seam for an agent to react to spoken input WITHOUT the auto-reply brain.

guidance.when: Let an agent (e.g. a narrator/host) HEAR what peers said and react on its own terms — {op:'enable'} once, then poll {op:'read', since:<cursor>} for new utterances. Unlike voice:agent {op:'brain'}, this never auto-replies — you decide what to do with the speech.
guidance.notWhen: For the agent to AUTO-converse (peer speech → spoken reply) use `voice:agent {op:'brain', on:true}` instead. Buffering needs the ears: {op:'enable'} turns them on; {op:'disable'} stops buffering but leaves the shared ears (toggle those via voice:agent).
guidance.chaining: voice:join → voice:transcript {op:'enable'} → voice:transcript {op:'read'} (note the cursor) → … → voice:transcript {op:'read', since:<cursor>} for only what's new.

tools.name: watch:create
tools.description: The unified subscription primitive — watch(pattern, {wake, once, min_sleep_sec, urgency, timeout_sec, mode}): register an interest, receive a delivery. DELIVERY — wake:false (DEFAULT, cheap) injects updates into your coord inbox (next natural turn, no token cost); wake:true (opt-in, a turn = tokens) re-invokes you when it fires. CARDINALITY — once:true is one-shot (auto-consumes — a grant); once:false is standing (re-fires per match). Sugar: events:await = watch(key,{wake:true,once:true}); topics:subscribe = watch(topic,{wake:false}). Lifecycle: events:cancel / events:status (wake) · topics:unsubscribe (inject). PREDICATE (wake:true): predicate:{tool,args,path,op,value}+interval_sec — the engine polls a read-only tool under YOUR role and wakes you on the false→true cross.

guidance.when: Prefer wake:false (inject) for continuous awareness of a churning area — no cost. Use wake:true ONLY for specific readiness ("wake me when THIS grant/lock/deadline is ready"); for a standing wake watch set min_sleep_sec to bound the re-wake rate. once:true for a one-shot grant; once:false to keep following.
guidance.notWhen: A sub-minute wait inside one turn — just do the bounded blocking call. A recurring TIME schedule — the pot/routines own time-based wakes. Ambient interest where a wake would burn turns — use wake:false.
guidance.chaining: wake:true → end your turn; on wake the turn text carries the event + payload. events:cancel (wake) / topics:unsubscribe (inject) to stop; events:status to inspect your active wake watches + recent wakes.

tools.name: wiki:backlinks
tools.description: Find markdown files that reference [[target]] across the workspace, for one OR many pages in ONE call — pass `target` for one or `targets:[…]` for several (1–100), with an optional shared `harness` filter. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, target, harness, hits[] | error }], counts } — correlate each result by its target, not by position; one failed scan never fails the rest.

guidance.when: User asks "what links to X?", "where is `[[name]]` referenced?". Wiki-style backlink lookup across markdown files. Look up several pages at once via `targets:[…]`.
guidance.notWhen: For cross-resource full-text search, use `search:query`. For markdown TOC, use `harness:markdown_index`.
guidance.chaining: single `target` | `targets:[…]` → { ok, results:[{ ok, target, harness, hits[] | error }], counts } — correlate by target not position; one failure never fails the rest.

tools.name: work-item:await
tools.description: Sleep until a work item changes status instead of polling work_items:get. With no `state`, arms the general work-item:status:<id> (ANY transition). With a single `state` (done|unblocked|blocked|claimed), arms only that specific key. Then END YOUR TURN.

guidance.when: You are blocked on a peer/dependency work item (its completion, unblock, or any transition) — arm this and end your turn instead of re-reading work_items:get.
guidance.notWhen: Just inspecting an item once — work_items:get. Waiting on a PLAN item (P-NNN) — plan-item:await. Ambient interest in a topic — topics:subscribe.
guidance.chaining: work-item:await { id: "WI-123", state: "done" } → end turn → on wake the item has settled; continue.

tools.name: work_items:amend
tools.description: Record a structural decision on a plan-run node (split | drop | reapproach | expand | note) durably, in one call. The Queen/operator disposes; a bee proposes. A disruptive amend on an in-flight node is flagged NEEDS-COMPENSATION (coordinate, never silently yank). The record is the commit-before-dispatch truth — amend BEFORE dispatching the dependent work.

guidance.when: You are making (or, as a cup, PROPOSING) a non-re-derivable structural change to a plan-run node — split it, drop/re-approach the approach, expand a deferred region. Record it here in ONE call before dispatching the dependent work; the durable record is the resumable truth.
guidance.notWhen: A routine progress update / finding → work_items:comment. Re-prioritizing the frontier (re-derivable, costs nothing to lose) → no amend needed. Finishing a node → work_items:complete / set_state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:amend { id, kind, rationale }. A bee PROPOSES (disposition=proposed); the Queen DISPOSES. requiresCompensation=true ⇒ a worker is mid-execution on the node — coordinate (coord:send) before/with the change.

tools.name: work_items:burn_down
tools.description: One-call leader census for a harness work queue: terminal counts, in-flight rows with assignee liveness, parked rows (blocked/needs-human/claimHold), and unclaimed rows. Pass `since` to also get closedSince/openedSince — itemized (not just counted) terminal transitions and newly-created items, capped + newest-first. Replaces hand-joining work_items:list with coord:presence for drain/fleet leader wakes.

guidance.when: You are leading a drain/fleet/Queen pass and need to know what is done, actively held by a live or dead assignee, intentionally parked, and still unclaimed.
guidance.notWhen: You need full per-item bodies/checkpoints/comments — use work_items:get for the specific ids after this census.
guidance.chaining: work_items:burn_down → work_items:get for detail on a row → coord:send or work_items:claim/release/set_state as needed.

tools.name: work_items:checkpoint
tools.description: Write (or clear) one OR many work-items' checkpoints — a compressed snapshot of your in-flight state. Single: { id, checkpoint? }. Many: items:[{ id, checkpoint?, harness? }]. Your prior transcript does NOT carry across a task boundary / re-spawn; the checkpoint is your continuity, re-injected on the next invocation of that item (yours or a successor's). Replace-on-write; `append:true` joins instead (EI-9036). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, harness, cleared, length, contentHash, verified, storedHead, by | error }], counts }. Writes are verify-read; fails loudly on an invisible write (checkpoint_verify_failed). A plain replace shrinking a substantial checkpoint >50% gets a non-blocking `shrinkWarning` (EI-9325, likely truncation).

guidance.when: At a task boundary or on graceful eviction, before you finish/yield: persist what a successor (or your next fresh-context wake) needs to continue — what is done, what is left, current approach, gotchas, open threads. Keep it COMPRESSED (a digest, not a transcript).
guidance.notWhen: Mid-task scratch state that the live transcript already holds — checkpoint only the durable, cross-boundary gist. Do not dump file contents or full tool output.
guidance.chaining: work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint } before work_items:complete / on yield. Pass blank to clear a stale note. Also fixes EI-6772: a claim held through long PURELY-LOCAL tool use (no papercusp-su calls) can go presence-stale and be reclaimed — checkpointing doubles as a liveness pulse (no separate heartbeat verb).

tools.name: work_items:claim
tools.description: Claim one OR many work-items (assign to yourself, or to `assignee`). Claiming a feature sets taken_by; an issue sets assignee. Single: { id, assignee? }. Many same assignee: { ids:[…], assignee? }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, assignee?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem? | error, holder? }], counts } — correlate by id; a claim_conflict on one item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You are starting work on work-item(s) — claim so peers do not duplicate. Claim a swath at once via { ids:[…] }.
guidance.notWhen: A per-item `claim_conflict` means a LIVE peer holds it — coordinate with the `holder` (coord:send) or pick another item; do not blind-retry. (If the holder is dead, the stale-claim reclaim lane frees it.)
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:claim → work_items:set_state → work_items:release/close. There is no separate work_items:heartbeat — ANY papercusp-su tool call already refreshes your liveness (dispatch-heartbeat beats coord_presence on every settled dispatch), which is what the stale-claim reaper checks before reclaiming a held item. The gap is a long stretch of PURELY-LOCAL tool use (Bash/Read/vitest with zero papercusp-su calls) during a >10-15min single-claim investigation (EI-6772) — call work_items:checkpoint { id, checkpoint } partway through (it doubles as your progress note AND a liveness pulse) rather than going silent on the platform for the whole investigation.

tools.name: work_items:claim_next
tools.description: Self-select the next work-item. When scheduler claim-specs are enabled, this compatibility wrapper honors the caller/assignee claim-spec (same selector as scheduler:get_next) so a fleet member stays in its leader-steered lane; when the scheduler flag is off it degrades to the legacy oldest-first SKIP LOCKED claim. Competing agents never double-claim. Returns the claimed item, or on a miss a SELF-DESCRIBING result: `{ ok:false, drained, pendingUnclaimed, readyUnclaimed, error }`.

guidance.when: You are an idle agent picking up work. Fleet members should prefer scheduler:get_next, but this older wrapper is lane-safe while scheduler claim-specs are enabled.
guidance.notWhen: When a SPECIFIC item must go to a SPECIFIC agent — that is work_items:claim with an explicit assignee (named assignment, the exception — it deliberately bypasses the status/readiness floors self-select enforces, so an item claimable by id can still legitimately miss here).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_next → work_items:set_state → work_items:release. On a MISS, read `drained`: drained:true means the queue is empty (message leader + idle); drained:false means work exists but is currently blocked/gated (pendingUnclaimed>0) — do NOT idle, re-check shortly or help unblock the backlog rather than reporting the queue drained.

tools.name: work_items:claim_replica
tools.description: Claim one replica slot of a HIGH-STAKES (redundancy>1) work-item — the redundancy analogue of claim_next. Up to N distinct Swarms each get a distinct slot of the SAME item and run it independently. Returns the slot (replica_index + claim_id) or null when not high-stakes / all slots held.

guidance.when: You are a Swarm picking up a high-stakes item that is being run redundantly. Claim a replica slot, run the item independently, then record your result.
guidance.notWhen: A normal exactly-once item — that is work_items:claim_next. Marking an item high-stakes — that is work_items:set_redundancy.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_replica → (run the item) → work_items:record_replica_result { replicaIndex } → work_items:judge_redundancy resolves the winner.

tools.name: work_items:co_locate
tools.description: The Queen's co-location lever: stamp a work-item's Swarm affinity so tightly-coupled work runs on the SAME Swarm (instant coordination) and loosely-coupled work spreads. Pin with { swarm }, decide with { coLocateWith, tight? }, or read the current affinity with just { workItem }.

guidance.when: You are the Mug placing work: co-locate a work-item with its tight collaborators on one Swarm (coLocateWith), pin it to a specific Swarm (swarm), or check where it is affined. The affinity is honored by claim_next once the per-Pot claim lease is active.
guidance.notWhen: Ranking a bee's queue (work_items:reorder) or sending a specific item to a specific agent (work_items:claim). Co-location is about WHICH SWARM, not which bee.
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments (see where collaborators run) → work_items:co_locate { workItem, coLocateWith } → the affined Swarm claims it under the lease.

tools.name: work_items:comment
tools.description: Comment on one OR many work-items (any kind) in one call. Single: { id, body }. Many: items:[{ id, body, harness? }]. Appends to each item's thread (created on first comment) and notifies its subscribers. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, post? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You have an update, finding, or question to post on one or more work-items. Comment on several at once via items:[…] instead of one call each.
guidance.notWhen: A contextual aside not tied to a work-item → coord:send. A structured completion → work_items:complete.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:comment; work_items:subscribe to follow the thread.

tools.name: work_items:complete
tools.description: Finish one OR many work-items with a STRUCTURED completion record (what landed / migrations / tests / deferred-set) instead of a hand-written coord:send prose dump. The system renders + broadcasts each completion from the fields — you spend no tokens narrating. Optionally also transitions each item to a terminal `state`. Single: { id, completion }. Many: items:[{ id, completion, state?, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem, completion, reflect, stateError? } | error], counts }.

guidance.when: You finished work-item(s) / plan-item(s) / brief(s). Fill the structured completion fields (summary, whatLanded, migrations, tests, deferred) — do NOT also coord:send a prose summary; this emits it. To CLOSE the item, pass a terminal top-level `state` (feature: 'passed'|'deprecated'; issue: 'resolved'|'closed') — `completion.status` alone records the completion but does NOT change state, so the item stays claimable + reclaimable (you get a `stateWarning` when it does). Duplicate? Set `completion.duplicateOf` to the surviving id — auto-links + notifies the prior assignee (EI-8993).
guidance.notWhen: For a contextual aside (a question, a design note), use coord:send. To only change state without a completion record, use work_items:set_state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:complete { id, completion }. Auto-emits to coord:inbox (no coord:send needed). Read the returned `reflect` step (self-learning loop): file a friction marker via improvements:capture if one bit you, else nothing.

tools.name: work_items:completion_stats
tools.description: Genuine-completions metric for one harness: terminalTotal (every done/closed work-item, both families) vs genuineCompletions (terminal AND carrying both an owner and a completion_ref — the only rows the completion-integrity gate would accept without a skip) vs dedupOrUnverified (the difference — watchdog/hygiene/revert dedup flips, or pre-gate historical rows).

guidance.when: Reporting progress on a harness and the question is "how much REAL work landed", not just the raw done/closed count — a watchdog dedup sweep or hygiene close inflates the raw terminal count without any owner doing the work.
guidance.notWhen: Per-item detail — that is work_items:get. A live roster of who is doing what — that is fleet:status / fleet:assignments.

tools.name: work_items:create
tools.description: Create ONE or MANY work-items of any kind — feature | chunk | bug | change | task. Returns kind-independent WI-NNN ids. bug/change/task file a tracked issue; feature/chunk enter the harness work queue. Single: { kind, title, … }. Many: items:[{ kind, title, … }] with batch-level harness / workspace / assign_all_to_self. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, title, workItem } | { ok:false, title, error }], counts } — a mirror-duplicate or one bad item never fails the rest. Dedup with work_items:list/search first.

guidance.when: Track a unit of work an agent will do. Pick the kind by what it IS: bug (code is broken), change (a code change / fix / refactor / DX ask — the DEFAULT for most coding work-items), feature (a pipeline-sized coding work-unit that plans into chunks), chunk (a sub-unit of a feature, pass `parent`), or task (NON-CODE work only — research a library, make a decision, a manual verification / ops step). File several at once via items:[…] instead of a round-trip each.
guidance.notWhen: NEVER use `task` for anything that edits code — that is `change` (or `feature` if pipeline-sized); `task` is non-code only. A passing question with no owner → coord:ask. A validator finding inside a live pipeline run → the validator pipeline, not here.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list (dedup) → work_items:create → work_items:claim/claim_next when you start → work_items:set_state on progress; work_items:promote to give a bug/change a pipeline run.

tools.name: work_items:expand
tools.description: Expand a deferred-expansion node into child work_items in one call. The Queen/operator DISPOSES (children are created); a bee PROPOSES (recorded, the steerer ratifies). Each child carries payload.expanded_from = the parent id. Lets a plan-run start shallow and self-elaborate at the point of best context.

guidance.when: You have reached an "expand-here" node (or any node) that should now fan out into concrete child work_items — the decomposition you deferred until you had the context to make it well.
guidance.notWhen: A flat structural note / re-approach → work_items:amend. A single follow-up → just create/convert one work_item. Re-prioritizing existing nodes → no expansion.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:expand { id, children:[{title, files?, brief?}] }. A bee PROPOSES (disposition=proposed, nothing created yet); the Queen DISPOSES (children created with payload.expanded_from = parent).

tools.name: work_items:get
tools.description: Fetch one OR many work-items by id (WI-/F-/EI-…) across every kind in ONE call — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100). Pass `harness` to disambiguate a feature id that may repeat across harnesses. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem?, checkpoint?, checkpointAgeMs?, checkpointUpdatedAtMs?, error? }], counts } — correlate each result by its id, not by position; a missing id comes back as that item's { ok:false } without failing the rest. `checkpoint` is the item's in-flight state left by work_items:checkpoint (null if none was ever written) — check it before assuming state was lost on a cold resume. `checkpointAgeMs`/`checkpointUpdatedAtMs` (EI-8885) are the checkpoint's write recency — a checkpoint is a HYPOTHESIS about current state, more trustworthy the fresher it is; treat one older than your own recent activity as possibly stale and re-verify against ground truth (re-read the real file, re-run the real test) rather than trusting a prose narrative that may predate a fix landing.

guidance.when: You have one or more work-item ids and need their full state (kind, lifecycle, assignee, parent). Pass every id you need at once via `ids` instead of calling per id.
guidance.notWhen: Browsing or filtering the queue → work_items:list / work_items:search (they already return many rows).
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { ids:[…] } for detail on the ones you care about.

tools.name: work_items:hold_open
tools.description: Hold a work-item OPEN without releasing your claim: stamps you as held_open_by (+ reason), excludes it from claim_next/scheduler self-select, and makes a terminal transition (done/resolved/closed/dropped) by anyone ELSE refuse until you clear it. { id, reason } to hold; { id, clear:true } to lift. Clearing another agent's hold needs force:true (leader override). Returns { ok, id, held, heldBy, reason }.

guidance.when: You are gating an item — verifying, awaiting evidence, or keeping a recurring/leader item alive — and peers must neither close it nor self-select it while you do. Your claim stays; work continues.
guidance.notWhen: You are WALKING AWAY from the item — that is work_items:park (checkpoint + release) or release { claimHold:true } (release + hold). Blocked on a dependency → set_state{blocked}. Done → complete (a holder completing their own held item is allowed).
guidance.chaining: work_items:hold_open { id, reason } → work → complete/set_state yourself (holder passes the guard), or hold_open { id, clear:true } to hand it back to normal lifecycle.

tools.name: work_items:judge_redundancy
tools.description: Judge a high-stakes item's redundant replicas + adopt the winner (reuse gym:judge). Scores each complete replica's result on the gym rubric, picks the highest composite (deterministic tie-break), settles the item to passed, marks winner/losers. Needs ≥2 complete replicas. Returns the winner + every replica's score.

guidance.when: All (or ≥2) replicas of a high-stakes item have recorded their results and you want to pick + adopt the best one. The frozen Opus judge compares them above the per-replica validators.
guidance.notWhen: Fewer than 2 replicas have recorded (wait for them). A normal exactly-once item (it has no replicas to compare). Scoring a gym optimization run — that is gym:judge directly.
guidance.chaining: work_items:set_redundancy → claim_replica (×N) → record_replica_result (×N) → work_items:judge_redundancy (adopt winner).

tools.name: work_items:link
tools.description: Link one OR many work-items to targets (rel: blocks | relates | duplicates | fixes) — single inline { id, rel, target_id } or items:[{ id, rel, target_id | target_kind+target_ref, remove? }] (a source can fan out to many targets in one call). Blocking works across kinds. Pass remove:true to unlink. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, rel, dst? | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: You discovered one or more dependencies/relationships: a work-item blocks/relates-to/duplicates/fixes other work-items or plan items. Create several edges at once via items:[…].
guidance.chaining: work_items:get both sides → work_items:link { rel:"blocks", target_id } (or items:[…]).

tools.name: work_items:list
tools.description: List work-items across kinds (feature/chunk/bug/change/task). Default shows top-level items (chunks are hidden — pass parent or includeChildren). Filter by harness, kind, state. Returns the WorkItem array directly — each row's summary is EXCERPTED to keep the list bounded (a row carries summary_truncated + summary_full_chars when cut); use work_items:get { id } for a full body.

guidance.when: You want the current work-items in a harness (or operator-wide). Default hides chunks; pass `parent` to see a parent's chunks. Each row carries `priority` (the shared backlog order, LOWER = claimed sooner) so the Mug can read the whole backlog's order in one call before steering it with work_items:set_priority.
guidance.notWhen: EI-7589: a row's `assignee:null` does NOT by itself mean 'unclaimed' when the row carries a `plan_item`/`plan_ref` link (payload.plan_item, or the trimmed/standard `plan_ref` field) — a plan-item can be under active coverage (effectiveStatus 'wip', a live worker holding it) while the work-item row's own assignee stays null. Before self-claiming a plan-linked row, cross-check `plans:items { slug }` for that item's effectiveStatus — do not trust the bare assignee field alone, or you risk duplicating in-flight work.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:get { id } for detail; work_items:claim to take one; work_items:set_priority to re-order the backlog.

tools.name: work_items:observe
tools.description: Observe one OR many work-items WITHOUT claiming (tuple-space `rd`) — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (1–100): reports each item's availability + who holds it. Distinct from claim (`in`). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, …observation | error }], counts } — correlate by id, not position.

guidance.when: Inspect one or more work-items' claimability before deciding to claim — read without taking. Pass every id you are weighing at once.
guidance.chaining: work_items:observe → work_items:claim (if available).

tools.name: work_items:park
tools.description: Park a work-item to resume later: writes the resume CHECKPOINT, releases your claim, and broadcasts a one-line note — one verb for the checkpoint→release→announce dance. { id, checkpoint, reason, harness? }. The item stays claimable (state untouched); the checkpoint is re-injected on the next pickup (yours or a successor’s).

guidance.when: You are deliberately shelving in-flight work to pick something else up (a redirect, a higher-priority item, end of a stint) and intend it to be RESUMED — by you or anyone. The checkpoint should let a cold successor continue without re-deriving: done / left / approach / gotchas.
guidance.notWhen: The item is DONE (work_items:complete), blocked on a dependency (work_items:set_state{blocked} with the reason), or you are abandoning it as wrong/obsolete (set_state{dropped}). Park = "good work, paused on purpose".
guidance.chaining: work_items:park { id, checkpoint, reason } → later work_items:claim/pickup re-injects the checkpoint. For a do-not-self-select shelf add work_items:release { claimHold:true } semantics via a follow-up release call.

tools.name: work_items:pickup
tools.description: Pick up a specific work-item in ONE call: fetch its full detail, claim it for you, and (when `intent` is given) declare your intent / plan lane. Collapses the get→claim(→declare-intent) round-trips into one and closes the get→claim race.

guidance.when: You have decided to work a SPECIFIC work-item id — pickup fetches its detail, claims it, and optionally declares your intent in one round-trip instead of work_items:get → work_items:claim → coord:declare-intent.
guidance.notWhen: You are still deciding whether to take it (inspect first with work_items:get), or you want the oldest unassigned item regardless of which (work_items:claim_next).
guidance.chaining: work_items:list → work_items:pickup { id, intent } → work → work_items:complete.

tools.name: work_items:promote
tools.description: Promote one OR many bug/change work-items into a feature pipeline run (mints an F-FIX feature in the target harness and links it). Single: { id, harness? }. Many: items:[{ id, harness? }]. An operator-scope item needs an explicit harness. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, … | error }], counts } — correlate by id; one failure never fails the rest.

guidance.when: A filed bug/change is ready to be worked by the pipeline — for one item or several at once.
guidance.notWhen: It is a passing idea (leave it filed) or already a feature.
guidance.chaining: work_items:create { kind:"bug" } → work_items:promote { harness } → the pipeline picks up the feature.

tools.name: work_items:reclaim_config
tools.description: Read or set the stale-claim reclaim policy: reclaimGraceMs (a heartbeat-less claim is presumed orphaned + reclaimed after this; default = the 10-min liveness window), reclaimParkedGraceMs (the LONGER grace before reaping a briefly-parked/resumable holder that beat recently — the reclaim-churn fix, default 30m, clamped ≥ reclaimGraceMs) and reclaimRequeueCap (requeues before a mid-flight item is dead-lettered to blocked; default 3). Threaded into the periodic reclaim sweep. set is audited + one-call-revertible.

guidance.when: Tighten reclaim (shorter grace) to free orphaned work faster after a crash wave, or loosen it to avoid reclaiming briefly-quiet live work; raise reclaimParkedGraceMs to give loop-dropped members longer to re-arm before their claim is yanked (kills claim→release→reclaim churn); raise the requeue cap to retry flaky items more before dead-lettering.
guidance.notWhen: For the presence/liveness window itself (shared STALE_MS source) this only overrides the RECLAIM grace. For handoff TTL use coord:handoff_config; for session reaping use coord:session_reaper_config.
guidance.chaining: fleet:assignments shows orphaned claims; config:list-overrides shows the active override; config:reset-overrides reverts it.

tools.name: work_items:record_replica_result
tools.description: Record your replica's result for a high-stakes item slot you hold + mark it complete (ready to judge). `text` is the distilled output the judge scores (and the winner's is adopted). Owner-checked — no double-record.

guidance.when: You finished running your replica of a high-stakes item — record the distilled result so the judge can compare it against the other Swarms.
guidance.notWhen: A normal item — that is work_items:complete / work_items:set_state. You do not hold the slot (you must claim_replica first).
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim_replica → (run) → work_items:record_replica_result → work_items:judge_redundancy.

tools.name: work_items:redundancy_status
tools.description: Read one OR many work-items' redundancy config + replica ledger (pass `id` for one or `ids` for several, all in the shared `harness`): target N, each slot's status (claimed/complete/winner/loser), owner, lease expiry, and judge verdict. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, redundancy, completeCount, judgeable, replicas, … | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: Checking how one or more high-stakes items are progressing across their Swarms — how many replicas completed, whether judged, which replica won.
guidance.notWhen: A normal item (it has no replicas). The plain item state — that is work_items:get.
guidance.chaining: work_items:redundancy_status → (if ≥2 complete) work_items:judge_redundancy.

tools.name: work_items:release
tools.description: Release one OR many work-items (clear assignee / taken_by) so another agent can pick them up. Single: { id }. Many: { ids:[…] } or items:[{ id, harness? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem? | error, holder? }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest. Refuses to clear ANOTHER agent's live claim: a non-holder caller gets `{ ok:false, error:"not_holder", holder }` per item — `force:true` (leader/reaper override only, NOT routine members) releases it anyway. A voluntary release records a short re-claim cooldown. `claimHold:true` (both families) ALSO durably parks the item out of claim_next/scheduler:get_next self-select (WI-2797) and stamps you as holder — it stays directly claimable by id; `claimHold:false` clears the hold. To hold WITHOUT releasing your claim, use work_items:hold_open.

guidance.when: You claimed work-item(s) but are no longer working them. Release several at once via ids:[…]. Add claimHold:true when the item must NOT be opportunistically re-claimed by the next self-selecting agent (a recurring do-not-pick-up ticket) — plain release lets it re-surface immediately.
guidance.notWhen: A per-item `not_holder` means a LIVE peer currently holds it — coordinate with the `holder` (coord:send), do not blind-force. `force:true` exists for the legitimate leader/reaper override path (reclaiming a dead/stuck agent's item), not for routine members clearing a peer's in-flight claim.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:release.

tools.name: work_items:reorder
tools.description: Move one OR many work-items to a position (`rank`, 0-based, 0 = head-of-line) within their assignee's ordered work-list — peers shift down. Single: { id, rank }. Many: items:[{ id, rank, writer?, harness? }]. `writer`='cup' (default, a cup resequencing its own list) | 'mug' (Mug overlay). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, … | error }], counts }.

guidance.when: You are a cup resequencing your own work-list, or the Mug injecting/rebalancing — for one item or several at once. Claim items first; rank is per-assignee.
guidance.notWhen: You only want to START an item (work_items:claim) or change its lifecycle state (work_items:set_state). Reorder changes ORDER, not ownership or state.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → work_items:reorder → fleet:assignments { agent } to see the ordered queue. The Mug: fleet:assignments → work_items:reorder { writer:"mug", items:[…] }.

tools.name: work_items:search
tools.description: Search work-items across kinds (feature/chunk/bug/change/task): full-text over title + body/summary PLUS a semantic (embedding cosine) leg, so differently-worded matches surface too (P-008; semantic:false for lexical-only). Filter by harness or kind. Use to dedup before creating. Returns { ok, count, items } — NOTE the matches array is `items`, not `results` (unlike work_items:get/list, which use `results`); a code:run helper expecting `.results` on this tool silently sees [] (EI-5920).

guidance.when: You want to find existing work-items by free text (e.g. dedup before filing, or locate a known issue/feature).
guidance.chaining: work_items:search (dedup) → work_items:create, or → work_items:get { id } for detail.

tools.name: work_items:set_live_verified
tools.description: Mark a feature-family work-item LIVE-VERIFIED — an additive payload marker { at, by, deployedSha?, evidence? } that separates "done" (code on staging) from "confirmed live" (deployed + exercised). Does NOT change the lifecycle state. Confirm deployment first (release:deploy status / dev:pipeline_position), then record the deployedSha + evidence. clear:true retracts it (rollback). Read via work_items:get (payload.live_verified). Non-feature items return applicable:false.

guidance.when: A pipeline/operator work-item is done = code-on-staging, and you have now confirmed it DEPLOYED + exercised on the live host — record the deployedSha + what you exercised so "shipped" vs "live" is no longer ambiguous.
guidance.notWhen: Not for the lifecycle state (work_items:set_state) — this is an additive live-confirmation marker, not a state. Issue-family items return applicable:false.
guidance.chaining: release:deploy { op:"status" } / dev:pipeline_position (confirm the deployed SHA) → work_items:set_live_verified { id, deployedSha, evidence }. clear:true to retract on rollback. work_items:get shows payload.live_verified.

tools.name: work_items:set_priority
tools.description: The Queen's steer-don't-dispatch lever: set one or many work-items' BACKLOG priority — the order the decentralized claim layer pulls against (lower = claimed sooner). Single: { workItem, priority?|position? }; many via items:[…] (each: explicit priority, position:'top'|'bottom', or priority:null to clear). Returns { ok, results:[…], counts:{ ok, failed, written, proposed } }. Gate on `written` (or counts.written/proposed), NOT `ok`: a non-lease-holder proposal returns ok:true but writes nothing (issue-family items too). ⚠ EI-6835: `priority`/`position:'bottom'` set an EXPLICIT value, which under NULLS LAST ALWAYS sorts BEFORE the (usually much larger) unprioritized pool — do NOT use a 'large number' or 'bottom' to try to DEPRIORITIZE an item; that PROMOTES it instead. To deprioritize, clear it (`priority: null`) or (feature-family) flip it to `blocked`.

guidance.when: The Mug steering the SHARED backlog: promote/demote what the fleet claims next via position:'top'/'bottom' or an explicit integer; reprioritize several via items:[…]. Multi-Swarm: only the steering-lease holder commits (others get proposed:true).
guidance.notWhen: Ranking a single bee's already-claimed work-list (work_items:reorder), pinning to a Swarm (work_items:co_locate), or changing lifecycle state (work_items:set_state). GLOBAL backlog order (incl. issue-family). To DEPRIORITIZE, don't use this — see the EI-6835 warning above.
guidance.chaining: work_items:list (the backlog) → set_priority { workItem, position:'top' } → the next claim_next pulls it first.

tools.name: work_items:set_redundancy
tools.description: Mark a high-stakes work-item for BOINC redundancy: run it independently on N Swarms then judge + adopt the best (reuse gym:judge). Pass { id, redundancy: N≥2 } to opt in, or { redundancy: 1 } to clear (back to exactly-once). Opt-in, off by default — inert until PAPERCUSP_WORKITEM_REDUNDANCY=1.

guidance.when: A work-item is high-stakes enough to be worth running redundantly (the cost of a wrong result exceeds the cost of a second independent run + a judge). Set redundancy: 2 to fan it out to two Swarms; a judge picks the winner.
guidance.notWhen: Routine work — redundancy doubles the cost. Issue-family items (bugs/changes) — only feature-family pipeline items carry redundancy. Pinning which Swarm runs it — that is work_items:co_locate.
guidance.chaining: work_items:set_redundancy { id, redundancy: 2 } → work_items:claim_replica (each Swarm) → work_items:record_replica_result → work_items:judge_redundancy (adopt the winner).

tools.name: work_items:set_state
tools.description: Set lifecycle state for one OR many work-items. Feature-family uses feature statuses; issue-family stores only open|resolved|closed, so blocked/needs-human/in_progress/wip/todo/done/dropped alias to open. EI-9360: for issue-family, requesting needs-human (any dialect spelling) now AUTOMATICALLY sets payload.needsHuman (EI-7776's floor — reads as fully drained, not pending) and requesting blocked AUTOMATICALLY applies the WI-2797 self-select claim hold (reads as pending-but-gated) — either way the item is durably excluded from claim_next/scheduler:get_next self-selection (still directly claimable by id) without a separate manual call; see aliasNote. Reopening another agent's terminal completion into non-terminal is rejected unless `force:true`. Single: { id, state }. Many same state: { ids:[…], state }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, state, harness?, decision?, force? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, workItem?, aliased, requestedState, appliedState, aliasNote? | error }], counts } — check `aliased`/`appliedState`, not just `ok` (EI-7712).

guidance.when: Use after moving lifecycle. Batch a wave with { ids:[…], state } or items:[…]. Prefer work_items:complete for terminal evidence. Issue-family needs-human/blocked requests are auto-excluded from self-select on alias to open (EI-9360) — no extra call needed; blocked can be un-parked via release{claimHold:false}, needs-human clears when the diagnosis is addressed. If "already terminally completed", read terminalOwner/ref before any `force:true` reopen.
guidance.chaining: work_items:claim → … → work_items:set_state { state }.

tools.name: work_items:subscribe
tools.description: Subscribe to one OR many work-items so their updates fan out to your inbox — pass `id` for one or `ids` for several (shared `mode`: full | digest | mention). Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, error? }], counts }.

guidance.when: You want to follow one or more work-items you do not own (e.g. ones that block yours). Subscribe to several at once via `ids`.
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:subscribe.

tools.name: work_items:tag
tools.description: Tag one OR many work-items with a topic (or untag with remove:true) — routes the item to that topic's subscribers. Single: { id, topic }. Many same topic: { ids:[…], topic }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, topic, harness?, remove? }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, topic? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest.

guidance.when: You want a work-item visible to agents following an area (topics:list to see topics). Tag several at once via ids:[…]+topic or items:[…].
guidance.chaining: topics:list → work_items:tag { topic } (or { ids, topic }).

tools.name: work_items:update
tools.description: Edit one OR many work-items' title / body / severity / kind / found-during / linked feature. Notifies subscribers. Single: { id, …fields }. Many heterogeneous: items:[{ id, …fields }]. Returns { ok, results:[{ ok, id, item? | error }], counts } — correlate by id; a not-found item never fails the rest. Field-edit is issue-family only (bug/change/task); a feature-family item edits via its pipeline. A `body` edit that would drastically shrink a substantial existing body is rejected unless confirmShrink:true (EI-8497 fat-finger guard). (State → work_items:set_state; structural decisions → work_items:amend; tags → work_items:tag; comments → work_items:comment.)

guidance.when: Refine work-item(s) you or someone else filed — clarify the title/body, re-rate severity, correct a mislabeled kind (bug↔change — the kind picks the auto-implement lane, so keep it honest), or attach the feature that will fix it. Edit several at once via items:[…].
guidance.notWhen: Changing lifecycle state (work_items:set_state), recording a structural decision like split/drop (work_items:amend), adding a note (work_items:comment), or routing to a topic (work_items:tag).
guidance.chaining: work_items:get → work_items:update { id, …fields }.
